sanskrit.deva:
विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कारो भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः ।
भूतकृद्भूतभृद्भावो भूतात्मा भूतभावनः ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
viśvaṃ viṣṇur vaṣaṭkāro bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ |
bhūtakṛd bhūtabhṛd bhāvo bhūtātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ || 14 ||

padaccheda.iast: viśvam viṣṇuḥ vaṣaṭkāraḥ bhūta-bhavya-bhavat-prabhuḥ bhūta-kṛt bhūta-bhṛt bhāvaḥ bhūta-ātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: विश्वम् विष्णुः वषट्कारः भूत-भव्य-भवत्-प्रभुः भूत-कृत् भूत-भृत् भावः भूत-आत्मा भूत-भावनः

words.meaning: lord of past, future and present

translations.text: (He is) Viśva, the All (Brahman, the cause of all); Viṣṇu, the Pervader; Vaṣaṭkāra, he for whom ‘vaṣaṭ’ is called; the Lord of past, future and present; Bhūtakṛt, the Maker (and the Cutter) of beings; Bhūtabhṛt, the Bearer of beings; Bhāva, Being; Bhūtātmā, the Self of beings; Bhūtabhāvana, he who brings forth beings.

notes: Śaṅkara: viśvam: Brahman is called ‘the All’ as the cause of the universe; the very first name names the cause by a word for the effect, to show that he is fitly praised even by names of effects such as Viriñci. Or: the universe is not other than the supreme Puruṣa in truth, so Brahman is called the All (‘Puruṣa alone is all this’, Muṇḍaka 2.1.10; ‘Brahman alone is all this’); nothing apart from it truly is. Or it is viśva because it enters (viśati) (‘having created it, he entered it’, Taittirīya 2.6); or because at dissolution all beings enter into it (‘into which they go and enter’, Taittirīya 3.1): either way Brahman is viśva.

Śaṅkara, on the same: or the word names the syllable Om, since name and named are not wholly different: the All is Om, which is Brahman. He cites the Upaniṣads on Om (Kaṭha 1.2.15–16, Praśna 5.2 and 5.5, Taittirīya 1.8, Chāndogya 2.23.3, and Gauḍapāda's verses ‘Om is the lower and the higher Brahman … he who knows Om is a sage’) and the law books (Gītā 8.13, 10.25; ‘the Vedas begin with Om and rest in Om; all speech is Om, so let one practise Om’).

Śaṅkara, on the same: ‘all this is Brahman, born from it, dissolving into it, breathing in it: so let one meditate, calm’ (Chāndogya 3.14.1): when all is one's Self, attachment and the rest cannot arise. To show that praise and bowing are to be done by one free of injury and the like, he cites the verses on seeing all as oneself (Gītā 6.32; Prahlāda's words in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa, ‘this whole world is the spread of Viṣṇu; it is to be seen as oneself, without difference’; the marks of the devotee of Viṣṇu: he does not swerve from his own dharma, is the same to friend and foe, takes nothing, harms none). They are to be done with faith, not without it (Gītā 17.28); ‘Om tat sat’ (Gītā 17.23) makes even a defective act whole; and having meditated on oneself as Viṣṇu (‘only one who is Viṣṇu should praise Viṣṇu’, Mahābhārata). One should not stay where Vāsudeva is reviled, and should have the highest devotion to God and the teacher (Śvetāśvatara 6.23).

Śaṅkara, on the same: naming him destroys all sin even without faith and devotion (‘naming Vāsudeva, knowingly or unknowingly, all sin dissolves like salt in water’, and other verses); how much more the naming of the thousand names with faith. Remembering and meditating are included in naming, for ‘what one thinks with the mind, that one speaks’. The Brahman taught in answer to the six questions (verses 2–11) is what is named by ‘the All’.

Śaṅkara: viṣṇuḥ: what is that All? Viṣṇu. The Ṛgveda (‘knowing his name, proclaim it … O Viṣṇu, we seek your favour’) enjoins naming Viṣṇu for gaining right knowledge. viṣṇu: he pervades (veveṣṭi), from viṣ ‘to pervade’ with the suffix nu: free of the limits of place, time and thing (‘pervading all within and without, Nārāyaṇa stands’). Or from viś ‘to enter’ (‘because all this is entered by his power, he is called Viṣṇu’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa; ‘my splendour fills heaven and earth … by my stride I am named Viṣṇu’, Mahābhārata).

Śaṅkara: vaṣaṭkāraḥ: he for whom ‘vaṣaṭ’ is called in the sacrifice; or the sacrifice in which it is called (‘Viṣṇu is the sacrifice’); or he who pleases the gods as the mantras with vaṣaṭ; or the deity (‘Prajāpati and Vaṣaṭkāra’). bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ: lord of what was, will be and is; his lordship, beyond the divisions of time, is pure being. bhūtakṛt: as Viriñci, resting on rajas, he makes beings; as Rudra, resting on tamas, he cuts (kṛntati) them. bhūtabhṛt: resting on sattva, he bears, protects, upholds or nourishes beings. bhāvaḥ: he becomes (bhavati) in the form of the manifold, or simply is; or he is being, existence. bhūtātmā: the self of beings, the inner controller (‘he is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.7.3). bhūtabhāvanaḥ: who brings forth beings or makes them grow.

sanskrit.deva:
पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः ।
अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञोऽक्षर एव च ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pūtātmā paramātmā ca muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ |
avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetrajño 'kṣara eva ca || 15 ||

lines.iast: pūtātmā paramātmā ca muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ
lines.deva: पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः

lines.iast: avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetrajño 'kṣara eva ca
lines.deva: अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञोऽक्षर एव च

padaccheda.iast: pūta-ātmā parama-ātmā ca muktānām paramā gatiḥ avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetra-jñaḥ akṣaraḥ eva ca
padaccheda.deva: पूत-आत्मा परम-आत्मा च मुक्तानाम् परमा गतिः अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्र-ज्ञः अक्षरः एव च

translations.text: (He is) Pūtātmā, whose Self is pure; Paramātmā, the supreme Self; the highest goal of the freed; Avyaya, the Undecaying; Puruṣa; Sākṣī, the Witness; Kṣetrajña, the Knower of the field; and Akṣara, the Imperishable, (one with the knower of the field).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: names such as bhūtakṛt might suggest that he depends on the guṇas; that is now denied.

Śaṅkara: pūtātmā: he whose self is pure (‘alone and without qualities’, Śvetāśvatara 6.11); his taking on the colour of the guṇas is by his own will. paramātmā: supreme and the Self, unlike effect and cause, ever pure, conscious and free by nature. muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ: the deity to be reached by the freed, the highest, for one who has reached him does not return (‘having come to me, there is no rebirth’, Gītā 8.16). avyayaḥ: without decay, destruction or change (‘ageless, deathless, undecaying’). puruṣaḥ: he lies (śete) in the city (pura), the body (‘pervading the holy city of nine gates, the great Self is called puruṣa’, Mahābhārata); or he was (āsīt) before (purā) (‘I was here before’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.4.1); or he sits among the exalted (puruṣu), or gives many (puru) fruits, or at dissolution brings the many worlds to an end; or from filling (pūraṇa) and abiding (sadana) (Mahābhārata).

Śaṅkara: sākṣī: he sees directly, without anything between, by his own nature as knowing (Pāṇini 5.2.91). kṣetrajñaḥ: he knows the field, the body (‘know me as the knower of the field’, Gītā 13.2; Brahma Purāṇa). akṣaraḥ: he does not perish (na kṣarati), the supreme Self; or from aś ‘to pervade’. eva: the knower of the field and the imperishable are in truth not different (‘that you are’); ca: and there is a difference for practical purposes only, for common acceptance is no valid means of knowing (prasiddher apramāṇatvāt).

sanskrit.deva:
योगो योगविदां नेता प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः ।
नारसिंहवपुः श्रीमान्केशवः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yogo yogavidāṃ netā pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ |
nārasiṃhavapuḥ śrīmān keśavaḥ puruṣottamaḥ || 16 ||

padaccheda.iast: yogaḥ yoga-vidām netā pradhāna-puruṣa-īśvaraḥ nārasiṃha-vapuḥ śrīmān keśavaḥ puruṣa-uttamaḥ
padaccheda.deva: योगः योग-विदाम् नेता प्रधान-पुरुष-ईश्वरः नारसिंह-वपुः श्रीमान् केशवः पुरुष-उत्तमः

words.meaning: in the form of man and lion

translations.text: (He is) Yoga; the Leader of those who know yoga; the Lord of Pradhāna and of Puruṣa (the jīva); he whose body is of man and lion; Śrīmān, with whom Śrī dwells; Keśava; Puruṣottama.

notes: Śaṅkara: yogaḥ: ‘holding all the senses of knowledge with the mind, the sense of oneness of the knower of the field and the supreme Self is yoga’; since he is to be reached by it, he is called yoga. yogavidāṃ netā: the leader of those who know, reflect on or gain yoga, bearing their gain and safekeeping (Gītā 9.22). pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ: lord of pradhāna, the Prakṛti made of māyā, and of puruṣa, the jīva. nārasiṃhavapuḥ: whose body shows the limbs of a man and a lion. śrīmān: on whose breast Śrī always dwells.

Śaṅkara: keśavaḥ: whose hair (keśa) is beautiful, the suffix va in praise (Pāṇini 5.2.109); or ka (Brahmā), a (Viṣṇu) and īśa (Śiva), the three forms, are called keśāḥ, and stand in his control; or from slaying Keśin (‘because you have slain the wicked Keśin, you will be known by the name Keśava’, Nārada to Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). puruṣottamaḥ: the highest of puruṣas; the compound in the genitive is allowed here, since he is not singled out from a class by genus, quality or action; or it is a compound in the ablative: ‘since I am beyond the perishable and higher than the imperishable, I am known as Puruṣottama’ (Gītā 15.18).

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वः शर्वः शिवः स्थाणुर्भूतादिर्निधिरव्ययः ।
संभवो भावनो भर्ता प्रभवः प्रभुरीश्वरः ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarvaḥ śarvaḥ śivaḥ sthāṇur bhūtādir nidhir avyayaḥ |
saṃbhavo bhāvano bhartā prabhavaḥ prabhur īśvaraḥ || 17 ||

lines.iast: sarvaḥ śarvaḥ śivaḥ sthāṇur bhūtādir nidhir avyayaḥ
saṃbhavo bhāvano bhartā prabhavaḥ prabhur īśvaraḥ

padaccheda.iast: sarvaḥ śarvaḥ śivaḥ sthāṇuḥ bhūta-ādiḥ nidhiḥ avyayaḥ saṃbhavaḥ bhāvanaḥ bhartā prabhavaḥ prabhuḥ īśvaraḥ
padaccheda.deva: सर्वः शर्वः शिवः स्थाणुः भूत-आदिः निधिः अव्ययः संभवः भावनः भर्ता प्रभवः प्रभुः ईश्वरः

translations.text: (He is) Sarva, the All; Śarva, the Destroyer; Śiva, the Pure; Sthāṇu, the Steadfast; Bhūtādi, the first cause of beings; the imperishable Treasure; Saṃbhava, who comes into being (of his own will); Bhāvana, who brings forth (the fruits of action); Bhartā, the Supporter; Prabhava, the Origin; Prabhu, the Mighty; Īśvara, the Lord.

notes: Śaṅkara: sarvaḥ: ‘because he is the origin and end of all, the existent and the non-existent, and knows all at all times, he is called Sarva’ (Vyāsa, Mahābhārata). śarvaḥ: he destroys (śṛṇāti) all creatures at dissolution. śivaḥ: pure, being free of the three guṇas; since scripture teaches that they are one (‘he is Brahmā, he is Śiva’, Kaivalya 8), it is Hari who is praised by names such as Śiva. sthāṇuḥ: because he is steady. bhūtādiḥ: the first cause of beings. nidhir avyayaḥ: the treasure in which all is laid down at dissolution (Pāṇini 3.3.93), qualified as imperishable.

Śaṅkara: saṃbhavaḥ: his coming into being is right, by his own will (‘to establish dharma I come into being age after age’, Gītā 4.8; ‘by my own will I am born, free of the sorrow of the womb’). bhāvanaḥ: he brings forth the fruits of all who enjoy them (Brahmasūtra 3.2.38). bhartā: he bears the world as its ground. prabhavaḥ: from him the great elements come forth; or his birth is eminent. prabhuḥ: most able in all acts. īśvaraḥ: his lordship has no condition (‘he is the lord of all’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.22).

sanskrit.deva:
स्वयंभूः शंभुरादित्यः पुष्कराक्षो महास्वनः ।
अनादिनिधनो धाता विधाता धातुरुत्तमः ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
svayaṃbhūḥ śaṃbhur ādityaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāsvanaḥ |
anādinidhano dhātā vidhātā dhātur uttamaḥ || 18 ||

padaccheda.iast: svayaṃbhūḥ śaṃbhuḥ ādityaḥ puṣkara-akṣaḥ mahā-svanaḥ anādi-nidhanaḥ dhātā vidhātā dhātuḥ uttamaḥ
padaccheda.deva: स्वयंभूः शंभुः आदित्यः पुष्कर-अक्षः महा-स्वनः अनादि-निधनः धाता विधाता धातुः उत्तमः

translations.text: (He is) Svayaṃbhū, who is of himself; Śaṃbhu, who brings happiness (to his devotees); Āditya, (the golden Puruṣa in the sun); Puṣkarākṣa, the Lotus-eyed; Mahāsvana, whose great voice (is the Veda); without beginning or end; Dhātā, the Supporter; Vidhātā, the Ordainer (of actions and their fruits); the highest Support.

notes: Śaṅkara: svayaṃbhūḥ: he is of himself (‘he himself shone forth’, Manu 1.7); or he is above all and is by himself; or he is himself both what is above and what is below (‘encompassing, self-existent’); or, as the supreme Lord, he is independent, not dependent on another (‘the self-existent pierced the openings outward’, Kaṭha 2.1.1). śaṃbhuḥ: he brings happiness to his devotees. ādityaḥ: the golden Puruṣa within the sun's orb; or Viṣṇu among the twelve Ādityas (‘of the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu’, Gītā 10.21); or the lord of Aditi, the unbroken earth; or like the sun: as the one sun appears many in many vessels of water, so the one Self appears many in many bodies.

Śaṅkara: puṣkarākṣaḥ: whose eyes are likened to the lotus. mahāsvanaḥ: whose great, revered sound is the Veda (‘the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda … are the breath of this great being’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.4.10). anādinidhanaḥ: without birth or death. dhātā: he bears the world as Ananta and in other forms. vidhātā: the maker of actions and their fruits; or he bears in a special way even Ananta and the rest. dhātur uttamaḥ: one name, with its qualifier, ‘the highest support’; or ‘higher than Dhātṛ, Viriñci’; or two names: the conscious support, higher than all the elements, earth and the rest, since consciousness upholds the whole manifold of effect and cause; and uttama, the most exalted of the exalted.

sanskrit.deva:
अप्रमेयो हृषीकेशः पद्मनाभोऽमरप्रभुः ।
विश्वकर्मा मनुस्त्वष्टा स्थविष्ठः स्थविरो ध्रुवः ॥ १९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aprameyo hṛṣīkeśaḥ padmanābho 'maraprabhuḥ |
viśvakarmā manus tvaṣṭā sthaviṣṭhaḥ sthaviro dhruvaḥ || 19 ||

lines.iast: viśvakarmā manus tvaṣṭā sthaviṣṭhaḥ sthaviro dhruvaḥ

padaccheda.iast: aprameyaḥ hṛṣīka-īśaḥ padma-nābhaḥ amara-prabhuḥ viśva-karmā manuḥ tvaṣṭā sthaviṣṭhaḥ sthaviraḥ dhruvaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अप्रमेयः हृषीक-ईशः पद्म-नाभः अमर-प्रभुः विश्व-कर्मा मनुः त्वष्टा स्थविष्ठः स्थविरः ध्रुवः

translations.text: (He is) Aprameya, beyond the means of knowledge; Hṛṣīkeśa, the Lord of the senses; Padmanābha, from whose navel (the lotus of the world springs); the Lord of the immortals; Viśvakarmā, whose work is the universe; Manu, the Thinker; Tvaṣṭā, who makes (beings) thin (at dissolution); Sthaviṣṭha, the grossest; the ancient, the firm.

notes: Śaṅkara: aprameyaḥ: not known by perception, being without sound and the other qualities; nor by inference, having no mark that goes with it; nor by comparison, being partless and so without likeness; nor by presumption, since nothing is unexplained without it; nor by non-apprehension, being positive and the witness even of absence; nor even by scripture as a means producing something new in it. How then is it known from scripture? As the witness of the means of knowledge, light by nature, it is not their object; scripture is its means only in removing what is superimposed on it. So he is immeasurable, being the witness.

Śaṅkara: hṛṣīkeśaḥ: the lord of the senses, as the knower of the field; or the supreme Self, under whose control the senses are; or he whose hair (keśa), the rays of the sun and moon, delights (hṛṣ) the world (‘the sun and moon wake and lull the world with their rays, called hair’, Mokṣadharma). padmanābhaḥ: in whose navel is the lotus, the cause of the whole world (‘in the navel of the unborn one was set the one’). amaraprabhuḥ: lord of the immortals. viśvakarmā: whose work is the universe; or whose act is all; or for his power of wondrous making; or for his likeness to Tvaṣṭṛ.

Śaṅkara: manuḥ: from thinking (‘there is no other thinker than he’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.7.23); or the mantra, or Prajāpati. tvaṣṭā: at dissolution he makes all beings thin (tvakṣ ‘to pare’). sthaviṣṭhaḥ: most gross. sthaviraḥ: ancient (‘the bright name of this ancient one’, Ṛgveda), or a word of age. dhruvaḥ: being steady. ‘sthaviro dhruvaḥ’ is one name with its qualifier: the ancient, firm one.

sanskrit.deva:
अग्राह्यः शाश्वतः कृष्णो लोहिताक्षः प्रतर्दनः ।
प्रभूतस्त्रिककुब्धाम पवित्रं मङ्गलं परम् ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
agrāhyaḥ śāśvataḥ kṛṣṇo lohitākṣaḥ pratardanaḥ |
prabhūtas trikakubdhāma pavitraṃ maṅgalaṃ param || 20 ||

padaccheda.iast: agrāhyaḥ śāśvataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ lohita-akṣaḥ pratardanaḥ prabhūtaḥ tri-kakup-dhāma pavitram maṅgalam param
padaccheda.deva: अग्राह्यः शाश्वतः कृष्णः लोहित-अक्षः प्रतर्दनः प्रभूतः त्रि-ककुप्-धाम पवित्रम् मङ्गलम् परम्

translations.text: (He is) Agrāhya, not grasped (by the organs); Śāśvata, Everlasting; Kṛṣṇa, (being and bliss); Lohitākṣa, the Red-eyed; Pratardana, the Destroyer (at dissolution); Prabhūta, rich (in knowledge and lordship); the Abode of the three regions; the Purifier; the supreme Auspicious.

notes: Śaṅkara: agrāhyaḥ: not grasped by the organs of action (‘from which words turn back, with the mind, not reaching it’, Taittirīya 2.4). śāśvataḥ: he is at all times (‘everlasting, auspicious, unfallen’). kṛṣṇaḥ: he whose nature is being, consciousness and bliss (‘kṛṣ means being, ṇa means bliss; Viṣṇu, being both, is called Kṛṣṇa’, Vyāsa); or for his dark colour (‘because my colour is dark (kṛṣṇa), I am Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna’, Mahābhārata). lohitākṣaḥ: whose eyes are red. pratardanaḥ: he destroys beings at dissolution. prabhūtaḥ: full of the qualities of knowledge, lordship and the rest.

Śaṅkara: trikakubdhāma: the abode of the three regions, above, below and between; one name. pavitram: that by which, or he who, purifies; or a seer or deity, so named (Pāṇini 3.2.185–186). maṅgalaṃ param: ‘the Brahman that by mere remembrance drives away all that is inauspicious and spreads the auspicious is called maṅgala’ (Viṣṇu Purāṇa); or because he is auspicious; param: higher than all beings; one name with its qualifier.

sanskrit.deva:
ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः ।
हिरण्यगर्भो भूगर्भो माधवो मधुसूदनः ॥ २१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
īśānaḥ prāṇadaḥ prāṇo jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ |
hiraṇyagarbho bhūgarbho mādhavo madhusūdanaḥ || 21 ||

lines.iast: īśānaḥ prāṇadaḥ prāṇo jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ
lines.deva: ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः

padaccheda.iast: īśānaḥ prāṇa-daḥ prāṇaḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajā-patiḥ hiraṇya-garbhaḥ bhū-garbhaḥ mādhavaḥ madhu-sūdanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: ईशानः प्राण-दः प्राणः ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजा-पतिः हिरण्य-गर्भः भू-गर्भः माधवः मधु-सूदनः

translations.text: (He is) Īśāna, the Ruler (of all beings); Prāṇada, who gives (and takes) the breath; Prāṇa; Jyeṣṭha, the Eldest; Śreṣṭha, the Best; Prajāpati, the Lord of creatures; Hiraṇyagarbha; Bhūgarbha, who holds the earth within him; Mādhava, the Lord of Śrī; Madhusūdana, the Slayer of Madhu.

notes: Śaṅkara: īśānaḥ: because he controls all beings. prāṇadaḥ: he gives the prāṇas, makes them move (‘who would breathe, who would live?’, Taittirīya 2.7); or as Time he cuts them off; or purifies them; or severs them. prāṇaḥ: he breathes: the knower of the field, or the supreme Self (‘the prāṇa of prāṇa’, Kena 1.2), or the chief prāṇa. jyeṣṭhaḥ: the eldest (Pāṇini 5.3.62); śreṣṭhaḥ: most to be praised (Pāṇini 5.3.60): ‘prāṇa is the eldest and the best’ (Chāndogya 5.1.1), or the chief prāṇa; or eldest as the cause of all, best as surpassing all. prajāpatiḥ: lord of all creatures, as Īśvara. hiraṇyagarbhaḥ: Brahmā, Viriñci, within the golden egg, whose self he is (‘Hiraṇyagarbha arose in the beginning’, Ṛgveda 10.121.1). bhūgarbhaḥ: who has the earth in his womb.

Śaṅkara: mādhavaḥ: the husband (dhava) of Mā, Śrī; or he who is taught in the Madhu-vidyā; or ‘know Mādhava, Bhārata, by silence, meditation and yoga’ (Vyāsa). madhusūdanaḥ: he slew the asura Madhu (‘the great asura Madhu, born from the dirt of the ear, Puruṣottama slew, doing a service to Brahmā; for that slaying gods, dānavas, men and seers call Janārdana Madhusūdana’, Mahābhārata).

sanskrit.deva:
ईश्वरो विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः ।
अनुत्तमो दुराधर्षः कृतज्ञः कृतिरात्मवान् ॥ २२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
īśvaro vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ |
anuttamo durādharṣaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kṛtir ātmavān || 22 ||

lines.iast: īśvaro vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ
lines.deva: ईश्वरो विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः

padaccheda.iast: īśvaraḥ vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ anuttamaḥ durādharṣaḥ kṛta-jñaḥ kṛtiḥ ātmavān
padaccheda.deva: ईश्वरः विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः अनुत्तमः दुराधर्षः कृत-ज्ञः कृतिः आत्मवान्

translations.text: (He is) Īśvara, having all powers; Vikramī, the Valiant; Dhanvī, the Archer; Medhāvī, the Wise; Vikrama, who strode (over the world); Krama, the Step; Anuttama, the Unsurpassed; Durādharṣa, the Unassailable; Kṛtajña, who knows (the merit and demerit of) deeds; Kṛti, the deed (whose ground he is); Ātmavān, established in his own greatness.

notes: Śaṅkara: īśvaraḥ: as having all powers. vikramī: from valour. dhanvī: having a bow (‘among the bearers of weapons I am Rāma’, Gītā 10.31). medhāvī: medhā is the power of holding many books. vikramaḥ: he strode over the whole world; or he moves by Garuḍa, the bird (vi). kramaḥ: from striding, or as the cause of order (‘Viṣṇu in the stride’, Manu 12.121). anuttamaḥ: than whom none is higher (‘than whom nothing is higher’, Śvetāśvatara 3.9; ‘none is equal to you, how a greater?’, Gītā 11.43). durādharṣaḥ: not to be assailed by gods and the rest.

Śaṅkara: kṛtajñaḥ: he knows the deeds of beings, merit and demerit; or he gives liberation even to those who offer a leaf or a flower. kṛtiḥ: human effort, or action; since he is the Self of all and its ground, it is figuratively called his. ātmavān: established in his own greatness (‘on what does he rest? On his own greatness’, Chāndogya 7.24.1).

sanskrit.deva:
सुरेशः शरणं शर्म विश्वरेताः प्रजाभवः ।
अहः संवत्सरो व्यालः प्रत्ययः सर्वदर्शनः ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sureśaḥ śaraṇaṃ śarma viśvaretāḥ prajābhavaḥ |
ahaḥ saṃvatsaro vyālaḥ pratyayaḥ sarvadarśanaḥ || 23 ||

padaccheda.iast: sura-īśaḥ śaraṇam śarma viśva-retāḥ prajā-bhavaḥ ahaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ vyālaḥ pratyayaḥ sarva-darśanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सुर-ईशः शरणम् शर्म विश्व-रेताः प्रजा-भवः अहः संवत्सरः व्यालः प्रत्ययः सर्व-दर्शनः

translations.text: (He is) Sureśa, the Lord of the gods; Śaraṇa, the Refuge; Śarma, Bliss; Viśvaretā, the seed of the universe; Prajābhava, from whom creatures arise; Ahaḥ, the Day (being light); Saṃvatsara, the Year (as Time); Vyāla, (as) a serpent (not to be seized); Pratyaya, Cognition; Sarvadarśana, whose eyes are everywhere.

notes: Śaṅkara: sureśaḥ: lord of the suras, the gods; or lord of those who give well (su-rā). śaraṇam: as he takes away the pain of the afflicted. śarma: being of the nature of the supreme bliss. viśvaretāḥ: as the cause of the universe, its seed. prajābhavaḥ: from whom all creatures come forth. ahaḥ: being light by nature. saṃvatsaraḥ: Viṣṇu standing as Time is called the year. vyālaḥ: like a serpent (vyāla), he cannot be seized. pratyayaḥ: cognition, knowing (‘Brahman is consciousness’, Aitareya 3.1.3). sarvadarśanaḥ: all the eyes are his, since he is the Self of all (‘with eyes everywhere’, Śvetāśvatara 3.3).

sanskrit.deva:
अजः सर्वेश्वरः सिद्धः सिद्धिः सर्वादिरच्युतः ।
वृषाकपिरमेयात्मा सर्वयोगविनिःसृतः ॥ २४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ajaḥ sarveśvaraḥ siddhaḥ siddhiḥ sarvādir acyutaḥ |
vṛṣākapir ameyātmā sarvayogaviniḥsṛtaḥ || 24 ||

lines.iast: ajaḥ sarveśvaraḥ siddhaḥ siddhiḥ sarvādir acyutaḥ

padaccheda.iast: ajaḥ sarva-īśvaraḥ siddhaḥ siddhiḥ sarva-ādiḥ acyutaḥ vṛṣākapiḥ ameya-ātmā sarva-yoga-viniḥsṛtaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अजः सर्व-ईश्वरः सिद्धः सिद्धिः सर्व-आदिः अच्युतः वृषाकपिः अमेय-आत्मा सर्व-योग-विनिःसृतः

translations.text: (He is) Aja, the Unborn; Sarveśvara, the Lord of all lords; Siddha, ever accomplished; Siddhi, Fulfilment (being consciousness in all things); Sarvādi, the first cause of all; Acyuta, the Unfallen; Vṛṣākapi, (dharma and the Boar); Ameyātmā, whose Self cannot be measured; Sarvayogaviniḥsṛta, free of every bond.

notes: Śaṅkara: ajaḥ: he is not born (‘he was not born, nor will be’; ‘I was not born, am not born, will not be born; I am the knower of the field of all beings, so I am called aja’, Mahābhārata). sarveśvaraḥ: lord of all lords (‘he is the lord of all’). siddhaḥ: his nature is ever accomplished. siddhiḥ: being consciousness in all things, or being unsurpassed; the fruits of heaven and the rest perish, so they are no true fruit. sarvādiḥ: the first cause of all beings. acyutaḥ: by the strength of his own nature he has not fallen, does not and will not fall (‘everlasting, auspicious, unfallen’; ‘because I never fell before, I am Acyuta’, the Lord). Here the first hundred names are explained.

Śaṅkara: vṛṣākapiḥ: vṛṣa is dharma, which rains (varṣati) all desires; kapi is the Boar, who raised the earth from the water (ka); being both he is Vṛṣākapi (‘kapi is the Boar and best, vṛṣa is called dharma; so Prajāpati Kaśyapa called me Vṛṣākapi’, Mahābhārata). ameyātmā: his Self cannot be measured as ‘so much’. sarvayogaviniḥsṛtaḥ: he has gone out from every bond (‘this Puruṣa is unattached’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.3.15); or he is beyond the yogas taught in the various śāstras.

sanskrit.deva:
वसुर्वसुमनाः सत्यः समात्मासंमितः समः ।
अमोघः पुण्डरीकाक्षो वृषकर्मा वृषाकृतिः ॥ २५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vasur vasumanāḥ satyaḥ samātmāsaṃmitaḥ samaḥ |
amoghaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣo vṛṣakarmā vṛṣākṛtiḥ || 25 ||

padaccheda.iast: vasuḥ vasu-manāḥ satyaḥ sama-ātmā asaṃmitaḥ samaḥ amoghaḥ puṇḍarīka-akṣaḥ vṛṣa-karmā vṛṣa-ākṛtiḥ
padaccheda.deva: वसुः वसु-मनाः सत्यः सम-आत्मा असंमितः समः अमोघः पुण्डरीक-अक्षः वृष-कर्मा वृष-आकृतिः

translations.text: (He is) Vasu, (in whom all dwell); Vasumanā, of excellent mind; Satya, the True; Samātmā, even-minded; Asaṃmita, not measured (by anything); Sama, ever the same; Amogha, Unfailing; Puṇḍarīkākṣa, (who pervades the lotus of the heart); Vṛṣakarmā, whose acts are dharma; Vṛṣākṛti, who takes form for dharma.

notes: Śaṅkara: vasuḥ: all beings dwell (vasanti) in him, and he dwells in them; or Vasu as in ‘of the Vasus I am Pāvaka’ (Gītā 10.23). vasumanāḥ: vasu, wealth, here means excellence: his mind is excellent, being untroubled by attachment and aversion, the afflictions or pride. satyaḥ: the supreme Self, being of a nature that is not false (‘Brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite’, Taittirīya 2.1); or as being both the formed and the formless (Taittirīya 2.6); or sat (prāṇa), ti (food) and yam (the sun) (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 5.5.1); or as good among the good. samātmā: his mind is even, unspoiled by attachment and aversion; or the one Self, the same in all beings. asaṃmitaḥ: not measured by any of the things there are. samaḥ: the same at all times, free of all change; or he who is with Mā, Lakṣmī.

Śaṅkara: amoghaḥ: worshipped, praised or remembered, he gives the whole fruit and makes nothing vain; or his resolves come true (‘whose desires are true, whose resolves are true’, Chāndogya 8.1.5). puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ: he pervades (aśnute) the lotus of the heart and is perceived there (‘the lotus in the middle of the city’); or his eyes are shaped like the lotus. vṛṣakarmā: whose acts are dharma. vṛṣākṛtiḥ: whose form is taken for dharma (‘to establish dharma I come into being’, Gītā 4.8).
The edition's line reads samātmāsaṃmitaḥ; Śaṅkara takes it as samātmā and asaṃmitaḥ, two names.

sanskrit.deva:
रुद्रो बहुशिरा बभ्रुर्विश्वयोनिः शुचिश्रवाः ।
अमृतः शाश्वतस्थाणुर्वरारोहो महातपाः ॥ २६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
rudro bahuśirā babhrur viśvayoniḥ śuciśravāḥ |
amṛtaḥ śāśvatasthāṇur varāroho mahātapāḥ || 26 ||

padaccheda.iast: rudraḥ bahu-śirāḥ babhruḥ viśva-yoniḥ śuci-śravāḥ amṛtaḥ śāśvata-sthāṇuḥ vara-ārohaḥ mahā-tapāḥ
padaccheda.deva: रुद्रः बहु-शिराः बभ्रुः विश्व-योनिः शुचि-श्रवाः अमृतः शाश्वत-स्थाणुः वर-आरोहः महा-तपाः

translations.text: (He is) Rudra, (who makes beings weep at dissolution); Bahuśirā, many-headed; Babhru, the Bearer (of the worlds); Viśvayoni, the source of the universe; Śuciśravā, whose names are pure; Amṛta, Deathless; everlasting and steadfast; Varāroha, the excellent height (from which there is no return); Mahātapā, whose knowledge (tapas) is great.

notes: Śaṅkara: rudraḥ: at dissolution, withdrawing creatures, he makes them weep (rodayati); or he gives (rāti) rud; or drives away sorrow and its cause (‘because the Lord drives away sorrow and its cause he is called Rudra; so Śiva is the supreme cause’, Liṅga Purāṇa). bahuśirāḥ: having many heads (‘Puruṣa has a thousand heads’). babhruḥ: he bears (bibharti) the worlds. viśvayoniḥ: as the cause of the universe. śuciśravāḥ: whose names (śravas), worth hearing, are pure. amṛtaḥ: he has no death (‘ageless, deathless’). śāśvatasthāṇuḥ: everlasting and steady.

Śaṅkara: varārohaḥ: whose lap (āroha) is excellent; or in whom the ascent is excellent, since those who have ascended do not return (‘he does not return’, Chāndogya 8.15.1; ‘having reached which they do not return’, Gītā 8.21). mahātapāḥ: whose tapas, knowledge, with the things to be created as its object, is great (‘whose tapas consists of knowledge’, Muṇḍaka 1.1.9); or whose lordship or splendour is great.

sanskrit.deva:
सर्वगः सर्वविद्भानुर्विष्वक्सेनो जनार्दनः ।
वेदो वेदविदव्यङ्गो वेदाङ्गो वेदवित्कविः ॥ २७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sarvagaḥ sarvavid bhānur viṣvakseno janārdanaḥ |
vedo vedavid avyaṅgo vedāṅgo vedavit kaviḥ || 27 ||

lines.iast: vedo vedavid avyaṅgo vedāṅgo vedavit kaviḥ

padaccheda.iast: sarva-gaḥ sarva-vit bhānuḥ viṣvaksenaḥ janārdanaḥ vedaḥ veda-vit avyaṅgaḥ veda-aṅgaḥ veda-vit kaviḥ
padaccheda.deva: सर्व-गः सर्व-वित् भानुः विष्वक्सेनः जनार्दनः वेदः वेद-वित् अव्यङ्गः वेद-अङ्गः वेद-वित् कविः

translations.text: (He is) Sarvaga, everywhere; the all-knowing Light; Viṣvaksena, (before whom the hosts of demons scatter); Janārdana, (who strikes down the wicked, or to whom men pray); Veda, who makes known; Vedavit, who knows the Veda; Avyaṅga, without defect; Vedāṅga, whose limbs are the Vedas; Vedavit, who reflects on the Vedas; Kavi, the all-seeing.

notes: Śaṅkara: sarvagaḥ: he goes everywhere, pervading all as the cause. sarvavid bhānuḥ: he knows or finds all, and he shines (‘him shining, all shines after’, Muṇḍaka 2.2.11; ‘the light in the sun’, Gītā 15.12): one name, ‘the all-knowing light’. viṣvaksenaḥ: before whom the army of the daityas flees on every side (viṣvak) at the mere stir of battle. janārdanaḥ: he afflicts (ardayati) wicked men, or sends them to hell and the rest; or men pray to (ardyate) him for the human ends, prosperity and the highest good.

Śaṅkara: vedaḥ: he makes known (vedayati) (‘out of compassion for them I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge’, Gītā 10.11). vedavit: he knows the meaning of the Veda as it is (‘I am the maker of the Vedānta and the knower of the Veda’, Gītā 15.15; ‘all the Vedas … all sacrifices are Kṛṣṇa’, Mahābhārata). avyaṅgaḥ: full of knowledge and the rest, without defect; or he has no manifestation (‘this is unmanifest’, Gītā 2.25). vedāṅgaḥ: the Vedas are his limbs. vedavit: he reflects on (vindate) the Vedas. kaviḥ: he who sees beyond, the seer of all (‘there is no other seer’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.7.23; ‘the seer, the wise’, Īśa 8).

sanskrit.deva:
लोकाध्यक्षः सुराध्यक्षो धर्माध्यक्षः कृताकृतः ।
चतुरात्मा चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्दंष्ट्रश्चतुर्भुजः ॥ २८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
lokādhyakṣaḥ surādhyakṣo dharmādhyakṣaḥ kṛtākṛtaḥ |
caturātmā caturvyūhaś caturdaṃṣṭraś caturbhujaḥ || 28 ||

padaccheda.iast: loka-adhyakṣaḥ sura-adhyakṣaḥ dharma-adhyakṣaḥ kṛta-akṛtaḥ catur-ātmā catur-vyūhaḥ catur-daṃṣṭraḥ catur-bhujaḥ
padaccheda.deva: लोक-अध्यक्षः सुर-अध्यक्षः धर्म-अध्यक्षः कृत-अकृतः चतुर्-आत्मा चतुर्-व्यूहः चतुर्-दंष्ट्रः चतुर्-भुजः

translations.text: (He is) the Overseer of the worlds; the Overseer of the gods; the Overseer of dharma (and adharma); Kṛtākṛta, made (as effect) and unmade (as cause); Caturātmā, whose glories are four; Caturvyūha, of four emanations; Caturdaṃṣṭra, four-tusked; Caturbhuja, four-armed.

notes: Śaṅkara: lokādhyakṣaḥ: he oversees all the worlds as their chief witness. surādhyakṣaḥ: overseer of the gods, the guardians of the worlds and the rest. dharmādhyakṣaḥ: he sees dharma and adharma directly, to give the fruit that fits. kṛtākṛtaḥ: made as the effect, unmade as the cause. caturātmā: in creation and the rest he has four separate glories (in creation Brahmā, Dakṣa and the others, time, and all creatures; in preservation Viṣṇu, Manu and the others, time, and all beings; in dissolution Rudra, time, Antaka and the rest, and all creatures: Viṣṇu Purāṇa). caturvyūhaḥ: ‘dividing himself fourfold as Vāsudeva and the others, Janārdana brings about creation and the rest’ (Vyāsa). caturdaṃṣṭraḥ: with four tusks, as Narasiṃha; or ‘tusk’ means horn, by likeness (‘four horns’, Ṛgveda 4.58.3). caturbhujaḥ: he has four arms.

sanskrit.deva:
भ्राजिष्णुर्भोजनं भोक्ता सहिष्णुर्जगदादिजः ।
अनघो विजयो जेता विश्वयोनिः पुनर्वसुः ॥ २९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhrājiṣṇur bhojanaṃ bhoktā sahiṣṇur jagadādijaḥ |
anagho vijayo jetā viśvayoniḥ punarvasuḥ || 29 ||

padaccheda.iast: bhrājiṣṇuḥ bhojanam bhoktā sahiṣṇuḥ jagat-ādi-jaḥ anaghaḥ vijayaḥ jetā viśva-yoniḥ punar-vasuḥ
padaccheda.deva: भ्राजिष्णुः भोजनम् भोक्ता सहिष्णुः जगत्-आदि-जः अनघः विजयः जेता विश्व-योनिः पुनर्-वसुः

words.meaning: born at the beginning of the world

translations.text: (He is) Bhrājiṣṇu, pure radiance; Bhojana, the enjoyed (Prakṛti, his māyā); Bhoktā, the Enjoyer (as Puruṣa); Sahiṣṇu, who overcomes (Hiraṇyākṣa and the rest); Jagadādija, born (as Hiraṇyagarbha) at the beginning of the world; Anagha, Sinless; Vijaya, Victory; Jetā, the Conqueror; Viśvayoni, (the universe and its source); Punarvasu, who dwells in body after body.

notes: Śaṅkara: bhrājiṣṇuḥ: being of the one taste of light. bhojanam: Prakṛti, māyā, as what is to be enjoyed, is called bhojana. bhoktā: as Puruṣa he enjoys it. sahiṣṇuḥ: he overcomes Hiraṇyākṣa and the others. jagadādijaḥ: as Hiraṇyagarbha he himself is born at the beginning of the world. anaghaḥ: no sin is in him (‘free of evil’, Chāndogya 8.1.5). vijayaḥ: he wins over the world by knowledge, dispassion, lordship and his other qualities. jetā: because he surpasses all beings by nature. viśvayoniḥ: the universe is his source, or he is the universe and its source. punarvasuḥ: he dwells again and again in bodies as the knower of the field.

sanskrit.deva:
उपेन्द्रो वामनः प्रांशुरमोघः शुचिरूर्जितः ।
अतीन्द्रः संग्रहः सर्गो धृतात्मा नियमो यमः ॥ ३० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
upendro vāmanaḥ prāṃśur amoghaḥ śucir ūrjitaḥ |
atīndraḥ saṃgrahaḥ sargo dhṛtātmā niyamo yamaḥ || 30 ||

lines.iast: upendro vāmanaḥ prāṃśur amoghaḥ śucir ūrjitaḥ
atīndraḥ saṃgrahaḥ sargo dhṛtātmā niyamo yamaḥ
lines.deva: अतीन्द्रः संग्रहः सर्गो धृतात्मा नियमो यमः

padaccheda.iast: upendraḥ vāmanaḥ prāṃśuḥ amoghaḥ śuciḥ ūrjitaḥ atīndraḥ saṃgrahaḥ sargaḥ dhṛta-ātmā niyamaḥ yamaḥ
padaccheda.deva: उपेन्द्रः वामनः प्रांशुः अमोघः शुचिः ऊर्जितः अतीन्द्रः संग्रहः सर्गः धृत-आत्मा नियमः यमः

translations.text: (He is) Upendra, (Indra's younger brother, or Indra above Indra); Vāmana, the Dwarf; Prāṃśu, the Tall (striding the three worlds); Amogha, whose acts are never vain; Śuci, Pure; Ūrjita, Mighty; Atīndra, beyond Indra; Saṃgraha, who gathers all in; Sarga, Creation; Dhṛtātmā, who holds himself (one, unborn); Niyama, who sets creatures to their tasks; Yama, the inner Controller.

notes: Śaṅkara: upendraḥ: he came to Indra (upa-indra) as his younger brother; or he is an Indra above (upari) (‘as you are placed above me as Indra by the cows, the gods on earth will sing of you, Kṛṣṇa, as Upendra’, Harivaṃśa). vāmanaḥ: in the form of a dwarf he begged of Bali; or he is to be worshipped (‘all the gods worship the dwarf seated in the middle’, Kaṭha 2.2.3). prāṃśuḥ: striding over the three worlds he became tall (the Harivaṃśa: when the water fell on his hand, the dwarf was no dwarf; he showed the form made of all the gods, earth his feet, heaven his head …). amoghaḥ: none of his acts is vain. śuciḥ: he purifies those who remember, praise and worship him (‘untouched, great, pure’). ūrjitaḥ: of the utmost strength.

Śaṅkara: atīndraḥ: he stands beyond Indra by his natural knowledge, lordship and the rest. saṃgrahaḥ: because he withdraws all into himself. sargaḥ: being the creation, or its cause. dhṛtātmā: who holds his self in one form, free of birth and the rest. niyamaḥ: he sets creatures to their own tasks. yamaḥ: he controls them from within.

sanskrit.deva:
वेद्यो वैद्यः सदायोगी वीरहा माधवो मधुः ।
अतीन्द्रियो महामायो महोत्साहो महाबलः ॥ ३१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vedyo vaidyaḥ sadāyogī vīrahā mādhavo madhuḥ |
atīndriyo mahāmāyo mahotsāho mahābalaḥ || 31 ||

lines.iast: vedyo vaidyaḥ sadāyogī vīrahā mādhavo madhuḥ
lines.deva: वेद्यो वैद्यः सदायोगी वीरहा माधवो मधुः

padaccheda.iast: vedyaḥ vaidyaḥ sadā-yogī vīra-hā mādhavaḥ madhuḥ atīndriyaḥ mahā-māyaḥ mahā-utsāhaḥ mahā-balaḥ
padaccheda.deva: वेद्यः वैद्यः सदा-योगी वीर-हा माधवः मधुः अतीन्द्रियः महा-मायः महा-उत्साहः महा-बलः

translations.text: (He is) Vedya, to be known (by those who seek the highest good); Vaidya, who knows all sciences; Sadāyogī, ever manifest; Vīrahā, who slays the (demon) heroes; Mādhava, the Lord of knowledge (mā); Madhu, sweet as honey; Atīndriya, beyond the senses; Mahāmāya, the great wielder of māyā; Mahotsāha, of great energy; Mahābala, of great strength.

notes: Śaṅkara: vedyaḥ: worthy to be known by those who seek the highest good. vaidyaḥ: he knows all sciences. sadāyogī: his nature is always manifest. vīrahā: to protect dharma he slays the heroic asuras. mādhavaḥ: the lord of mā, knowledge (‘Hari's knowledge is called mā; since you are its lord, you are named Mādhava; dhava means lord’, Harivaṃśa). madhuḥ: as honey gives the highest delight, so does he. atīndriyaḥ: being without sound and the rest, not the object of the senses (‘soundless, touchless’, Kaṭha 1.3.15). mahāmāyaḥ: he works māyā even on the workers of māyā (‘my māyā is hard to cross’, Gītā 7.14). mahotsāhaḥ: ever ready for the creation, preservation and dissolution of the world. mahābalaḥ: strongest of the strong.

sanskrit.deva:
महाबुद्धिर्महावीर्यो महाशक्तिर्महाद्युतिः ।
अनिर्देश्यवपुः श्रीमानमेयात्मा महाद्रिधृक् ॥ ३२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
mahābuddhir mahāvīryo mahāśaktir mahādyutiḥ |
anirdeśyavapuḥ śrīmān ameyātmā mahādridhṛk || 32 ||

padaccheda.iast: mahā-buddhiḥ mahā-vīryaḥ mahā-śaktiḥ mahā-dyutiḥ anirdeśya-vapuḥ śrīmān ameya-ātmā mahā-adri-dhṛk
padaccheda.deva: महा-बुद्धिः महा-वीर्यः महा-शक्तिः महा-द्युतिः अनिर्देश्य-वपुः श्रीमान् अमेय-आत्मा महा-अद्रि-धृक्

translations.text: (He is) Mahābuddhi, of great understanding; Mahāvīrya, whose power (ignorance, the cause of the great world) is great; Mahāśakti, of great might; Mahādyuti, of great light (within and without); Anirdeśyavapu, whose form cannot be pointed out; Śrīmān, of full lordship; Ameyātmā, whose understanding none can measure; Mahādridhṛk, who held up the great mountain (Mandara and Govardhana).

notes: Śaṅkara: mahābuddhiḥ: wisest of the wise. mahāvīryaḥ: his power, ignorance, the cause from which the great (mahat) arises, is great. mahāśaktiḥ: of great power and ability. mahādyutiḥ: his light within and without is great (‘self-luminous’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.3.9; ‘the light of lights’, Muṇḍaka 2.2.10). anirdeśyavapuḥ: his form cannot be pointed out to another as ‘this, that’, being known only in itself. śrīmān: whose glory, lordship, is entire. ameyātmā: his understanding (ātman) cannot be measured by any being. mahādridhṛk: he held the great mountain, Mandara at the churning of the nectar and Govardhana to protect the cows.

sanskrit.deva:
महेष्वासो महीभर्ता श्रीनिवासः सतां गतिः ।
अनिरुद्धः सुरानन्दो गोविन्दो गोविदां पतिः ॥ ३३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
maheṣvāso mahībhartā śrīnivāsaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ |
aniruddhaḥ surānando govindo govidāṃ patiḥ || 33 ||

padaccheda.iast: mahā-iṣvāsaḥ mahī-bhartā śrī-nivāsaḥ satām gatiḥ aniruddhaḥ sura-ānandaḥ govindaḥ go-vidām patiḥ
padaccheda.deva: महा-इष्वासः मही-भर्ता श्री-निवासः सताम् गतिः अनिरुद्धः सुर-आनन्दः गोविन्दः गो-विदाम् पतिः

translations.text: (He is) Maheṣvāsa, the great Archer; Mahībhartā, who bore the earth (out of the one ocean); Śrīnivāsa, in whose breast Śrī dwells; the Refuge of the good; Aniruddha, never obstructed; Surānanda, the gods' delight; Govinda; the Lord of those who know speech (the Veda).

notes: Śaṅkara: maheṣvāsaḥ: whose shooting of arrows is great. mahībhartā: he bore the goddess Earth, sunk in the one ocean. śrīnivāsaḥ: on whose breast Śrī dwells, never leaving. satāṃ gatiḥ: the means of the human ends for the good, the followers of the Veda. aniruddhaḥ: not obstructed by anyone in his appearances. surānandaḥ: he gladdens the gods. govindaḥ: ‘because I found (avindam) the earth (go) lost in the cave, the gods praised me as Govinda’ (Mokṣadharma); ‘I am Indra of the gods; you have become the Indra of cows (go); men will praise you as Govinda for ever’; ‘go is speech; since you find it, the sages call you Govinda’ (Harivaṃśa). govidāṃ patiḥ: go is speech; those who find it are govidaḥ; he is their lord in a special way.

sanskrit.deva:
मरीचिर्दमनो हंसः सुपर्णो भुजगोत्तमः ।
हिरण्यनाभः सुतपाः पद्मनाभः प्रजापतिः ॥ ३४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
marīcir damano haṃsaḥ suparṇo bhujagottamaḥ |
hiraṇyanābhaḥ sutapāḥ padmanābhaḥ prajāpatiḥ || 34 ||

padaccheda.iast: marīciḥ damanaḥ haṃsaḥ suparṇaḥ bhujaga-uttamaḥ hiraṇya-nābhaḥ su-tapāḥ padma-nābhaḥ prajā-patiḥ
padaccheda.deva: मरीचिः दमनः हंसः सुपर्णः भुजग-उत्तमः हिरण्य-नाभः सु-तपाः पद्म-नाभः प्रजा-पतिः

translations.text: (He is) Marīci, the light (of the luminous); Damana, who tames (creatures who stray); Haṃsa, (who slays the fear of the round for one who thinks ‘I am he’); Suparṇa, fair-winged; the best of serpents; Hiraṇyanābha, whose navel is fair as gold; Sutapā, (as Nara and Nārāyaṇa) of good austerity; Padmanābha, (shining in the lotus of the heart); Prajāpati, the father of creatures.

notes: Śaṅkara: marīciḥ: the light even of those that shine (‘I am the light of the luminous’, Gītā 10.36). damanaḥ: as Vaivasvata and others he tames creatures that stray from their duties. haṃsaḥ: for one who thinks ‘I am he’ (ahaṃ saḥ) he slays (hanti) the fear of the round; or he goes (hanti) in all bodies (‘the swan dwelling in the bright’, Kaṭha 2.2.2). suparṇaḥ: of fair wings (‘two birds of fair wings’, Muṇḍaka 3.1.1). bhujagottamaḥ: the best of those that move on their arms (serpents). hiraṇyanābhaḥ: whose navel is fair like gold, or good and lovely. sutapāḥ: in the hermitage of Badarī, as Nara and Nārāyaṇa, he practises good austerity (‘one-pointedness of mind and senses is the highest austerity’). padmanābhaḥ: whose navel is round like a lotus; or who shines in the middle of the lotus of the heart. prajāpatiḥ: the father of creatures.

sanskrit.deva:
अमृत्युः सर्वदृक्सिंहः संधाता संधिमान्स्थिरः ।
अजो दुर्मर्षणः शास्ता विश्रुतात्मा सुरारिहा ॥ ३५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
amṛtyuḥ sarvadṛk siṃhaḥ saṃdhātā saṃdhimān sthiraḥ |
ajo durmarṣaṇaḥ śāstā viśrutātmā surārihā || 35 ||

lines.iast: amṛtyuḥ sarvadṛk siṃhaḥ saṃdhātā saṃdhimān sthiraḥ

padaccheda.iast: amṛtyuḥ sarva-dṛk siṃhaḥ saṃdhātā saṃdhimān sthiraḥ ajaḥ durmarṣaṇaḥ śāstā viśruta-ātmā sura-ari-hā
padaccheda.deva: अमृत्युः सर्व-दृक् सिंहः संधाता संधिमान् स्थिरः अजः दुर्मर्षणः शास्ता विश्रुत-आत्मा सुर-अरि-हा

translations.text: (He is) Amṛtyu, without death or its cause; Sarvadṛk, who sees (all deeds); Siṃha, (who slays); Saṃdhātā, who joins men to the fruits of their acts; Saṃdhimān, (himself the one joined, the enjoyer); Sthira, steady; Aja, (who goes and casts out); Durmarṣaṇa, not to be borne (by the demons); Śāstā, the Teacher; Viśrutātmā, whose nature (truth, knowledge) is renowned; Surārihā, slayer of the gods' foes.

notes: Śaṅkara: amṛtyuḥ: neither death, destruction, nor its cause is in him. sarvadṛk: by his natural knowing he sees all the deeds, done and undone, of beings. siṃhaḥ: he slays (hinasti); the form is correct as one of the pṛṣodara group. Here the second hundred names are explained. saṃdhātā: he joins men to the fruits of their acts. saṃdhimān: he himself is also the one so joined, the enjoyer. sthiraḥ: being ever of one form. ajaḥ: he goes (aj), or casts out. durmarṣaṇaḥ: the demons cannot bear him. śāstā: he instructs all through scripture, tradition and the rest. viśrutātmā: his self, truth, knowledge and the rest, is especially heard of. surārihā: as the slayer of the enemies of the gods.

The edition's p. 70 is not inked at the ends of its last three lines; the lost words of the glosses on saṃdhimān, aja and durmarṣaṇa are supplied from the Gita Press and Mysore editions, which agree: ‘he is also the enjoyer of the fruits: saṃdhimān’; ‘he goes (ajati), or casts out: aja’; ‘he cannot be borne by the Dānavas and the rest: durmarṣaṇa’.

sanskrit.deva:
गुरुर्गुरुतमो धाम सत्यः सत्यपराक्रमः ।
निमिषोऽनिमिषः स्रग्वी वाचस्पतिरुदारधीः ॥ ३६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
gurur gurutamo dhāma satyaḥ satyaparākramaḥ |
nimiṣo 'nimiṣaḥ sragvī vācaspatir udāradhīḥ || 36 ||

padaccheda.iast: guruḥ guru-tamaḥ dhāma satyaḥ satya-parākramaḥ nimiṣaḥ animiṣaḥ sragvī vācaḥ-patiḥ udāra-dhīḥ
padaccheda.deva: गुरुः गुरु-तमः धाम सत्यः सत्य-पराक्रमः निमिषः अनिमिषः स्रग्वी वाचः-पतिः उदार-धीः

translations.text: (He is) Guru, the Teacher (of all knowledge); Gurutama, the greatest Teacher (even of Viriñci); Dhāma, Light; Satya, Truth; Satyaparākrama, of true valour; Nimiṣa, (his eyes closed in the sleep of yoga); Animiṣa, ever awake; Sragvī, who wears (the Vaijayantī) garland; Vācaspati, lord of knowledge, of understanding that grasps all.

notes: Śaṅkara: guruḥ: as the teacher of all branches of knowledge, or as the father of all. gurutamaḥ: he hands on the knowledge of Brahman even to Viriñci and the others (‘who made Brahmā first’, Śvetāśvatara 6.18). dhāma: light (‘Nārāyaṇa, the supreme light’); or the abode of all desires (‘the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode’). satyaḥ: being dharma in the form of true speech (‘so they call truth the highest’); or the true of the true (‘the prāṇas are true; he is their truth’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.1.20). satyaparākramaḥ: whose valour is not false. nimiṣaḥ: his eyes are closed as he delights in the sleep of yoga. animiṣaḥ: ever awake by nature; or as the Fish, or as the Self.
Śaṅkara: sragvī: he always wears the garland called Vaijayantī, made of the subtle elements. vācaspatir udāradhīḥ: the lord of speech, knowledge, whose understanding grasps all things; one name.

sanskrit.deva:
अग्रणीर्ग्रामणीः श्रीमान्न्यायो नेता समीरणः ।
सहस्रमूर्धा विश्वात्मा सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् ॥ ३७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
agraṇīr grāmaṇīḥ śrīmān nyāyo netā samīraṇaḥ |
sahasramūrdhā viśvātmā sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt || 37 ||

lines.iast: agraṇīr grāmaṇīḥ śrīmān nyāyo netā samīraṇaḥ

padaccheda.iast: agraṇīḥ grāmaṇīḥ śrīmān nyāyaḥ netā samīraṇaḥ sahasra-mūrdhā viśva-ātmā sahasra-akṣaḥ sahasra-pāt
padaccheda.deva: अग्रणीः ग्रामणीः श्रीमान् न्यायः नेता समीरणः सहस्र-मूर्धा विश्व-आत्मा सहस्र-अक्षः सहस्र-पात्

translations.text: (He is) Agraṇī, who leads (seekers of liberation) to the highest state; Grāmaṇī, the leader of the host of beings; Śrīmān, of surpassing radiance; Nyāya, reason (that leads to non-difference); Netā, who drives the machine of the world; Samīraṇa, (as breath) moving beings; thousand-headed; the Self of the universe; thousand-eyed; thousand-footed.

notes: Śaṅkara: agraṇīḥ: he leads seekers of liberation to the highest state. grāmaṇīḥ: as the leader of the host (grāma) of beings. śrīmān: his radiance surpasses all. nyāyaḥ: reasoning that supports the means of knowledge and leads to non-difference. netā: he works the machine of the world. samīraṇaḥ: as breath he makes beings move. sahasramūrdhā, sahasrākṣaḥ, sahasrapāt: having a thousand heads, eyes and feet (‘Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet’, Ṛgveda 10.90.1). viśvātmā: the self of the universe.

sanskrit.deva:
आवर्तनो निवृत्तात्मा संवृतः सम्प्रमर्दनः ।
अहःसंवर्तको वह्निरनिलो धरणीधरः ॥ ३८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
āvartano nivṛttātmā saṃvṛtaḥ sampramardanaḥ |
ahaḥsaṃvartako vahnir anilo dharaṇīdharaḥ || 38 ||

padaccheda.iast: āvartanaḥ nivṛtta-ātmā saṃvṛtaḥ sampramardanaḥ ahaḥ-saṃvartakaḥ vahniḥ anilaḥ dharaṇī-dharaḥ
padaccheda.deva: आवर्तनः निवृत्त-आत्मा संवृतः सम्प्रमर्दनः अहः-संवर्तकः वह्निः अनिलः धरणी-धरः

translations.text: (He is) Āvartana, who turns the wheel of the round; Nivṛttātmā, whose nature is free of the bonds of the round; Saṃvṛta, covered (by ignorance); Sampramardana, who crushes (through Rudra and Time); Ahaḥsaṃvartaka, (the sun) who brings round the day; Vahni, who bears (the oblations); Anila, (without abode, beginning or taking); Dharaṇīdhara, who holds up the earth.

notes: Śaṅkara: āvartanaḥ: he turns the wheel of the round. nivṛttātmā: his nature is turned away from the bonds of the round. saṃvṛtaḥ: covered by the ignorance that conceals. sampramardanaḥ: he crushes well through his glories, Rudra, Time and the rest. ahaḥsaṃvartakaḥ: the sun, who rightly sets the days going. vahniḥ: from bearing (vahana). anilaḥ: having no abode (nilaya); or being without beginning; or not taking; or as breath (ana). dharaṇīdharaḥ: as Śeṣa and as the Boar he holds up the earth.

sanskrit.deva:
सुप्रसादः प्रसन्नात्मा विश्वधृग्विश्वभुग्विभुः ।
सत्कर्ता सत्कृतः साधुर्जह्नुर्नारायणो नरः ॥ ३९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
suprasādaḥ prasannātmā viśvadhṛg viśvabhug vibhuḥ |
satkartā satkṛtaḥ sādhur jahnur nārāyaṇo naraḥ || 39 ||

lines.iast: satkartā satkṛtaḥ sādhur jahnur nārāyaṇo naraḥ

padaccheda.iast: su-prasādaḥ prasanna-ātmā viśva-dhṛk viśva-bhuk vibhuḥ sat-kartā sat-kṛtaḥ sādhuḥ jahnuḥ nārāyaṇaḥ naraḥ
padaccheda.deva: सु-प्रसादः प्रसन्न-आत्मा विश्व-धृक् विश्व-भुक् विभुः सत्-कर्ता सत्-कृतः साधुः जह्नुः नारायणः नरः

translations.text: (He is) Suprasāda, whose grace (gives liberation even to Śiśupāla and other wrongdoers); Prasannātmā, whose mind is clear; Viśvadhṛk, who masters the world; Viśvabhuk, who enjoys and protects the world; Vibhu, (becoming manifold as Hiraṇyagarbha and the rest); Satkartā, who honours; Satkṛta, honoured by the honoured; Sādhu, the good; Jahnu, who takes away (beings at dissolution); Nārāyaṇa, the abode of all that comes from Nara; Nara, the Leader.

notes: Śaṅkara: suprasādaḥ: his grace is good, for he gives liberation even to those who wronged him, Śiśupāla and the others. prasannātmā: his inner organ is unclouded by rajas and tamas; or he is clear by nature, compassionate; or all his desires are attained. viśvadhṛk: he masters (dhṛṣ) the world. viśvabhuk: he enjoys the world, or protects it. vibhuḥ: he becomes manifold as Hiraṇyagarbha and the rest. satkartā: he honours, worships. satkṛtaḥ: honoured even by the honoured. sādhuḥ: as acting by right; or as he accomplishes; or he accomplishes whatever is to be accomplished. jahnuḥ: at dissolution he takes beings away; or he leaves aside the ignorant and those without devotion, and leads others to the supreme.

Śaṅkara: nārāyaṇaḥ: nara is the Self; the effects born from it, space and the rest, are nāra; he pervades them as their cause, so they are his abode (ayana) (‘whatever in the world is seen or heard, pervading all that within and without, Nārāyaṇa stands’; ‘the elements born from Nara are called nāra; they are his abode, so he is Nārāyaṇa’, Mahābhārata); or he is the abode of the nāras, the jīvas, at dissolution (Taittirīya 3.1; Brahmavaivarta); or ‘the waters are called nārāḥ, the children of Nara; since they were his first abode, he is Nārāyaṇa’ (Manu 1.10). ‘Homage to Nārāyaṇa’ is the mantra that at once removes the dread poison of the round (Narasiṃha Purāṇa). naraḥ: ‘the eternal supreme Self is called nara because he leads (nayati)’ (Vyāsa).

sanskrit.deva:
असंख्येयोऽप्रमेयात्मा विशिष्टः शिष्टकृच्छुचिः ।
सिद्धार्थः सिद्धसंकल्पः सिद्धिदः सिद्धिसाधनः ॥ ४० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
asaṃkhyeyo 'prameyātmā viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭakṛc chuciḥ |
siddhārthaḥ siddhasaṃkalpaḥ siddhidaḥ siddhisādhanaḥ || 40 ||

padaccheda.iast: asaṃkhyeyaḥ aprameya-ātmā viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭa-kṛt śuciḥ siddha-arthaḥ siddha-saṃkalpaḥ siddhi-daḥ siddhi-sādhanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: असंख्येयः अप्रमेय-आत्मा विशिष्टः शिष्ट-कृत् शुचिः सिद्ध-अर्थः सिद्ध-संकल्पः सिद्धि-दः सिद्धि-साधनः

translations.text: (He is) Asaṃkhyeya, in whom there is no number (of name and form); Aprameyātmā, whose nature is beyond measure; Viśiṣṭa, surpassing all; Śiṣṭakṛt, who gives the command (and protects the good); Śuci, stainless; Siddhārtha, whose aims are attained; Siddhasaṃkalpa, whose resolves come true; Siddhida, who gives fulfilment (as each has earned); Siddhisādhana, the means of fulfilment.

notes: Śaṅkara: asaṃkhyeyaḥ: in him there is no number, no difference of name and form. aprameyātmā: whose nature cannot be measured. viśiṣṭaḥ: because he surpasses all. śiṣṭakṛt: he makes the command; or he makes, that is, protects, the good; or, as a root of general sense may stand for a particular one, ‘do’ for ‘bring wood’. śuciḥ: stainless. siddhārthaḥ: whose desired aims are already achieved (‘whose desires are true’, Chāndogya 8.1.5). siddhasaṃkalpaḥ: whose resolves are fulfilled (‘whose resolves are true’). siddhidaḥ: he gives to doers the fruit that fits their part. siddhisādhanaḥ: as the means of accomplishment.

sanskrit.deva:
वृषाही वृषभो विष्णुर्वृषपर्वा वृषोदरः ।
वर्धनो वर्धमानश्च विविक्तः श्रुतिसागरः ॥ ४१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vṛṣāhī vṛṣabho viṣṇur vṛṣaparvā vṛṣodaraḥ |
vardhano vardhamānaś ca viviktaḥ śrutisāgaraḥ || 41 ||

padaccheda.iast: vṛṣāhī vṛṣabhaḥ viṣṇuḥ vṛṣa-parvā vṛṣa-udaraḥ vardhanaḥ vardhamānaḥ ca viviktaḥ śruti-sāgaraḥ
padaccheda.deva: वृषाही वृषभः विष्णुः वृष-पर्वा वृष-उदरः वर्धनः वर्धमानः च विविक्तः श्रुति-सागरः

translations.text: (He is) Vṛṣāhī, (to whom the twelve-day rite, dharma, belongs); Vṛṣabha, who showers desires on devotees; Viṣṇu, (the Strider); Vṛṣaparvā, whose steps (to the highest abode) are dharma; Vṛṣodara, whose womb showers forth creatures; Vardhana, who makes grow; Vardhamāna, who grows (as the manifold); and Vivikta, who stands apart; Śrutisāgara, in whom the Vedas are laid as in an ocean.

notes: Śaṅkara: vṛṣāhī: vṛṣa is dharma, merit; the day (ahan) that is dharma is the rite of twelve days and the like, vṛṣāha (with the compound-final suffix ṭac, Pāṇini 5.4.91); he has it (-in). vṛṣabhaḥ: he showers (varṣati) desires on his devotees. viṣṇuḥ: ‘Viṣṇu, from striding’ (Vyāsa). vṛṣaparvā: the steps of dharma, as stairs to the supreme abode. vṛṣodaraḥ: his belly as it were rains creatures. vardhanaḥ: he makes grow. vardhamānaḥ: he grows as the manifold. viviktaḥ: though growing so, he stands apart. śrutisāgaraḥ: the Vedas are laid in him as in the ocean.

sanskrit.deva:
सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः ।
नैकरूपो बृहद्रूपः शिपिविष्टः प्रकाशनः ॥ ४२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
subhujo durdharo vāgmī mahendro vasudo vasuḥ |
naikarūpo bṛhadrūpaḥ śipiviṣṭaḥ prakāśanaḥ || 42 ||

lines.iast: subhujo durdharo vāgmī mahendro vasudo vasuḥ
lines.deva: सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः

padaccheda.iast: su-bhujaḥ durdharaḥ vāgmī mahā-indraḥ vasu-daḥ vasuḥ naika-rūpaḥ bṛhat-rūpaḥ śipiviṣṭaḥ prakāśanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सु-भुजः दुर्धरः वाग्मी महा-इन्द्रः वसु-दः वसुः नैक-रूपः बृहत्-रूपः शिपिविष्टः प्रकाशनः

translations.text: (He is) Subhuja, whose fair arms guard the world; Durdhara, (bearing what none else can bear, and hard to hold in meditation); Vāgmī, from whom the Veda came forth; Mahendra, lord even of lords; Vasuda, giver of wealth; Vasu, (himself the wealth given); Naikarūpa, of many forms; Bṛhadrūpa, of vast form (the Boar); Śipiviṣṭa, who abides in the victims (as the sacrifice) or in the rays; Prakāśana, who lights all.

notes: Śaṅkara: subhujaḥ: his fair arms protect the world. durdharaḥ: he bears the earth and the rest, which others cannot bear, and none can bear him; or he is held in the heart only with difficulty by seekers of liberation in meditation. vāgmī: from him came the speech that is the Veda. mahendraḥ: great and Indra, lord even of the lords. vasudaḥ: giver of wealth (‘eater of food, giver of wealth’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.24). vasuḥ: he is himself the wealth given; or he covers (vas) his own nature by māyā; or he is the wind, dwelling only in the mid-region (‘Vasu dwelling in the mid-region’, Kaṭha 2.2.2). naikarūpaḥ: he has not one form (‘Indra by his māyās goes in many forms’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.5.19). bṛhadrūpaḥ: whose form, the Boar and the rest, is vast.

Śaṅkara: śipiviṣṭaḥ: śipi are the victims; he dwells in them as the sacrifice (‘Viṣṇu is the sacrifice; the victims are śipi’); or śipi are the rays, and he has entered them (a verse he cites: water is called śi; the rays that drink and guard it are śipi). prakāśanaḥ: his nature is to illumine all.

sanskrit.deva:
ओजस्तेजोद्युतिधरः प्रकाशात्मा प्रतापनः ।
ऋद्धः स्पष्टाक्षरो मन्त्रश्चन्द्रांशुर्भास्करद्युतिः ॥ ४३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ojastejodyutidharaḥ prakāśātmā pratāpanaḥ |
ṛddhaḥ spaṣṭākṣaro mantraś candrāṃśur bhāskaradyutiḥ || 43 ||

padaccheda.iast: ojaḥ-tejaḥ-dyuti-dharaḥ prakāśa-ātmā pratāpanaḥ ṛddhaḥ spaṣṭa-akṣaraḥ mantraḥ candra-aṃśuḥ bhāskara-dyutiḥ
padaccheda.deva: ओजः-तेजः-द्युति-धरः प्रकाश-आत्मा प्रतापनः ऋद्धः स्पष्ट-अक्षरः मन्त्रः चन्द्र-अंशुः भास्कर-द्युतिः

words.meaning: bearer of vigour, valour and light

translations.text: (He is) the Bearer of vigour, valour and light; Prakāśātmā, whose nature is light; Pratāpana, who heats the world (through the sun); Ṛddha, rich (in dharma, knowledge, dispassion); Spaṣṭākṣara, whose syllable (Om) is clear; Mantra, (the Ṛc, Yajus and Sāman); Candrāṃśu, (cooling) as moonbeams; Bhāskaradyuti, bright as the sun.

notes: Śaṅkara: ojastejodyutidharaḥ: ojas is the strength of life, tejas valour and like qualities, dyuti light; he bears them. Or ojas and tejas are two names (‘of the strong I am the strength … the light of the luminous’, Gītā 7.10–11), and dyutidhara, who bears the light of knowledge. prakāśātmā: whose self is light. pratāpanaḥ: through his glories, the sun and the rest, he heats the world. ṛddhaḥ: full of dharma, knowledge, dispassion and the rest. spaṣṭākṣaraḥ: whose syllable, the high-pitched Om, is clear. mantraḥ: the mantra in the form of Ṛc, Yajus and Sāman; or as known from the mantras. candrāṃśuḥ: like the moon's rays he gladdens those whose minds are burnt by the sharp sun of the round. bhāskaradyutiḥ: like the sun in splendour.

sanskrit.deva:
अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुः शशबिन्दुः सुरेश्वरः ।
औषधं जगतः सेतुः सत्यधर्मपराक्रमः ॥ ४४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bhānuḥ śaśabinduḥ sureśvaraḥ |
auṣadhaṃ jagataḥ setuḥ satyadharmaparākramaḥ || 44 ||

padaccheda.iast: amṛta-aṃśu-udbhavaḥ bhānuḥ śaśa-binduḥ sura-īśvaraḥ auṣadham jagataḥ setuḥ satya-dharma-parākramaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अमृत-अंशु-उद्भवः भानुः शश-बिन्दुः सुर-ईश्वरः औषधम् जगतः सेतुः सत्य-धर्म-पराक्रमः

translations.text: (He is) Amṛtāṃśūdbhava, from whom the moon arose (at the churning); Bhānu, who shines; Śaśabindu, (the moon, nourishing creatures); Sureśvara, the Lord of the gods; Auṣadha, the medicine (for the disease of the round); the Bridge of the world; Satyadharmaparākrama, whose dharma (knowledge and other qualities) and valour are true.

notes: Śaṅkara: amṛtāṃśūdbhavaḥ: from whom the moon, of nectar rays, arose when the ocean was churned. bhānuḥ: he shines (‘him shining, all shines after’, Muṇḍaka 2.2.11). śaśabinduḥ: the moon, marked with a hare, who nourishes creatures (‘becoming the moon, full of sap, I nourish all plants’, Gītā 15.13). sureśvaraḥ: lord of the gods, and of those who give well. auṣadham: as the medicine for the disease of the round. jagataḥ setuḥ: as the means of crossing; or a bridge, a dike, that keeps the classes and stages of life from mingling (‘he is the bridge, the dike, that these worlds may not mingle’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.22). satyadharmaparākramaḥ: whose dharma, knowledge and other qualities, and valour, are true.

sanskrit.deva:
भूतभव्यभवन्नाथः पवनः पावनोऽनलः ।
कामहा कामकृत्कान्तः कामः कामप्रदः प्रभुः ॥ ४५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhūtabhavyabhavannāthaḥ pavanaḥ pāvano 'nalaḥ |
kāmahā kāmakṛt kāntaḥ kāmaḥ kāmapradaḥ prabhuḥ || 45 ||

lines.iast: kāmahā kāmakṛt kāntaḥ kāmaḥ kāmapradaḥ prabhuḥ

padaccheda.iast: bhūta-bhavya-bhavat-nāthaḥ pavanaḥ pāvanaḥ analaḥ kāma-hā kāma-kṛt kāntaḥ kāmaḥ kāma-pradaḥ prabhuḥ
padaccheda.deva: भूत-भव्य-भवत्-नाथः पवनः पावनः अनलः काम-हा काम-कृत् कान्तः कामः काम-प्रदः प्रभुः

words.meaning: lord of past, future and present

translations.text: (He is) the Lord of the beings of past, future and present; Pavana, who purifies; Pāvana, who makes (the wind) blow; Anala, (the jīva, taking the breaths as self); Kāmahā, who destroys the desires (of seekers of liberation); Kāmakṛt, who fulfils the desires (of the good); Kānta, most beautiful; Kāma, the one desired; Kāmaprada, who gives desires abundantly; Prabhu, (eminent in being).

notes: Śaṅkara: bhūtabhavyabhavannāthaḥ: lord of the hosts of beings, past, future and present; they pray to him; or he afflicts them (upatapati), rules them, governs them. pavanaḥ: he purifies (‘of purifiers I am the wind’, Gītā 10.31). pāvanaḥ: he makes the wind move (‘from fear of him the wind blows’, Taittirīya 2.8). analaḥ: the jīva, who takes (lāti) the breaths (ana) as himself; or from the root of smell with the negative (‘without smell, without taste’, Kaṭha 1.3.15); or for whom there is no ‘enough’. kāmahā: he destroys the desires of devotees who seek liberation, and of those who do harm. kāmakṛt: he fulfils the desires of the sattvic; or as the father of Kāma, Pradyumna. kāntaḥ: most beautiful. kāmaḥ: he is desired by those who seek the human ends. kāmapradaḥ: he gives desires to devotees abundantly. prabhuḥ: from eminent being.

sanskrit.deva:
युगादिकृद्युगावर्तो नैकमायो महाशनः ।
अदृश्यो व्यक्तरूपश्च सहस्रजिदनन्तजित् ॥ ४६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yugādikṛd yugāvarto naikamāyo mahāśanaḥ |
adṛśyo vyaktarūpaś ca sahasrajid anantajit || 46 ||

padaccheda.iast: yuga-ādi-kṛt yuga-āvartaḥ naika-māyaḥ mahā-aśanaḥ adṛśyaḥ vyakta-rūpaḥ ca sahasra-jit ananta-jit
padaccheda.deva: युग-आदि-कृत् युग-आवर्तः नैक-मायः महा-अशनः अदृश्यः व्यक्त-रूपः च सहस्र-जित् अनन्त-जित्

words.meaning: maker of the beginning of the ages

translations.text: (He is) Yugādikṛt, the maker of the ages and their beginnings; Yugāvarta, who as Time turns the ages; Naikamāya, whose māyās are many; Mahāśana, the great Eater (at the end of the kalpa); Adṛśya, beyond the senses; and Vyaktarūpa, manifest (in the gross form, and to yogins); Sahasrajit, who conquers thousands (of asuras); Anantajit, who conquers everywhere by unthinkable power.

notes: Śaṅkara: yugādikṛt: as the maker of time and its divisions, the ages; or who makes the beginning of the ages. Here the third hundred names are explained. yugāvartaḥ: as Time he turns the ages, Kṛta and the rest. naikamāyaḥ: he bears not one māyā but many (the n is not dropped by ‘nalopo nañaḥ’, Pāṇini 6.3.73, since there is also a negative na without the marker ñ). mahāśanaḥ: at the end of the kalpa he swallows all; great is his eating. adṛśyaḥ: beyond the reach of all the organs of knowledge. vyaktarūpaḥ: in his gross form his form is manifest; or, being self-luminous, it is manifest to yogins. sahasrajit: he conquers thousands of asuras in battle. anantajit: by his unthinkable power he conquers all beings everywhere, in battle and in play.

sanskrit.deva:
इष्टोऽविशिष्टः शिष्टेष्टः शिखण्डी नहुषो वृषः ।
क्रोधहा क्रोधकृत्कर्ता विश्वबाहुर्महीधरः ॥ ४७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
iṣṭo 'viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ śikhaṇḍī nahuṣo vṛṣaḥ |
krodhahā krodhakṛt kartā viśvabāhur mahīdharaḥ || 47 ||

padaccheda.iast: iṣṭaḥ aviśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭa-iṣṭaḥ śikhaṇḍī nahuṣaḥ vṛṣaḥ krodha-hā krodha-kṛt kartā viśva-bāhuḥ mahī-dharaḥ
padaccheda.deva: इष्टः अविशिष्टः शिष्ट-इष्टः शिखण्डी नहुषः वृषः क्रोध-हा क्रोध-कृत् कर्ता विश्व-बाहुः मही-धरः

translations.text: (He is) Iṣṭa, beloved (as supreme bliss, or worshipped by sacrifice); Aviśiṣṭa, the same (as the inner controller of all); Śiṣṭeṣṭa, dear to the wise; Śikhaṇḍī, (as the cowherd) with the peacock feather; Nahuṣa, who binds beings by māyā; Vṛṣa, dharma; Krodhahā, who slays the anger of the good; Krodhakṛt, who rouses anger against the wicked; Kartā, the maker (of the world); Viśvabāhu, whose arms are everywhere; Mahīdhara, who holds the earth (or worship).

notes: Śaṅkara: iṣṭaḥ: dear, being supreme bliss; or worshipped by sacrifice. aviśiṣṭaḥ: being the inner controller of all, the same in all. śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ: dear to the wise; or the wise are dear to him (‘I am exceedingly dear to the man of knowledge, and he to me’, Gītā 7.17); or worshipped by the wise. śikhaṇḍī: whose ornament is a peacock feather, in the dress of a cowherd. nahuṣaḥ: he binds (nah) beings by māyā. vṛṣaḥ: dharma, as raining desires (‘the Lord is known as dharma, vṛṣa, in the worlds’, Mahābhārata). krodhahā: he slays the anger of the good. krodhakṛt: he makes anger against the wicked. kartā: the maker of the world, the work (‘he who is the maker of these persons, whose work this is’, Kauṣītaki 4.19); or krodhakṛt-kartā, the cutter of those who make anger, the daityas, as one name. viśvabāhuḥ: as the support of all, or whose arms are everywhere (‘arms on every side’). mahīdharaḥ: he holds worship (mahī), or the earth.

sanskrit.deva:
अच्युतः प्रथितः प्राणः प्राणदो वासवानुजः ।
अपां निधिरधिष्ठानमप्रमत्तः प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ ४८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
acyutaḥ prathitaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇado vāsavānujaḥ |
apāṃ nidhir adhiṣṭhānam apramattaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ || 48 ||

padaccheda.iast: acyutaḥ prathitaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇa-daḥ vāsava-anujaḥ apām nidhiḥ adhiṣṭhānam apramattaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अच्युतः प्रथितः प्राणः प्राण-दः वासव-अनुजः अपाम् निधिः अधिष्ठानम् अप्रमत्तः प्रतिष्ठितः

translations.text: (He is) Acyuta, free of the six changes; Prathita, renowned (for creating and the rest); Prāṇa, (who as the thread-self moves creatures); Prāṇada, who gives (or takes) strength; Vāsavānuja, born after Indra (of Aditi); the Treasure-house of the waters (the ocean); Adhiṣṭhāna, the ground (of beings, as Brahman); Apramatta, never heedless (in giving fruits); Pratiṣṭhita, established in his own greatness.

notes: Śaṅkara: acyutaḥ: free of the six changes of being (‘everlasting, auspicious, unfallen’). prathitaḥ: renowned for the work of creating the world and the rest. prāṇaḥ: as the thread-self (sūtrātman) he moves creatures (‘I am prāṇa’, the Ṛgvedins). prāṇadaḥ: he gives strength (prāṇa) to gods and asuras, or takes it away. vāsavānujaḥ: born of Aditi and Kaśyapa as the younger brother of Vāsava (Indra). apāṃ nidhiḥ: where the waters are stored (‘of lakes I am the ocean’, Gītā 10.24). adhiṣṭhānam: Brahman, on which beings rest as on their material cause (‘all beings rest in me’, Gītā 9.4). apramattaḥ: he is never careless in giving to those entitled the fruit their acts deserve. pratiṣṭhitaḥ: established in his own greatness (Chāndogya 7.24.1).

sanskrit.deva:
स्कन्दः स्कन्दधरो धुर्यो वरदो वायुवाहनः ।
वासुदेवो बृहद्भानुरादिदेवः पुरंदरः ॥ ४९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
skandaḥ skandadharo dhuryo varado vāyuvāhanaḥ |
vāsudevo bṛhadbhānur ādidevaḥ puraṃdaraḥ || 49 ||

padaccheda.iast: skandaḥ skanda-dharaḥ dhuryaḥ vara-daḥ vāyu-vāhanaḥ vāsudevaḥ bṛhat-bhānuḥ ādi-devaḥ puraṃdaraḥ
padaccheda.deva: स्कन्दः स्कन्द-धरः धुर्यः वर-दः वायु-वाहनः वासुदेवः बृहत्-भानुः आदि-देवः पुरंदरः

translations.text: (He is) Skanda, who flows as nectar (or dries as wind); Skandadhara, who upholds the path of dharma; Dhurya, who bears the burden (of the birth and the rest of all beings); Varada, giver of boons; Vāyuvāhana, who drives the seven winds; Vāsudeva, (who covers all and in whom all dwell, the shining one); Bṛhadbhānu, whose great rays (in sun and moon) light the world; Ādideva, the first cause and god; Puraṃdara, who destroyed the cities of the gods' foes.

notes: Śaṅkara: skandaḥ: he flows as nectar, or dries up as wind. skandadharaḥ: he upholds skanda, the path of dharma. dhuryaḥ: he bears the yoke of the birth and the rest of all beings. varadaḥ: he gives the boons desired; or as the sacrificer gives the fee (vara) (‘the cow is the vara’). vāyuvāhanaḥ: he makes the seven winds, āvaha and the rest, blow.

Śaṅkara: vāsudevaḥ: vāsu, he dwells (vasati) or makes dwell, or covers all; deva, he shines, plays, wishes to conquer, deals, goes; both together (‘I cover the whole world like the sun with its rays; I am the dwelling of all beings: so I am called Vāsudeva’; ‘from dwelling in all beings, from being Vasu, from the source of the gods, he is to be known as Vāsudeva’, Udyogaparvan; ‘because he dwells everywhere and all dwells in him, the wise call him Vāsudeva’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). bṛhadbhānuḥ: whose great rays, in the moon, the sun and the rest, light the world. ādidevaḥ: the first, the cause, and god, having shining and the other qualities. puraṃdaraḥ: he broke the cities of the foes of the gods (Pāṇini 6.3.69).

sanskrit.deva:
अशोकस्तारणस्तारः शूरः शौरिर्जनेश्वरः ।
अनुकूलः शतावर्तः पद्मी पद्मनिभेक्षणः ॥ ५० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aśokas tāraṇas tāraḥ śūraḥ śaurir janeśvaraḥ |
anukūlaḥ śatāvartaḥ padmī padmanibhekṣaṇaḥ || 50 ||

lines.iast: aśokas tāraṇas tāraḥ śūraḥ śaurir janeśvaraḥ

padaccheda.iast: aśokaḥ tāraṇaḥ tāraḥ śūraḥ śauriḥ jana-īśvaraḥ anukūlaḥ śata-āvartaḥ padmī padma-nibha-īkṣaṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अशोकः तारणः तारः शूरः शौरिः जन-ईश्वरः अनुकूलः शत-आवर्तः पद्मी पद्म-निभ-ईक्षणः

translations.text: (He is) Aśoka, untouched by sorrow and the other five waves; Tāraṇa, who carries (beings) across the ocean of the round; Tāra, who saves (from the fear of womb, birth, age and death); Śūra, the Valiant; Śauri, son of Vasudeva of Śūra's line; Janeśvara, the Lord of creatures; Anukūla, well-disposed (to all, being their Self); Śatāvarta, of a hundred appearances; Padmī, lotus in hand; Padmanibhekṣaṇa, whose eyes are like lotuses.

notes: Śaṅkara: aśokaḥ: free of the six waves, sorrow and the rest. tāraṇaḥ: he carries across the ocean of the round. tāraḥ: he carries across from fear, of the womb, birth, old age and death. śūraḥ: from valour. śauriḥ: the son of Vasudeva, a descendant of Śūra. janeśvaraḥ: lord of creatures. anukūlaḥ: being the Self of all, he is well disposed to all; none acts against himself. śatāvartaḥ: for the protection of dharma he has a hundred appearances; or he dwells in the hundred channels as prāṇa. padmī: a lotus is in his hand. padmanibhekṣaṇaḥ: his eyes are like lotuses.

sanskrit.deva:
पद्मनाभोऽरविन्दाक्षः पद्मगर्भः शरीरभृत् ।
महर्द्धिरृद्धो वृद्धात्मा महाक्षो गरुडध्वजः ॥ ५१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
padmanābho 'ravindākṣaḥ padmagarbhaḥ śarīrabhṛt |
maharddhir ṛddho vṛddhātmā mahākṣo garuḍadhvajaḥ || 51 ||

padaccheda.iast: padma-nābhaḥ aravinda-akṣaḥ padma-garbhaḥ śarīra-bhṛt mahā-ṛddhiḥ ṛddhaḥ vṛddha-ātmā mahā-akṣaḥ garuḍa-dhvajaḥ
padaccheda.deva: पद्म-नाभः अरविन्द-अक्षः पद्म-गर्भः शरीर-भृत् महा-ऋद्धिः ऋद्धः वृद्ध-आत्मा महा-अक्षः गरुड-ध्वजः

translations.text: (He is) Padmanābha, (abiding in the centre of the lotus); Aravindākṣa, lotus-eyed; Padmagarbha, (to be worshipped) within the lotus of the heart; Śarīrabhṛt, who sustains bodies (as food and breath); Maharddhi, of great glory; Ṛddha, grown great (as the manifold); Vṛddhātmā, whose Self is ancient; Mahākṣa, of great eyes; Garuḍadhvaja, whose banner bears Garuḍa.

notes: Śaṅkara: padmanābhaḥ: he abides in the navel, the pericarp, of the lotus. aravindākṣaḥ: whose eyes are like lotuses. padmagarbhaḥ: to be worshipped within the lotus called the heart. śarīrabhṛt: nourishing as food or breath, he sustains the bodies of the embodied; or by his own māyā he bears bodies. maharddhiḥ: his glory is great. ṛddhaḥ: he has grown, in the form of the manifold. vṛddhātmā: whose self is old, ancient. mahākṣaḥ: two great eyes, or many great eyes, are his. garuḍadhvajaḥ: his banner is marked with Garuḍa.

sanskrit.deva:
अतुलः शरभो भीमः समयज्ञो हविर्हरिः ।
सर्वलक्षणलक्षण्यो लक्ष्मीवान्समितिंजयः ॥ ५२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
atulaḥ śarabho bhīmaḥ samayajño havirhariḥ |
sarvalakṣaṇalakṣaṇyo lakṣmīvān samitiṃjayaḥ || 52 ||

padaccheda.iast: atulaḥ śarabhaḥ bhīmaḥ samaya-jñaḥ haviḥ-hariḥ sarva-lakṣaṇa-lakṣaṇyaḥ lakṣmīvān samitiṃjayaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अतुलः शरभः भीमः समय-ज्ञः हविः-हरिः सर्व-लक्षण-लक्षण्यः लक्ष्मीवान् समितिंजयः

translations.text: (He is) Atula, without compare; Śarabha, (shining as the inner Self in the bodies that perish); Bhīma, whom all fear; Samayajña, who knows the times (of creation, preservation and dissolution); Havirhari, who takes the share of the oblation; Sarvalakṣaṇalakṣaṇya, the one known by all the means of knowledge; Lakṣmīvān, on whose breast Lakṣmī dwells; Samitiṃjaya, victor in battle.

notes: Śaṅkara: atulaḥ: there is no measure (tulā) to compare him with (‘there is no likeness of him whose name is great glory’, Śvetāśvatara 4.19; ‘none is equal to you’, Gītā 11.43). śarabhaḥ: śara are bodies, since they perish; he shines in them as the inner Self. bhīmaḥ: all fear him (Pāṇini 3.4.74); or, to those on the right path, not terrible. samayajñaḥ: he knows the times of creation, preservation and dissolution; or the six seasons; or his worship is evenness in all beings (‘evenness is the worship of Acyuta’, Prahlāda).

Śaṅkara: havirhariḥ: he takes (harati) the share of the oblation in sacrifices (‘I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices’, Gītā 9.24); or two names: haviḥ, he who is offered with oblation (‘they bound Puruṣa, the victim’), and hariḥ, who takes away the sin of those who remember him, or the round, or who is tawny (‘I take away the sin of those who remember me and the share of oblations; and my colour is tawny: so I am called Hari’). sarvalakṣaṇalakṣaṇyaḥ: the knowledge that arises from all the means of knowledge is lakṣaṇa; he is the one fit to be so known, being alone the highest truth. lakṣmīvān: Lakṣmī dwells always on his breast. samitiṃjayaḥ: he wins in battle.

sanskrit.deva:
विक्षरो रोहितो मार्गो हेतुर्दामोदरः सहः ।
महीधरो महाभागो वेगवानमिताशनः ॥ ५३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vikṣaro rohito mārgo hetur dāmodaraḥ sahaḥ |
mahīdharo mahābhāgo vegavān amitāśanaḥ || 53 ||

lines.iast: vikṣaro rohito mārgo hetur dāmodaraḥ sahaḥ

padaccheda.iast: vikṣaraḥ rohitaḥ mārgaḥ hetuḥ dāmodaraḥ sahaḥ mahī-dharaḥ mahā-bhāgaḥ vegavān amita-aśanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: विक्षरः रोहितः मार्गः हेतुः दामोदरः सहः मही-धरः महा-भागः वेगवान् अमित-अशनः

translations.text: (He is) Vikṣara, without decay; Rohita, (taking by his will) the red form of the Fish; Mārga, the Way (sought by seekers of liberation); Hetu, the cause, material and efficient; Dāmodara, (known by a mind made lofty by restraint, or bound with a rope at the belly); Saha, who overcomes and endures; Mahīdhara, (as the mountains) bearing the earth; Mahābhāga, of great enjoyments and fortune; Vegavān, swift; Amitāśana, who at dissolution eats the universe.

notes: Śaṅkara: vikṣaraḥ: his perishing (kṣara) has gone. rohitaḥ: of his own will he takes a red form, the form of the fish. mārgaḥ: seekers of liberation seek (mārgayanti) him; or he is the way by which the supreme bliss is reached. hetuḥ: he alone is the cause, material and efficient. dāmodaraḥ: his udara, his mind, made lofty by dama and the other means, is the means by which he is reached (‘they know Dāmodara from dama’, Mahābhārata); or he was bound at the belly (udara) with a rope (dāman) by Yaśodā (Brahma Purāṇa); or ‘the dāmas are the names of the worlds; they are within his belly’ (Vyāsa). sahaḥ: he overcomes all, or endures.

Śaṅkara: mahīdharaḥ: he holds the earth in the form of the mountains (‘the forests, the mountains and the quarters are Viṣṇu’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). mahābhāgaḥ: taking a body by his own will, he enjoys great enjoyments; or his fortune in his appearances is great. vegavān: having speed (‘unmoving, one, swifter than the mind’, Īśa 4). amitāśanaḥ: at dissolution he eats the universe.

sanskrit.deva:
उद्भवः क्षोभणो देवः श्रीगर्भः परमेश्वरः ।
करणं कारणं कर्ता विकर्ता गहनो गुहः ॥ ५४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
udbhavaḥ kṣobhaṇo devaḥ śrīgarbhaḥ parameśvaraḥ |
karaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ kartā vikartā gahano guhaḥ || 54 ||

lines.iast: karaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ kartā vikartā gahano guhaḥ
lines.deva: करणं कारणं कर्ता विकर्ता गहनो गुहः

padaccheda.iast: udbhavaḥ kṣobhaṇaḥ devaḥ śrī-garbhaḥ parama-īśvaraḥ karaṇam kāraṇam kartā vikartā gahanaḥ guhaḥ
padaccheda.deva: उद्भवः क्षोभणः देवः श्री-गर्भः परम-ईश्वरः करणम् कारणम् कर्ता विकर्ता गहनः गुहः

translations.text: (He is) Udbhava, the material cause of the manifold (or gone beyond the round); Kṣobhaṇa, who stirred Prakṛti and Puruṣa at creation; Deva, the God; Śrīgarbha, within whom the glory of the world lies; Parameśvara, the supreme Lord; Karaṇa, the instrument (of creating the world); Kāraṇa, its cause, material and efficient; Kartā, the free agent; Vikartā, maker of the varied world; Gahana, whose nature cannot be fathomed; Guha, who hides his nature by his māyā.

notes: Śaṅkara: udbhavaḥ: as the material cause of the coming forth of the manifold; or he has gone up beyond the round. kṣobhaṇaḥ: at creation he entered Prakṛti and Puruṣa and stirred them (Viṣṇu Purāṇa). devaḥ: he shines, plays in creation and the rest, wishes to conquer the asuras, deals in all beings, shines as the Self, is praised, goes everywhere (‘one god’, Śvetāśvatara 6.11). śrīgarbhaḥ: his glory, the world, lies within him. parameśvaraḥ: supreme and ruling (‘the supreme Lord, abiding the same in all beings’, Gītā 13.27). karaṇam: the most effective means in creating the world. kāraṇam: the cause, material and efficient. kartā: independent. vikartā: he makes the varied world. gahanaḥ: his nature, power and acts cannot be known. guhaḥ: he hides his nature by his māyā.

sanskrit.deva:
व्यवसायो व्यवस्थानः संस्थानः स्थानदो ध्रुवः ।
परर्द्धिः परमस्पष्टस्तुष्टः पुष्टः शुभेक्षणः ॥ ५५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vyavasāyo vyavasthānaḥ saṃsthānaḥ sthānado dhruvaḥ |
pararddhiḥ paramaspaṣṭas tuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ śubhekṣaṇaḥ || 55 ||

padaccheda.iast: vyavasāyaḥ vyavasthānaḥ saṃsthānaḥ sthāna-daḥ dhruvaḥ para-ṛddhiḥ parama-spaṣṭaḥ tuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ śubha-īkṣaṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: व्यवसायः व्यवस्थानः संस्थानः स्थान-दः ध्रुवः पर-ऋद्धिः परम-स्पष्टः तुष्टः पुष्टः शुभ-ईक्षणः

translations.text: (He is) Vyavasāya, pure knowing; Vyavasthāna, in whom all is ordered (and who orders the stations and classes); Saṃsthāna, in whom beings come to rest at dissolution; Sthānada, who gives (Dhruva and others) their stations; Dhruva, imperishable; Pararddhi, of supreme glory; Paramaspaṣṭa, supreme, and evident as consciousness; Tuṣṭa, content (being bliss); Puṣṭa, full; Śubhekṣaṇa, whose glance is auspicious.

notes: Śaṅkara: vyavasāyaḥ: being pure knowing. vyavasthānaḥ: all is set in order in him; or he arranges the offices of the guardians of the worlds, the kinds of creatures born from womb, egg and sweat, the classes brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, śūdra and the mixed, and the stages of life with their duties. saṃsthānaḥ: the coming to rest of beings, dissolution, is in him; or his station is excellent. sthānadaḥ: he gives Dhruva and the others places fitting their deeds. dhruvaḥ: being imperishable. pararddhiḥ: his glory is supreme. paramaspaṣṭaḥ: parama, whose beauty (mā) is supreme, or highest of all, his being depending on nothing else; and spaṣṭa, evident as consciousness. tuṣṭaḥ: being one with supreme bliss. puṣṭaḥ: being full in himself. śubhekṣaṇaḥ: his glance is auspicious: it gives liberation to seekers of liberation, enjoyments to those who seek them, cuts all doubts, purifies sinners, cuts the knot of the heart, exhausts all action and ends ignorance (‘the knot of the heart is cut’, Muṇḍaka 2.2.9).

sanskrit.deva:
रामो विरामो विरतो मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः ।
वीरः शक्तिमतां श्रेष्ठो धर्मो धर्मविदुत्तमः ॥ ५६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
rāmo virāmo virato mārgo neyo nayo 'nayaḥ |
vīraḥ śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭho dharmo dharmavid uttamaḥ || 56 ||

lines.iast: rāmo virāmo virato mārgo neyo nayo 'nayaḥ
lines.deva: रामो विरामो विरतो मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः

lines.iast: vīraḥ śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭho dharmo dharmavid uttamaḥ

padaccheda.iast: rāmaḥ virāmaḥ virataḥ mārgaḥ neyaḥ nayaḥ anayaḥ vīraḥ śaktimatām śreṣṭhaḥ dharmaḥ dharma-vit uttamaḥ
padaccheda.deva: रामः विरामः विरतः मार्गः नेयः नयः अनयः वीरः शक्तिमताम् श्रेष्ठः धर्मः धर्म-वित् उत्तमः

translations.text: (He is) Rāma, in whom yogins delight (and the son of Daśaratha); Virāma, in whom beings come to rest; Virata, without attachment to objects; Mārga, the Way (to immortality); Neya, (the Self) to whom the jīva is led; Naya, the Leader; Anaya, who has no leader; Vīra, the Valiant; the best of the mighty; Dharma, (who upholds all beings); the highest of the knowers of dharma.
