notes: Śaṅkara: rāmaḥ: yogins delight (ramante) in him, whose nature is eternal bliss (‘the supreme Brahman, the Self of consciousness and eternal bliss in which yogins delight, is named by the word rāma’, Padma Purāṇa); or Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who by his own will took a lovely form. virāmaḥ: in him beings come to their end. virataḥ: his attachment to the enjoyment of objects has gone. mārgaḥ: knowing him, seekers of liberation become fit for immortality; he alone is the path (‘there is no other path for going’, Śvetāśvatara 3.8). neyaḥ: by the way, right knowledge, the jīva is led to be the supreme Self. nayaḥ: who leads, the leader; way, led-to and leader are three forms of him. anayaḥ: he has no leader. Here the fourth hundred names are explained.

Śaṅkara: vīraḥ: from valour. śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ: mightier even than the mighty, Viriñci and the rest. dharmaḥ: as upholding (dhāraṇa) all beings (‘this subtle dharma’, Kaṭha 1.1.21); or he is worshipped by dharmas. dharmavid uttamaḥ: śruti and smṛti are his commands, so he is the highest of all the knowers of dharma.
Many editions read virajaḥ here; the edition reads virataḥ, and Śaṅkara explains virataḥ.

sanskrit.deva:
वैकुण्ठः पुरुषः प्राणः प्राणदः प्रणवः पृथुः ।
हिरण्यगर्भः शत्रुघ्नो व्याप्तो वायुरधोक्षजः ॥ ५७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ pṛthuḥ |
hiraṇyagarbhaḥ śatrughno vyāpto vāyur adhokṣajaḥ || 57 ||

lines.iast: vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ pṛthuḥ
lines.deva: वैकुण्ठः पुरुषः प्राणः प्राणदः प्रणवः पृथुः

padaccheda.iast: vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇa-daḥ praṇavaḥ pṛthuḥ hiraṇya-garbhaḥ śatru-ghnaḥ vyāptaḥ vāyuḥ adhokṣajaḥ
padaccheda.deva: वैकुण्ठः पुरुषः प्राणः प्राण-दः प्रणवः पृथुः हिरण्य-गर्भः शत्रु-घ्नः व्याप्तः वायुः अधोक्षजः

translations.text: (He is) Vaikuṇṭha, (who at the beginning held the elements together, checking their course); Puruṣa, (prior to all, burning all sins, lying in the city of the body); Prāṇa, (who moves as the knower of the field and as breath); Prāṇada, who cuts off the breath (at dissolution); Praṇava, Om; Pṛthu, vast (as the manifold); Hiraṇyagarbha, (whose womb is the golden egg); Śatrughna, slayer of the foes of the gods; Vyāpta, pervading (as cause); Vāyu, (who makes smell); Adhokṣaja, who never wanes (or is known when the senses are turned within).

notes: Śaṅkara: vaikuṇṭhaḥ: vikuṇṭhā is the checking of movement; at the beginning of the world he joined the elements together and checked their course (‘I joined earth with water, space with wind, and wind with light: so I am Vaikuṇṭha’, Śāntiparvan). puruṣaḥ: from abiding (sadana) before (purā) all, or from destroying (sādana) all sin (‘because he was before all this and burnt all sins’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.4.1); or from lying in the city (‘this Puruṣa lies in all cities’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.5.18). prāṇaḥ: he breathes, as the knower of the field, or moves beings as breath (Viṣṇu Purāṇa). prāṇadaḥ: he cuts off the breath of beings at dissolution. praṇavaḥ: he sounds forth (praṇauti) (‘therefore one sounds Om’); or he is bowed to (‘the Vedas bow to him here, so he is called praṇava’, Sanatkumāra). pṛthuḥ: spread out as the manifold.

Śaṅkara: hiraṇyagarbhaḥ: the golden egg, the cause of Hiraṇyagarbha's birth, sprung from his seed, is his womb. śatrughnaḥ: he slays the enemies of the gods. vyāptaḥ: as the cause he pervades all effects. vāyuḥ: he makes smell (‘I am the pure smell in the earth’, Gītā 7.9). adhokṣajaḥ: ‘because he never wanes downward’ (Udyogaparvan); or because he was born between heaven (akṣa) and earth (adhaḥ) as Virāj; or ‘when the host of the senses is turned down and drawn inward, knowledge of him arises: so he is called Adhokṣaja’.

sanskrit.deva:
ऋतुः सुदर्शनः कालः परमेष्ठी परिग्रहः ।
उग्रः संवत्सरो दक्षो विश्रामो विश्वदक्षिणः ॥ ५८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ṛtuḥ sudarśanaḥ kālaḥ parameṣṭhī parigrahaḥ |
ugraḥ saṃvatsaro dakṣo viśrāmo viśvadakṣiṇaḥ || 58 ||

padaccheda.iast: ṛtuḥ su-darśanaḥ kālaḥ parameṣṭhī parigrahaḥ ugraḥ saṃvatsaraḥ dakṣaḥ viśrāmaḥ viśva-dakṣiṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: ऋतुः सु-दर्शनः कालः परमेष्ठी परिग्रहः उग्रः संवत्सरः दक्षः विश्रामः विश्व-दक्षिणः

translations.text: (He is) Ṛtu, (Time, marked by the seasons); Sudarśana, whose knowledge gives the fruit of liberation (whose eyes are lotus-long, easily seen by devotees); Kāla, Time; Parameṣṭhī, abiding in his own greatness in the space of the heart; Parigraha, (grasped on every side by those who seek refuge); Ugra, (fearsome even to the sun); Saṃvatsara, in whom beings dwell; Dakṣa, able (growing as the world); Viśrāma, who gives rest (liberation); Viśvadakṣiṇa, the most skilful in all.

notes: Śaṅkara: ṛtuḥ: as Time he is marked by the word ‘season’. sudarśanaḥ: his knowledge (darśana), whose fruit is liberation, is auspicious; or his eyes are long like lotus petals; or he is easily seen by devotees. kālaḥ: he reckons all (‘of reckoners I am Time’, Gītā 10.30). parameṣṭhī: he is wont to abide in his own supreme greatness, in the space of the heart (‘Parameṣṭhin shines’). parigrahaḥ: being everywhere, he is grasped on every side by those who seek refuge; or known on every side; or he accepts the leaf, flower and the like offered by devotees. ugraḥ: he is the cause of fear even to the sun and the rest (‘from fear of him the sun rises’, Taittirīya 2.8). saṃvatsaraḥ: beings dwell (saṃvasanti) in him. dakṣaḥ: growing in the form of the world; or doing all acts quickly. viśrāmaḥ: to those who long for rest in the ocean of the round, tossed by the six waves, hunger, thirst and the rest, and tormented by the great afflictions, ignorance and the rest, and the lesser ones, pride and the rest, he gives rest, liberation. viśvadakṣiṇaḥ: abler than all, or skilful in all acts.

sanskrit.deva:
विस्तारः स्थावरस्थाणुः प्रमाणं बीजमव्ययम् ।
अर्थोऽनर्थो महाकोशो महाभोगो महाधनः ॥ ५९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vistāraḥ sthāvarasthāṇuḥ pramāṇaṃ bījam avyayam |
artho 'nartho mahākośo mahābhogo mahādhanaḥ || 59 ||

padaccheda.iast: vistāraḥ sthāvara-sthāṇuḥ pramāṇam bījam avyayam arthaḥ anarthaḥ mahā-kośaḥ mahā-bhogaḥ mahā-dhanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: विस्तारः स्थावर-स्थाणुः प्रमाणम् बीजम् अव्ययम् अर्थः अनर्थः महा-कोशः महा-भोगः महा-धनः

translations.text: (He is) Vistāra, in whom all the worlds are spread out; Sthāvarasthāṇu, abiding, and the ground in which earth and the rest abide; Pramāṇa, (consciousness, the means of knowing); the undecaying Seed; Artha, the end sought by all (being happiness); Anartha, who has no end to seek; Mahākośa, (covered by the great sheaths, food and the rest); Mahābhoga, whose enjoyment (bliss) is great; Mahādhana, whose wealth (the means of enjoyment) is great.

notes: Śaṅkara: vistāraḥ: all the worlds are spread out in him. sthāvarasthāṇuḥ: sthāvara, abiding by nature; sthāṇu, in whom earth and the other abiding things abide; one name. pramāṇam: as consciousness. bījam avyayam: the cause that does not become otherwise; one name with its qualifier. arthaḥ: being happiness, he is sought (arthyate) by all. anarthaḥ: having all his desires, he has nothing to gain. mahākośaḥ: the great sheaths, food and the rest, cover him. mahābhogaḥ: his enjoyment, which is happiness, is great. mahādhanaḥ: his wealth, the means of enjoyment, is great.

sanskrit.deva:
अनिर्विण्णः स्थविष्ठोऽभूर्धर्मयूपो महामखः ।
नक्षत्रनेमिर्नक्षत्री क्षमः क्षामः समीहनः ॥ ६० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anirviṇṇaḥ sthaviṣṭho 'bhūr dharmayūpo mahāmakhaḥ |
nakṣatranemir nakṣatrī kṣamaḥ kṣāmaḥ samīhanaḥ || 60 ||

padaccheda.iast: anirviṇṇaḥ sthaviṣṭhaḥ abhūḥ dharma-yūpaḥ mahā-makhaḥ nakṣatra-nemiḥ nakṣatrī kṣamaḥ kṣāmaḥ samīhanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अनिर्विण्णः स्थविष्ठः अभूः धर्म-यूपः महा-मखः नक्षत्र-नेमिः नक्षत्री क्षमः क्षामः समीहनः

translations.text: (He is) Anirviṇṇa, never wearied (having all he desires); Sthaviṣṭha, the vastest (as Virāj); Abhū, unborn; Dharmayūpa, the post to which the dharmas that worship him are bound; Mahāmakha, (in whom sacrifices become great, giving liberation); Nakṣatranemi, (who turns the wheel of the stars); Nakṣatrī, (as the moon); Kṣama, able in all things (and patient); Kṣāma, (who remains when all changes have waned); Samīhana, who strives well (for creation and the rest).

notes: Śaṅkara: anirviṇṇaḥ: having all his desires, he knows no weariness. sthaviṣṭhaḥ: standing as Virāj (‘fire is his head, the moon and sun his eyes’, Muṇḍaka 2.1.4). abhūḥ: unborn; or bhūḥ, being (from bhū with kvip), or the earth. dharmayūpaḥ: as the victim to the post, the dharmas that are his worship are bound to him. mahāmakhaḥ: the sacrifices offered to him become great, giving the fruit of liberation. nakṣatranemiḥ: Dhruva, at the tail of the porpoise of stars, turns the wheel of the lights; in the heart of that porpoise Viṣṇu stands like the nave of the wheel (‘Viṣṇu is the heart’, of the porpoise, Svādhyāya-brāhmaṇa). nakṣatrī: as the moon (‘among the stars I am the moon’, Gītā 10.21). kṣamaḥ: able in all acts; or forbearing (‘like the earth in patience’, Vālmīki). kṣāmaḥ: when all changes have waned, he remains in his own nature. samīhanaḥ: he strives rightly for creation and the rest.
The text has sthaviṣṭho 'bhūḥ; Śaṅkara takes it first as abhūḥ, ‘unborn’, then as bhūḥ.

sanskrit.deva:
यज्ञ इज्यो महेज्यश्च क्रतुः सत्रं सतां गतिः ।
सर्वदर्शी विमुक्तात्मा सर्वज्ञो ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥ ६१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yajña ijyo mahejyaś ca kratuḥ satraṃ satāṃ gatiḥ |
sarvadarśī vimuktātmā sarvajño jñānam uttamam || 61 ||

lines.iast: yajña ijyo mahejyaś ca kratuḥ satraṃ satāṃ gatiḥ
lines.deva: यज्ञ इज्यो महेज्यश्च क्रतुः सत्रं सतां गतिः

padaccheda.iast: yajñaḥ ijyaḥ mahā-ijyaḥ ca kratuḥ satram satām gatiḥ sarva-darśī vimukta-ātmā sarva-jñaḥ jñānam uttamam
padaccheda.deva: यज्ञः इज्यः महा-इज्यः च क्रतुः सत्रम् सताम् गतिः सर्व-दर्शी विमुक्त-आत्मा सर्व-ज्ञः ज्ञानम् उत्तमम्

translations.text: (He is) Yajña, the Sacrifice; Ijya, to be worshipped; and Mahejya, most to be worshipped (giving liberation); Kratu, the rite (with the sacrificial post); Satra, the session (or who protects the good); the Refuge of the good; Sarvadarśī, who sees all; Vimuktātmā, free by nature; Sarvajña, the All and the knower; the highest Knowledge.

notes: Śaṅkara: yajñaḥ: being in the form of all sacrifices; or he goes forth as sacrifice to please all the gods (‘Viṣṇu is the sacrifice’). ijyaḥ: he alone is to be worshipped (‘those who worship gods and fathers with holy sacrifices worship Viṣṇu, the Self, by the self’, Harivaṃśa). mahejyaḥ: of all deities to be worshipped, he most, as the giver of liberation. kratuḥ: the sacrifice with a post. satram: the rite enjoined as a session; or he protects (trā) the good (sat). satāṃ gatiḥ: for the good who seek liberation there is no other goal. sarvadarśī: by his natural knowing he sees all the deeds of beings. vimuktātmā: whose self is free by nature, or the free Self (‘freed, he is freed’, Kaṭha 2.2.1). sarvajñaḥ: the All and the knower (‘all this is this Self’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.4.6). jñānam uttamam: one name: the highest knowledge, unborn, unbounded, the best means of all, Brahman (‘Brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite’, Taittirīya 2.1).

sanskrit.deva:
सुव्रतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुघोषः सुखदः सुहृत् ।
मनोहरो जितक्रोधो वीरबाहुर्विदारणः ॥ ६२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
suvrataḥ sumukhaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sughoṣaḥ sukhadaḥ suhṛt |
manoharo jitakrodho vīrabāhur vidāraṇaḥ || 62 ||

lines.iast: suvrataḥ sumukhaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sughoṣaḥ sukhadaḥ suhṛt
lines.deva: सुव्रतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुघोषः सुखदः सुहृत्

padaccheda.iast: su-vrataḥ su-mukhaḥ sūkṣmaḥ su-ghoṣaḥ sukha-daḥ su-hṛt manaḥ-haraḥ jita-krodhaḥ vīra-bāhuḥ vidāraṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सु-व्रतः सु-मुखः सूक्ष्मः सु-घोषः सुख-दः सु-हृत् मनः-हरः जित-क्रोधः वीर-बाहुः विदारणः

translations.text: (He is) Suvrata, of good vow (to give safety to all who come to him); Sumukha, of fair face; Sūkṣma, subtle; Sughoṣa, whose sound (the Veda) is fair; Sukhada, who gives happiness (to the good, and cuts it off for the wicked); Suhṛt, the friend (who helps seeking no return); Manohara, who captivates the mind (being bliss); Jitakrodha, who has conquered anger; Vīrabāhu, whose arms are valiant; Vidāraṇa, who rends the unrighteous.

notes: Śaṅkara: suvrataḥ: whose vow is good (‘to one who comes to me once and asks, saying “I am yours”, I give safety from all: that is my vow’, Rāma in the Rāmāyaṇa). sumukhaḥ: whose face is fair (‘with a gracious face, eyes long like lotus petals’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa); or Rāma, son of Daśaratha, of glad face when sent to the forest (the Rāmāyaṇa verses: he accepted his father's word as gladly as the consecration); or by teaching all knowledge (Śvetāśvatara 6.18). sūkṣmaḥ: being free of sound and the rest, which make space and the other elements each grosser (‘all-pervading, most subtle’, Muṇḍaka 1.1.6). sughoṣaḥ: his sound, the Veda, is fair; or deep as thunder.

Śaṅkara: sukhadaḥ: he gives happiness to the well-behaved, or cuts it off for the ill-behaved. suhṛt: he helps without looking for a return. manoharaḥ: being unsurpassed bliss, he steals the mind (‘the infinite is happiness; there is no happiness in the small’, Chāndogya 7.23.1). jitakrodhaḥ: he has conquered anger; he slays the foes of the gods to keep the bounds of the Veda, not under the sway of anger. vīrabāhuḥ: keeping the bounds of the Veda by slaying the foes of the thirty gods, his arms are valiant. vidāraṇaḥ: he rends the unrighteous.

sanskrit.deva:
स्वापनः स्ववशो व्यापी नैकात्मा नैककर्मकृत् ।
वत्सरो वत्सलो वत्सी रत्नगर्भो धनेश्वरः ॥ ६३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
svāpanaḥ svavaśo vyāpī naikātmā naikakarmakṛt |
vatsaro vatsalo vatsī ratnagarbho dhaneśvaraḥ || 63 ||

padaccheda.iast: svāpanaḥ sva-vaśaḥ vyāpī naika-ātmā naika-karma-kṛt vatsaraḥ vatsalaḥ vatsī ratna-garbhaḥ dhana-īśvaraḥ
padaccheda.deva: स्वापनः स्व-वशः व्यापी नैक-आत्मा नैक-कर्म-कृत् वत्सरः वत्सलः वत्सी रत्न-गर्भः धन-ईश्वरः

translations.text: (He is) Svāpana, who by māyā lulls beings (to forgetting their Self); Svavaśa, independent (the cause of the world); Vyāpī, pervading like space; Naikātmā, standing in many forms (as his glories); Naikakarmakṛt, who does the many works (of creation and the rest); Vatsara, in whom all dwells; Vatsala, loving to his devotees; Vatsī, who protects his calves (his creatures); Ratnagarbha, (the ocean) with jewels within; Dhaneśvara, the Lord of wealth.

notes: Śaṅkara: svāpanaḥ: by māyā he makes beings void of the knowledge of their Self. svavaśaḥ: independent, being the cause of the world's rise, stay and end. vyāpī: pervading all like space (‘like space, all-pervading and eternal’); or as the cause pervading all effects. naikātmā: he stands in many ways as his glories, the powers that appear as the causes of creation and the rest. naikakarmakṛt: he does the works of the world's rise, wealth and ruin. vatsaraḥ: all dwells (vas) in him. vatsalaḥ: loving to his devotees (Pāṇini 5.2.98). vatsī: as he protects the calves; or creatures are calves to him, the father of the world. ratnagarbhaḥ: the ocean, with jewels in its womb. dhaneśvaraḥ: lord of riches.

sanskrit.deva:
धर्मगुब्धर्मकृद्धर्मी सदसत्क्षरमक्षरम् ।
अविज्ञाता सहस्रांशुर्विधाता कृतलक्षणः ॥ ६४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dharmagub dharmakṛd dharmī sad asat kṣaram akṣaram |
avijñātā sahasrāṃśur vidhātā kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ || 64 ||

lines.iast: dharmagub dharmakṛd dharmī sad asat kṣaram akṣaram

padaccheda.iast: dharma-gup dharma-kṛt dharmī sat asat kṣaram akṣaram avijñātā sahasra-aṃśuḥ vidhātā kṛta-lakṣaṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: धर्म-गुप् धर्म-कृत् धर्मी सत् असत् क्षरम् अक्षरम् अविज्ञाता सहस्र-अंशुः विधाता कृत-लक्षणः

translations.text: (He is) Dharmagup, who guards dharma; Dharmakṛt, who does dharma (to keep its bounds); Dharmī, who upholds the dharmas; Sat, the real (the supreme Brahman); Asat, (the lower Brahman, the modification); Kṣara, the perishable (all beings); Akṣara, the imperishable (the unchanging); Avijñātā, not the knower (bound by notions of agency, as the jīva is); Sahasrāṃśu, the thousand-rayed; Vidhātā, the supporter (of Śeṣa, the elephants of the quarters and the mountains); Kṛtalakṣaṇa, (whose nature is consciousness, maker of the śāstras and of the marks of things).

notes: Śaṅkara: dharmagup: he guards dharma (Gītā 4.8). dharmakṛt: though beyond dharma and adharma, he does dharma to keep its bounds. dharmī: he upholds the dharmas. sat: the supreme Brahman, not false (‘being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning’, Chāndogya 6.2.1). asat: the lower Brahman (‘a modification is a name resting on speech’, Chāndogya 6.1.4). kṣaram: all beings; akṣaram: the unchanging (‘two puruṣas are in the world, the perishable and the imperishable; all beings are the perishable, the unchanging is called the imperishable’, Gītā 15.16).

Śaṅkara: avijñātā: the knowing that imagines agency and the like in the Self is a construction; the jīva, wrapped in its impressions, is the knower (vijñātā); Viṣṇu, unlike it, is not. sahasrāṃśuḥ: the rays in the sun and the rest are his, so he is the true thousand-rayed (‘by whose light the sun burns, kindled’; ‘the light in the sun’, Gītā 15.12). vidhātā: he supports in a special way Śeṣa, the elephants of the quarters and the mountains, which support all beings. kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ: his nature is ever-accomplished consciousness; or he made the marks, the śāstras (‘the Vedas, the śāstras, all knowledge, from Janārdana’, as will be said, verse 136); or he made the marks that set each thing apart from like and unlike; or he made the Śrīvatsa mark on his own breast.

sanskrit.deva:
गभस्तिनेमिः सत्त्वस्थः सिंहो भूतमहेश्वरः ।
आदिदेवो महादेवो देवेशो देवभृद्गुरुः ॥ ६५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
gabhastinemiḥ sattvasthaḥ siṃho bhūtamaheśvaraḥ |
ādidevo mahādevo deveśo devabhṛdguruḥ || 65 ||

padaccheda.iast: gabhasti-nemiḥ sattva-sthaḥ siṃhaḥ bhūta-mahā-īśvaraḥ ādi-devaḥ mahā-devaḥ deva-īśaḥ deva-bhṛt-guruḥ
padaccheda.deva: गभस्ति-नेमिः सत्त्व-स्थः सिंहः भूत-महा-ईश्वरः आदि-देवः महा-देवः देव-ईशः देव-भृत्-गुरुः

words.meaning: nave of the wheel of rays

translations.text: (He is) Gabhastinemi, (the sun) in the midst of the wheel of rays; Sattvastha, who presides over sattva (and dwells in all beings); Siṃha, (valiant as a lion); Bhūtamaheśvara, the great Lord of beings (great by the true); Ādideva, the first and god; Mahādeva, (great because he is exalted in the lordship of the yoga of Self-knowledge); Deveśa, chief Lord of the gods; Devabhṛdguru, who rules even Indra (or bears the gods and proclaims all knowledge).

notes: Śaṅkara: gabhastinemiḥ: he stands as the sun in the middle of the wheel of rays. sattvasthaḥ: he presides chiefly over the guṇa sattva, which illumines; or he dwells in all beings. siṃhaḥ: like a lion for his valour; or the word is shortened, as Satyabhāmā is called Bhāmā. bhūtamaheśvaraḥ: the great lord of beings; or, by bhūta, the true, he is the supreme great Lord. ādidevaḥ: all beings are taken in (ādīyante) by him: he is the beginning and the god. mahādevaḥ: having given up all things, he is exalted in the great lordship of the yoga of Self-knowledge. deveśaḥ: chief lord of the gods. devabhṛdguruḥ: devabhṛt is Śakra, who bears the gods; he rules even him; or he is the guru who bears the gods and proclaims all knowledge.

sanskrit.deva:
उत्तरो गोपतिर्गोप्ता ज्ञानगम्यः पुरातनः ।
शरीरभूतभृद्भोक्ता कपीन्द्रो भूरिदक्षिणः ॥ ६६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
uttaro gopatir goptā jñānagamyaḥ purātanaḥ |
śarīrabhūtabhṛd bhoktā kapīndro bhūridakṣiṇaḥ || 66 ||

padaccheda.iast: uttaraḥ go-patiḥ goptā jñāna-gamyaḥ purātanaḥ śarīra-bhūta-bhṛt bhoktā kapi-indraḥ bhūri-dakṣiṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: उत्तरः गो-पतिः गोप्ता ज्ञान-गम्यः पुरातनः शरीर-भूत-भृत् भोक्ता कपि-इन्द्रः भूरि-दक्षिणः

words.meaning: sustainer of the elements of the body

translations.text: (He is) Uttara, who rises above the bondage of birth (or the highest); Gopati, (the cowherd, or the lord of the earth); Goptā, the protector of the world; Jñānagamya, reached by knowledge (not by action); Purātana, the Ancient; Śarīrabhūtabhṛt, (as prāṇa) sustaining the elements that make the body; Bhoktā, the protector (or enjoyer of supreme bliss); Kapīndra, (the Boar, or Rāma, lord of the monkeys); Bhūridakṣiṇa, whose sacrifices have abundant gifts.

notes: Śaṅkara: uttaraḥ: he rises above (uttarati) the bondage of birth and the round; or he is highest (‘Indra is higher than all’, Ṛgveda 10.86.1). gopatiḥ: as the cowherd who tends the cows; or the lord of the earth (go). goptā: protecting all beings, the guardian of the world. jñānagamyaḥ: reached neither by action nor by knowledge and action together, but by knowledge. purātanaḥ: unbounded by time, he was even before. śarīrabhūtabhṛt: as prāṇa he sustains the elements that make up the body. bhoktā: as protector; or as enjoying the fullness of supreme bliss. Here the fifth hundred names are explained. kapīndraḥ: kapi, the Boar, and Indra: he who took the form of the Boar; or Rāghava, lord of the monkeys. bhūridakṣiṇaḥ: showing the bounds of dharma, he performs sacrifices with many gifts.

sanskrit.deva:
सोमपोऽमृतपः सोमः पुरुजित्पुरुसत्तमः ।
विनयो जयः सत्यसंधो दाशार्हः सात्वतां पतिः ॥ ६७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
somapo 'mṛtapaḥ somaḥ purujit purusattamaḥ |
vinayo jayaḥ satyasaṃdho dāśārhaḥ sātvatāṃ patiḥ || 67 ||

lines.iast: vinayo jayaḥ satyasaṃdho dāśārhaḥ sātvatāṃ patiḥ
lines.deva: विनयो जयः सत्यसंधो दाशार्हः सात्वतां पतिः

padaccheda.iast: soma-paḥ amṛta-paḥ somaḥ puru-jit puru-sattamaḥ vinayaḥ jayaḥ satya-saṃdhaḥ dāśārhaḥ sātvatām patiḥ
padaccheda.deva: सोम-पः अमृत-पः सोमः पुरु-जित् पुरु-सत्तमः विनयः जयः सत्य-संधः दाशार्हः सात्वताम् पतिः

translations.text: (He is) Somapa, who drinks the soma (as the deity of all sacrifices); Amṛtapa, who drinks the nectar of the Self; Soma, (the moon nourishing the plants, or Śiva with Umā); Purujit, who conquers many; Purusattama, manifold (as the universe) and best; Vinaya, who chastises the wicked; Jaya, who conquers all; Satyasaṃdha, whose resolve is true; Dāśārha, worthy of gifts (or born of Daśārha's line); the Lord of the Sātvatas.

notes: Śaṅkara: somapaḥ: he drinks the soma in all sacrifices as the deity to be worshipped; or, as the sacrificer, showing the bounds of dharma. amṛtapaḥ: he drinks the nectar of the Self; or, saving the nectar the asuras were carrying off, he made the gods drink it and drank it himself. somaḥ: as the moon he nourishes the plants; or Śiva with Umā (sa-umā). purujit: he conquers many. purusattamaḥ: puru, being the universe; sattama, being the best; one name. vinayaḥ: he chastises the wicked. jayaḥ: he conquers all beings. satyasaṃdhaḥ: whose resolve is true (‘whose resolves are true’, Chāndogya 8.1.5). dāśārhaḥ: dāśa is a gift; he deserves it; or he was born in the line of Daśārha. sātvatāṃ patiḥ: Sātvata is the name of a tantra; those who make or teach it are Sātvats; he is their lord, who bears their gain and safekeeping.

sanskrit.deva:
जीवो विनयितासाक्षी मुकुन्दोऽमितविक्रमः ।
अम्भोनिधिरनन्तात्मा महोदधिशयोऽन्तकः ॥ ६८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
jīvo vinayitāsākṣī mukundo 'mitavikramaḥ |
ambhonidhir anantātmā mahodadhiśayo 'ntakaḥ || 68 ||

padaccheda.iast: jīvaḥ vinayitṛ-sākṣī mukundaḥ amita-vikramaḥ ambhaḥ-nidhiḥ ananta-ātmā mahā-udadhi-śayaḥ antakaḥ
padaccheda.deva: जीवः विनयितृ-साक्षी मुकुन्दः अमित-विक्रमः अम्भः-निधिः अनन्त-आत्मा महा-उदधि-शयः अन्तकः

translations.text: (He is) Jīva, (holding the breaths as the knower of the field); Vinayitāsākṣī, who sees directly the discipline of creatures; Mukunda, giver of liberation; Amitavikrama, whose three strides (and valour) are boundless; Ambhonidhi, (in whom the four ‘waters’, gods, men, fathers and asuras, are laid; or the ocean); Anantātmā, unbounded by place, time and thing; Mahodadhiśaya, who lies on the great ocean (into which he has gathered all beings); Antaka, who makes an end of beings.

notes: Śaṅkara: jīvaḥ: as the knower of the field he holds the breaths. vinayitāsākṣī: he sees directly the discipline (vinayitva) of creatures; or two words: vinayitā, from nī ‘to go’, and asākṣī, he does not see anything apart from the Self as directly present. mukundaḥ: he gives liberation (mukti); the form is correct as one of the pṛṣodara group (irregular formations), and the etymologists explain it by likeness of letters. amitavikramaḥ: his three steps are unbounded, or his valour is. ambhonidhiḥ: the waters (ambhāṃsi), the gods and the others, are laid in him (‘these are the four waters: gods, men, fathers, asuras’, Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa); or the ocean (‘of lakes I am the ocean’, Gītā 10.24). anantātmā: unbounded by place, time and thing. mahodadhiśayaḥ: withdrawing all beings and making the world one ocean, he lies on it. antakaḥ: he makes an end of beings.

sanskrit.deva:
अजो महार्हः स्वाभाव्यो जितामित्रः प्रमोदनः ।
आनन्दो नन्दनोऽनन्दः सत्यधर्मा त्रिविक्रमः ॥ ६९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ajo mahārhaḥ svābhāvyo jitāmitraḥ pramodanaḥ |
ānando nandano 'nandaḥ satyadharmā trivikramaḥ || 69 ||

padaccheda.iast: ajaḥ mahā-arhaḥ svābhāvyaḥ jita-amitraḥ pramodanaḥ ānandaḥ nandanaḥ anandaḥ satya-dharmā tri-vikramaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अजः महा-अर्हः स्वाभाव्यः जित-अमित्रः प्रमोदनः आनन्दः नन्दनः अनन्दः सत्य-धर्मा त्रि-विक्रमः

translations.text: (He is) Aja, (Kāma, born from a, Viṣṇu); Mahārha, worthy of worship; Svābhāvya, ever accomplished by his nature; Jitāmitra, who has conquered the foes within and without; Pramodana, ever rejoicing (and gladdening those who meditate); Ānanda, Bliss; Nandana, who gladdens; Ananda, (who has no pleasure of objects; or Nanda, rich in all things); Satyadharmā, whose dharma (knowledge and the rest) is true; Trivikrama, whose three strides (spanned the three worlds).

notes: Śaṅkara: ajaḥ: Kāma, born (ja) from a, Viṣṇu. mahārhaḥ: worthy of mahas, worship. svābhāvyaḥ: being ever accomplished in nature, he is not to be brought about. jitāmitraḥ: he has conquered the foes within, attachment, aversion and the rest, and without, Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Śiśupāla and the others. pramodanaḥ: tasting the nectar of the Self he ever rejoices; or he gladdens those who meditate on him. ānandaḥ: bliss is his nature (‘on a portion of this bliss other beings live’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.3.32). nandanaḥ: he gladdens. nandaḥ: rich in all accomplishments; or anandaḥ: no worldly pleasure is his (‘the infinite is happiness; there is no happiness in the small’, Chāndogya 7.23.1). satyadharmā: his dharma, knowledge and the rest, is true. trivikramaḥ: his three strides spanned the three worlds (‘he strode three steps’, Ṛgveda 1.22.17; ‘the three worlds are called tri; you stride over them all, so you are Trivikrama’, Harivaṃśa).
The edition prints nandano 'nandaḥ; Śaṅkara explains both nandaḥ and anandaḥ.

sanskrit.deva:
महर्षिः कपिलाचार्यः कृतज्ञो मेदिनीपतिः ।
त्रिपदस्त्रिदशाध्यक्षो महाशृङ्गः कृतान्तकृत् ॥ ७० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
maharṣiḥ kapilācāryaḥ kṛtajño medinīpatiḥ |
tripadas tridaśādhyakṣo mahāśṛṅgaḥ kṛtāntakṛt || 70 ||

padaccheda.iast: mahā-ṛṣiḥ kapila-ācāryaḥ kṛta-jñaḥ medinī-patiḥ tri-padaḥ tridaśa-adhyakṣaḥ mahā-śṛṅgaḥ kṛtānta-kṛt
padaccheda.deva: महा-ऋषिः कपिल-आचार्यः कृत-ज्ञः मेदिनी-पतिः त्रि-पदः त्रिदश-अध्यक्षः महा-शृङ्गः कृतान्त-कृत्

translations.text: (He is) the great seer Kapila, the teacher (of the knowledge of the pure Self); Kṛtajña, the made (the world) and the knower (the Self); Medinīpati, Lord of the earth; Tripada, of three steps; Tridaśādhyakṣa, who oversees the three states (waking and the others); Mahāśṛṅga, (the Fish who played in the ocean of dissolution with the ship bound to his great horn); Kṛtāntakṛt, who ends what is made (and cuts off death).

notes: Śaṅkara: maharṣiḥ kapilācāryaḥ: one name with its qualifier. He is a great seer, seeing the whole Veda, while others are seers in seeing part of it; and Kapila, the teacher of Sāṃkhya, the knowledge of the pure Self (‘the knowledge of the pure Self is called Sāṃkhya’, Vyāsa; ‘the seer Kapila, born first’, Śvetāśvatara 5.2; ‘of the perfected, the sage Kapila’, Gītā 10.26). kṛtajñaḥ: kṛta, the made, the world; jña, the knower, the Self; both. medinīpatiḥ: lord of the earth. tripadaḥ: three steps are his (‘he strode three steps’). tridaśādhyakṣaḥ: the three states, waking and the others, arising from the touching of the guṇas: he oversees them. mahāśṛṅgaḥ: as the Fish, he played in the great ocean of dissolution with the ship bound to his great horn. kṛtāntakṛt: he brings to an end what is made; or he cuts off death (kṛtānta).

sanskrit.deva:
महावराहो गोविन्दः सुषेणः कनकाङ्गदी ।
गुह्यो गभीरो गहनो गुप्तश्चक्रगदाधरः ॥ ७१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
mahāvarāho govindaḥ suṣeṇaḥ kanakāṅgadī |
guhyo gabhīro gahano guptaś cakragadādharaḥ || 71 ||

padaccheda.iast: mahā-varāhaḥ govindaḥ su-ṣeṇaḥ kanaka-aṅgadī guhyaḥ gabhīraḥ gahanaḥ guptaḥ cakra-gadā-dharaḥ
padaccheda.deva: महा-वराहः गोविन्दः सु-षेणः कनक-अङ्गदी गुह्यः गभीरः गहनः गुप्तः चक्र-गदा-धरः

translations.text: (He is) Mahāvarāha, the great Boar; Govinda, (known by words, by the sentences of the Vedānta); Suṣeṇa, whose host (of attendants) is fine; Kanakāṅgadī, with golden armlets; Guhya, (to be known from the secret Upaniṣads, set in the cave of the heart); Gabhīra, deep (in knowledge, lordship and power); Gahana, hard to enter (the witness of the three states and their absence); Gupta, hidden (beyond speech and mind); Cakragadādhara, who bears the discus (the mind) and the mace (the intellect).

notes: Śaṅkara: mahāvarāhaḥ: great and a boar. govindaḥ: he is found (vindate) by words (go), known through the sentences of the Vedānta (‘because he is to be known by words alone, he is called Govinda’, Viṣṇutilaka). suṣeṇaḥ: his host, made of his attendants, is fine. kanakāṅgadī: his armlets are of gold. guhyaḥ: as known from the secret Upaniṣads, or set in the cave, the space of the heart. gabhīraḥ: deep in knowledge, lordship, strength and power. gahanaḥ: hard to enter; or as the witness of the presence and absence of the three states. guptaḥ: being beyond the reach of speech and mind (‘this Self, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth’, Kaṭha 1.3.12). cakragadādharaḥ: ‘holding the discus, which is the principle of mind, and the mace, which is the principle of intellect, to protect the world’.

sanskrit.deva:
वेधाः स्वाङ्गोऽजितः कृष्णो दृढः संकर्षणोऽच्युतः ।
वरुणो वारुणो वृक्षः पुष्कराक्षो महामनाः ॥ ७२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vedhāḥ svāṅgo 'jitaḥ kṛṣṇo dṛḍhaḥ saṃkarṣaṇo 'cyutaḥ |
varuṇo vāruṇo vṛkṣaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāmanāḥ || 72 ||

padaccheda.iast: vedhāḥ sva-aṅgaḥ ajitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ dṛḍhaḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ acyutaḥ varuṇaḥ vāruṇaḥ vṛkṣaḥ puṣkara-akṣaḥ mahā-manāḥ
padaccheda.deva: वेधाः स्व-अङ्गः अजितः कृष्णः दृढः संकर्षणः अच्युतः वरुणः वारुणः वृक्षः पुष्कर-अक्षः महा-मनाः

translations.text: (He is) Vedhā, the Creator; Svāṅga, (himself his own instrument in action); Ajita, never conquered (in his appearances); Kṛṣṇa, (Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana); Dṛḍha, firm (never falling from his nature or power); Saṃkarṣaṇo 'cyuta, who draws in all creatures at dissolution and does not fall from his nature; Varuṇa, (the setting sun, drawing in his rays); Vāruṇa, (Vasiṣṭha or Agastya, son of Varuṇa); Vṛkṣa, standing unmoving like a tree; Puṣkarākṣa, (who pervades, and shines when meditated on in the lotus of the heart); Mahāmanā, (who creates, preserves and ends by mind alone).

notes: Śaṅkara: vedhāḥ: the creator (vidhātṛ); the form is correct as one of the pṛṣodara group. svāṅgaḥ: in doing the work he is himself the helping limb. ajitaḥ: not conquered by anyone in his appearances. kṛṣṇaḥ: Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana (‘know Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa to be the lord Nārāyaṇa; who but the lotus-eyed could have made the Mahābhārata?’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). dṛḍhaḥ: as he never falls from his nature, power and the rest. saṃkarṣaṇo 'cyutaḥ: one name with its qualifier: at dissolution he draws in all creatures at once, and does not fall from his own nature. varuṇaḥ: the setting sun, who draws in his rays (‘hear this call of mine, Varuṇa’, Ṛgveda 1.25.19). vāruṇaḥ: Vasiṣṭha or Agastya, son of Varuṇa.

Śaṅkara: vṛkṣaḥ: he stands unmoving like a tree (‘like a tree firm in heaven stands the One’, Śvetāśvatara 3.9). puṣkarākṣaḥ: from akṣ ‘to pervade’ with puṣkara before it; or, meditated on in the lotus of the heart, he shines in his own nature. mahāmanāḥ: he does creation, preservation and ending by mind alone (‘who by mind alone makes and withdraws the world’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa).

sanskrit.deva:
भगवान्भगहानन्दी वनमाली हलायुधः ।
आदित्यो ज्योतिरादित्यः सहिष्णुर्गतिसत्तमः ॥ ७३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhagavān bhagahānandī vanamālī halāyudhaḥ |
ādityo jyotirādityaḥ sahiṣṇur gatisattamaḥ || 73 ||

padaccheda.iast: bhagavān bhaga-hā ānandī vana-mālī hala-āyudhaḥ ādityaḥ jyotiḥ-ādityaḥ sahiṣṇuḥ gati-sattamaḥ
padaccheda.deva: भगवान् भग-हा आनन्दी वन-माली हल-आयुधः आदित्यः ज्योतिः-आदित्यः सहिष्णुः गति-सत्तमः

words.meaning: the sun in the orb of light

translations.text: (He is) Bhagavān, (having the six bhagas: lordship, dharma, fame, glory, dispassion and liberation); Bhagahā, who takes away lordship and the rest at dissolution; Ānandī, blissful (full of all wealth); Vanamālī, wearing the Vaijayantī garland; Halāyudha, (as Balarāma) armed with the plough; Āditya, (born of Aditi as Vāmana); Jyotirāditya, (standing in the sun's orb); Sahiṣṇu, who bears the pairs (heat and cold); Gatisattama, the goal and the best.

notes: Śaṅkara: bhagavān: ‘bhaga is the name of the six: entire lordship, dharma, fame, glory, dispassion and liberation’; he has them (‘he who knows the origin and end of beings, their coming and going, knowledge and ignorance, is to be called Bhagavān’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). bhagahā: at dissolution he takes away lordship and the rest. ānandī: being of the nature of happiness; or rich in all prosperity. vanamālī: he wears the forest-garland called Vaijayantī, made of the subtle elements. halāyudhaḥ: his weapon is the plough, in the form of Balabhadra. ādityaḥ: born of Aditi and Kaśyapa as Vāmana. jyotirādityaḥ: standing in the orb of the sun, in the light. sahiṣṇuḥ: he endures the pairs, cold and heat and the rest. gatisattamaḥ: the goal and the best.

sanskrit.deva:
सुधन्वा खण्डपरशुर्दारुणो द्रविणप्रदः ।
दिवःस्पृक्सर्वदृग्व्यासो वाचस्पतिरयोनिजः ॥ ७४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sudhanvā khaṇḍaparaśur dāruṇo draviṇapradaḥ |
divaḥspṛk sarvadṛgvyāso vācaspatir ayonijaḥ || 74 ||

padaccheda.iast: su-dhanvā khaṇḍa-paraśuḥ dāruṇaḥ draviṇa-pradaḥ divaḥ-spṛk sarva-dṛk-vyāsaḥ vācaḥ-patiḥ ayoni-jaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सु-धन्वा खण्ड-परशुः दारुणः द्रविण-प्रदः दिवः-स्पृक् सर्व-दृक्-व्यासः वाचः-पतिः अयोनि-जः

translations.text: (He is) Sudhanvā, whose bow (Śārṅga) is fine; Khaṇḍaparaśu, (as Paraśurāma) whose axe cuts down foes; Dāruṇa, terrible (to the foes of the good path); Draviṇaprada, who gives devotees the wealth they wish; Divaḥspṛk, touching heaven; Sarvadṛgvyāsa, who spreads out the knowledge of all knowers (Vyāsa, who divided the Vedas); Vācaspatir Ayonija, the lord of knowledge, not born of a womb.

notes: Śaṅkara: sudhanvā: his bow Śārṅga, made of the senses and the rest, is fine. khaṇḍaparaśuḥ: in the form of Jāmadagnya, his axe cuts (khaṇḍa) his enemies; or his axe is unbroken (akhaṇḍa). dāruṇaḥ: terrible to those who oppose the good way. draviṇapradaḥ: he gives devotees the wealth they wish. divaḥspṛk: he touches heaven. sarvadṛgvyāsaḥ: he spreads out (vyāsa) the knowledge of all knowers; or sarvadṛk, knowledge of every form, or the sight of all; and vyāsa: he divided the Veda fourfold, the Ṛgveda into twenty-one branches, the Yajurveda into a hundred and one, the Sāmaveda into a thousand and the Atharvaveda into nine, and likewise the Purāṇas; Vyāsa is Brahmā. vācaspatir ayonijaḥ: one name with its qualifier: the lord of speech, knowledge, who is not born from a mother.

sanskrit.deva:
त्रिसामा सामगः साम निर्वाणं भेषजं भिषक् ।
संन्यासकृच्छमः शान्तो निष्ठा शान्तिः परायणम् ॥ ७५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
trisāmā sāmagaḥ sāma nirvāṇaṃ bheṣajaṃ bhiṣak |
saṃnyāsakṛc chamaḥ śānto niṣṭhā śāntiḥ parāyaṇam || 75 ||

lines.iast: trisāmā sāmagaḥ sāma nirvāṇaṃ bheṣajaṃ bhiṣak
lines.deva: त्रिसामा सामगः साम निर्वाणं भेषजं भिषक्

lines.iast: saṃnyāsakṛc chamaḥ śānto niṣṭhā śāntiḥ parāyaṇam

padaccheda.iast: tri-sāmā sāma-gaḥ sāma nirvāṇam bheṣajam bhiṣak saṃnyāsa-kṛt śamaḥ śāntaḥ niṣṭhā śāntiḥ parāyaṇam
padaccheda.deva: त्रि-सामा साम-गः साम निर्वाणम् भेषजम् भिषक् संन्यास-कृत् शमः शान्तः निष्ठा शान्तिः परायणम्

translations.text: (He is) Trisāmā, praised by the singers with the three Sāmans called Devavrata; Sāmaga, who sings the Sāman; Sāma, the Sāmaveda; Nirvāṇa, supreme bliss where all sorrow is stilled; Bheṣaja, the remedy (for the disease of the round); Bhiṣak, the physician (who taught in the Gītā the knowledge that frees from it); Saṃnyāsakṛt, who made the fourth stage, renunciation, for liberation; Śama, who teaches calm (to renouncers); Śānta, tranquil (unattached to the pleasures of objects); Niṣṭhā, in whom beings rest at dissolution; Śānti, peace (the end of all ignorance); Parāyaṇa, the supreme abode with no fear of return.

notes: Śaṅkara: trisāmā: praised by the Sāman-singers with the three Sāmans known as Devavrata. sāmagaḥ: he sings the Sāman (‘of the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda’, Gītā 10.22). sāma: the Sāmaveda. nirvāṇam: supreme bliss, the stilling of all sorrow. bheṣajam: the medicine for the disease of the round. bhiṣak: he taught in the Gītā the highest knowledge that frees from the disease of the round (‘I hear of you as the best of physicians’, Ṛgveda 2.33.4). saṃnyāsakṛt: for liberation he made the fourth stage of life. śamaḥ: he teaches calm, the chief means of knowledge for renouncers (‘calm is the dharma of yatis’); the form śama is from the causative ‘he does it, he teaches it’ with the suffix ac; or he calms all beings. śāntaḥ: unattached to the pleasures of objects (‘without parts, without action, tranquil’, Śvetāśvatara 6.19). niṣṭhā: at dissolution beings rest wholly in him. śāntiḥ: the ending of all ignorance. parāyaṇam: that, Brahman, is the supreme place, without fear of return; in the masculine reading the compound is a bahuvrīhi.

sanskrit.deva:
शुभाङ्गः शान्तिदः स्रष्टा कुमुदः कुवलेशयः ।
गोहितो गोपतिर्गोप्ता वृषभाक्षो वृषप्रियः ॥ ७६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śubhāṅgaḥ śāntidaḥ sraṣṭā kumudaḥ kuvaleśayaḥ |
gohito gopatir goptā vṛṣabhākṣo vṛṣapriyaḥ || 76 ||

padaccheda.iast: śubha-aṅgaḥ śānti-daḥ sraṣṭā kumudaḥ kuvaleśayaḥ go-hitaḥ go-patiḥ goptā vṛṣabha-akṣaḥ vṛṣa-priyaḥ
padaccheda.deva: शुभ-अङ्गः शान्ति-दः स्रष्टा कुमुदः कुवलेशयः गो-हितः गो-पतिः गोप्ता वृषभ-अक्षः वृष-प्रियः

translations.text: (He is) Śubhāṅga, of fair form; Śāntida, who gives peace (freedom from attachment and aversion); Sraṣṭā, the creator of all beings; Kumuda, who delights in the earth; Kuvaleśaya, who lies on the waters (or on Śeṣa); Gohita, who held up Govardhana for the good of the cows; Gopati, lord of the earth; Goptā, the protector (who also hides himself by his māyā); Vṛṣabhākṣa, whose eyes rain all desires (whose sight is dharma); Vṛṣapriya, to whom dharma is dear.

notes: Śaṅkara: śubhāṅgaḥ: bearing a lovely body. śāntidaḥ: he gives peace, freedom from attachment, aversion and the rest. sraṣṭā: at the beginning he created all beings. kumudaḥ: he delights (mud) in the earth (ku). kuvaleśayaḥ: kuvala is water, which surrounds the earth; he lies on it; or Takṣaka lies in the jujube fruit (kuvala), and he too is Hari's glory; or kuvala is the belly of serpents, which move on the earth, and he lies on the belly of Śeṣa. gohitaḥ: for the increase of the cows he held up Govardhana; or he takes a body wishing to lighten the earth's burden. gopatiḥ: lord of the earth. goptā: protector of the world; or he hides himself by his own māyā. vṛṣabhākṣaḥ: his eyes rain all desires; or his sight is dharma. vṛṣapriyaḥ: dharma is dear to him; or he is dharma and dear.

sanskrit.deva:
अनिवर्ती निवृत्तात्मा संक्षेप्ता क्षेमकृच्छिवः ।
श्रीवत्सवक्षाः श्रीवासः श्रीपतिः श्रीमतां वरः ॥ ७७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anivartī nivṛttātmā saṃkṣeptā kṣemakṛc chivaḥ |
śrīvatsavakṣāḥ śrīvāsaḥ śrīpatiḥ śrīmatāṃ varaḥ || 77 ||

padaccheda.iast: anivartī nivṛtta-ātmā saṃkṣeptā kṣema-kṛt śivaḥ śrīvatsa-vakṣāḥ śrī-vāsaḥ śrī-patiḥ śrīmatām varaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अनिवर्ती निवृत्त-आत्मा संक्षेप्ता क्षेम-कृत् शिवः श्रीवत्स-वक्षाः श्री-वासः श्री-पतिः श्रीमताम् वरः

words.meaning: with the Śrīvatsa on his breast

translations.text: (He is) Anivartī, who never turns back (from battle with the asuras, or from dharma); Nivṛttātmā, whose mind is turned from objects by nature; Saṃkṣeptā, who draws the vast world into subtle form (at dissolution); Kṣemakṛt, who guards what is gained; Śiva, who purifies by the mere remembrance of his name; Śrīvatsavakṣā, with the Śrīvatsa mark on his breast; Śrīvāsa, on whose breast Śrī dwells; Śrīpati, the lord of Śrī (and of the supreme power); the best of those who have glory (the Vedas).

notes: Śaṅkara: anivartī: he does not turn back from the battles of gods and asuras; or, loving dharma, from dharma. nivṛttātmā: his mind is by nature turned from objects. saṃkṣeptā: at dissolution he draws the spread-out world into subtle form. kṣemakṛt: he guards what has been gained. śivaḥ: he purifies by the mere remembrance of his name. Here the sixth hundred names are explained. śrīvatsavakṣāḥ: the mark called Śrīvatsa is on his breast. śrīvāsaḥ: Śrī dwells on his breast, never leaving. śrīpatiḥ: at the churning of the nectar Śrī passed over all the gods and asuras and chose him as husband; or Śrī is the supreme power, and he is its lord (‘his supreme power is heard of as manifold’, Śvetāśvatara 6.8). śrīmatāṃ varaḥ: the chief of those whose glory is the Ṛc, Yajus and Sāman, Viriñci and the others (‘the Ṛcs, Sāmans and Yajus: that is the deathless glory of the good’).

sanskrit.deva:
श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः ।
श्रीधरः श्रीकरः श्रेयः श्रीमांल्लोकत्रयाश्रयः ॥ ७८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śrīdaḥ śrīśaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ śrīnidhiḥ śrīvibhāvanaḥ |
śrīdharaḥ śrīkaraḥ śreyaḥ śrīmāṃl lokatrayāśrayaḥ || 78 ||

padaccheda.iast: śrī-daḥ śrī-īśaḥ śrī-nivāsaḥ śrī-nidhiḥ śrī-vibhāvanaḥ śrī-dharaḥ śrī-karaḥ śreyaḥ śrīmān loka-traya-āśrayaḥ
padaccheda.deva: श्री-दः श्री-ईशः श्री-निवासः श्री-निधिः श्री-विभावनः श्री-धरः श्री-करः श्रेयः श्रीमान् लोक-त्रय-आश्रयः

translations.text: (He is) Śrīda, who gives glory to devotees; Śrīśa, Lord of Śrī; Śrīnivāsa, who ever dwells in the glorious; Śrīnidhi, in whom all glories are stored; Śrīvibhāvana, who gives beings their glories as their deeds deserve; Śrīdhara, who bears Śrī, mother of all, on his breast; Śrīkara, who makes glory for those who remember, praise and worship him; Śreya, the highest good (unfailing happiness); Śrīmān, glorious; Lokatrayāśraya, the support of the three worlds.

notes: Śaṅkara: śrīdaḥ: he gives glory to devotees. śrīśaḥ: lord of Śrī. śrīnivāsaḥ: he ever dwells in the glorious; śrī here means those who have it. śrīnidhiḥ: all glories are stored in him, who holds all powers. śrīvibhāvanaḥ: he gives all beings various glories according to their deeds. śrīdharaḥ: he bears on his breast Śrī, the mother of all beings. śrīkaraḥ: he makes glory for devotees who remember, praise and worship him. śreyaḥ: the gaining of unfailing happiness is the highest good, and that is the very form of the supreme. śrīmān: glories are his. lokatrayāśrayaḥ: as the support of the three worlds.

sanskrit.deva:
स्वक्षः स्वङ्गः शतानन्दो नन्दिर्ज्योतिर्गणेश्वरः ।
विजितात्माविधेयात्मा सत्कीर्तिश्छिन्नसंशयः ॥ ७९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
svakṣaḥ svaṅgaḥ śatānando nandir jyotirgaṇeśvaraḥ |
vijitātmāvidheyātmā satkīrtiś chinnasaṃśayaḥ || 79 ||

padaccheda.iast: su-akṣaḥ su-aṅgaḥ śata-ānandaḥ nandiḥ jyotiḥ-gaṇa-īśvaraḥ vijita-ātmā avidheya-ātmā sat-kīrtiḥ chinna-saṃśayaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सु-अक्षः सु-अङ्गः शत-आनन्दः नन्दिः ज्योतिः-गण-ईश्वरः विजित-आत्मा अविधेय-आत्मा सत्-कीर्तिः छिन्न-संशयः

translations.text: (He is) Svakṣa, whose eyes are fair as lotuses; Svaṅga, of fair limbs; Śatānanda, (the one supreme bliss divided a hundredfold by its adjuncts); Nandi, whose form is supreme bliss; Jyotirgaṇeśvara, the Lord of the hosts of lights; Vijitātmā, who has mastered his mind; Avidheyātmā, whose nature no one commands; Satkīrti, whose fame is true; Chinnasaṃśaya, in whom there is no doubt, seeing all directly.

notes: Śaṅkara: svakṣaḥ: his eyes are fair, like lotuses. svaṅgaḥ: his limbs are fair. śatānandaḥ: the one supreme bliss is divided a hundredfold by the differences of adjuncts (‘on a portion of this bliss other beings live’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.3.32). nandiḥ: his form is supreme bliss. jyotirgaṇeśvaraḥ: lord of the hosts of lights (‘him shining, all shines after’, Muṇḍaka 2.2.11; ‘the light in the sun’, Gītā 15.12). vijitātmā: who has conquered the mind. avidheyātmā: whose nature cannot be commanded by anyone. satkīrtiḥ: whose fame is true. chinnasaṃśayaḥ: having seen all directly, like an āmalaka fruit in the palm, he has no doubt anywhere.

sanskrit.deva:
उदीर्णः सर्वतश्चक्षुरनीशः शाश्वतस्थिरः ।
भूशयो भूषणो भूतिर्विशोकः शोकनाशनः ॥ ८० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
udīrṇaḥ sarvataścakṣur anīśaḥ śāśvatasthiraḥ |
bhūśayo bhūṣaṇo bhūtir viśokaḥ śokanāśanaḥ || 80 ||

padaccheda.iast: udīrṇaḥ sarvataḥ-cakṣuḥ anīśaḥ śāśvata-sthiraḥ bhū-śayaḥ bhūṣaṇaḥ bhūtiḥ viśokaḥ śoka-nāśanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: उदीर्णः सर्वतः-चक्षुः अनीशः शाश्वत-स्थिरः भू-शयः भूषणः भूतिः विशोकः शोक-नाशनः

translations.text: (He is) Udīrṇa, raised above all beings; Sarvataścakṣu, who sees all everywhere by his consciousness; Anīśa, who has no lord over him; Śāśvatasthira, ever being and yet never changing; Bhūśaya, (Rāma) who lay on the ground by the sea seeking the way to Laṅkā; Bhūṣaṇa, who adorns the earth with his appearances; Bhūti, being itself (the cause of all glories); Viśoka, without sorrow (being supreme bliss); Śokanāśana, who destroys the sorrow of his devotees by mere remembrance.

notes: Śaṅkara: udīrṇaḥ: as risen above all beings. sarvataścakṣuḥ: he sees all everywhere by his own consciousness (‘with eyes everywhere’, Śvetāśvatara 3.3). anīśaḥ: none is lord over him (‘there is no lord of him’, Śvetāśvatara 6.9). śāśvatasthiraḥ: though always being, he never undergoes change; one name. bhūśayaḥ: seeking the way to Laṅkā, he lay on the ground facing the sea. bhūṣaṇaḥ: he adorns the earth with his many appearances taken by his own will. bhūtiḥ: being, existence; or glory; or as the cause of all glories. viśokaḥ: sorrow has gone from him, being one with supreme bliss. śokanāśanaḥ: by mere remembrance he destroys the sorrow of his devotees.

sanskrit.deva:
अर्चिष्मानर्चितः कुम्भो विशुद्धात्मा विशोधनः ।
अनिरुद्धोऽप्रतिरथः प्रद्युम्नोऽमितविक्रमः ॥ ८१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
arciṣmān arcitaḥ kumbho viśuddhātmā viśodhanaḥ |
aniruddho 'pratirathaḥ pradyumno 'mitavikramaḥ || 81 ||

padaccheda.iast: arciṣmān arcitaḥ kumbhaḥ viśuddha-ātmā viśodhanaḥ aniruddhaḥ apratirathaḥ pradyumnaḥ amita-vikramaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अर्चिष्मान् अर्चितः कुम्भः विशुद्ध-आत्मा विशोधनः अनिरुद्धः अप्रतिरथः प्रद्युम्नः अमित-विक्रमः

translations.text: (He is) Arciṣmān, the true Radiance (by whose light the moon and sun shine); Arcita, worshipped even by Viriñci and the others; Kumbha, (in whom all rests as in a pot); Viśuddhātmā, pure, beyond the three guṇas; Viśodhana, who wipes out sins by remembrance; Aniruddha, (the fourth of the four emanations, never held back by foes); Apratiratha, who has no rival; Pradyumna, whose wealth is great; Amitavikrama, of unmeasured valour.

notes: Śaṅkara: arciṣmān: the moon, the sun and the rest are radiant by his radiance; he alone is the true radiant one. arcitaḥ: worshipped even by Viriñci and the others whom all the worlds worship. kumbhaḥ: all rests in him as in a pot. viśuddhātmā: pure, being beyond the three guṇas, and the Self. viśodhanaḥ: by mere remembrance he wipes out sins. aniruddhaḥ: the fourth of the four emanations; or never stopped by enemies. apratirathaḥ: no opponent (pratiratha) is his. pradyumnaḥ: his wealth (dyumna) is great; or as one of the four emanations. amitavikramaḥ: his valour is unmeasured, or not hurt.

sanskrit.deva:
कालनेमिनिहा वीरः शौरिः शूरजनेश्वरः ।
त्रिलोकात्मा त्रिलोकेशः केशवः केशिहा हरिः ॥ ८२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kālaneminihā vīraḥ śauriḥ śūrajaneśvaraḥ |
trilokātmā trilokeśaḥ keśavaḥ keśihā hariḥ || 82 ||

padaccheda.iast: kālanemi-nihā vīraḥ śauriḥ śūra-jana-īśvaraḥ tri-loka-ātmā tri-loka-īśaḥ keśavaḥ keśi-hā hariḥ
padaccheda.deva: कालनेमि-निहा वीरः शौरिः शूर-जन-ईश्वरः त्रि-लोक-आत्मा त्रि-लोक-ईशः केशवः केशि-हा हरिः

translations.text: (He is) Kālaneminihā, slayer of the asura Kālanemi; Vīra, the brave; Śauri, born of Śūra's line; Śūrajaneśvara, who by his valour rules even Vāsava and the brave; Trilokātmā, the Self of the three worlds (which are not other than he); Trilokeśa, at whose command the three worlds keep to their tasks; Keśava, (whose rays, called hair, shine in the sun; or in whom Ka, Brahmā, and Īśa are); Keśihā, slayer of Keśin; Hari, who takes away the round with its cause.

notes: Śaṅkara: kālaneminihā: he slew the asura Kālanemi. vīraḥ: valiant. śauriḥ: born in the line of Śūra. śūrajaneśvaraḥ: by his surpassing valour he rules the brave, Vāsava and the others. trilokātmā: the self of the three worlds as their inner controller; or the three worlds are not, in truth, other than he. trilokeśaḥ: at his command the three worlds keep each to its work. keśavaḥ: the rays (keśa) that enter the sun and the rest are his (‘my rays that shine are called hair; so the all-knowing call me Keśava’, Mahābhārata); or the powers named Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva are called keśa (‘three hairy ones’; in ‘my two hairs on the earth’ keśa is used for power); ‘Ka is Brahmā, and I am Īśa of all embodied beings; we were born of your parts, so you bear the name Keśava’ (Harivaṃśa). keśihā: he slew the asura Keśin. hariḥ: he takes away the round together with its cause.

sanskrit.deva:
कामदेवः कामपालः कामी कान्तः कृतागमः ।
अनिर्देश्यवपुर्विष्णुर्वीरोऽनन्तो धनंजयः ॥ ८३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kāmadevaḥ kāmapālaḥ kāmī kāntaḥ kṛtāgamaḥ |
anirdeśyavapur viṣṇur vīro 'nanto dhanaṃjayaḥ || 83 ||

padaccheda.iast: kāma-devaḥ kāma-pālaḥ kāmī kāntaḥ kṛta-āgamaḥ anirdeśya-vapuḥ viṣṇuḥ vīraḥ anantaḥ dhanaṃjayaḥ
padaccheda.deva: काम-देवः काम-पालः कामी कान्तः कृत-आगमः अनिर्देश्य-वपुः विष्णुः वीरः अनन्तः धनंजयः

translations.text: (He is) Kāmadeva, the god desired by those who seek the four ends; Kāmapāla, who guards the desires of the desirous; Kāmī, whose desires are all fulfilled; Kānta, most beautiful (or in whom Brahmā ends); Kṛtāgama, who made scripture, śruti and smṛti; Anirdeśyavapu, whose form cannot be pointed out; Viṣṇu, (whose radiance fills heaven and earth); Vīra, who moves (and the rest); Ananta, endless in place, time and thing; Dhanaṃjaya, (Arjuna, who won wealth).

notes: Śaṅkara: kāmadevaḥ: he is desired by those who seek the four human ends, dharma and the rest, and he is god. kāmapālaḥ: he guards the desires of the desirous. kāmī: his nature is to have all desires fulfilled. kāntaḥ: bearing a most lovely body; or at the end of two parārdhas the end even of Ka, Brahmā, is from him. kṛtāgamaḥ: he made scripture, śruti, smṛti and the rest (‘śruti and smṛti are my commands’; ‘the Vedas, the śāstras, knowledge: all this from Janārdana’, as will be said). anirdeśyavapuḥ: being beyond the guṇas, his form cannot be pointed out as ‘this, such’. viṣṇuḥ: his radiance, pervading heaven and earth, is surpassing (‘my radiance stands pervading heaven and earth … by my stride I am named Viṣṇu’, Mahābhārata).

Śaṅkara: vīraḥ: having going and the rest (the root vī: going, begetting, shining, casting, eating). anantaḥ: being all-pervading, eternal and the Self of all, unbounded by place, time and thing (‘Brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite’, Taittirīya 2.1); or ‘gandharvas, apsarases, siddhas … do not reach the end of his qualities; so he is Ananta’ (Viṣṇu Purāṇa). dhanaṃjayaḥ: Arjuna, who won much wealth in his conquest of the quarters (‘of the Pāṇḍavas I am Dhanaṃjaya’, Gītā 10.37).

sanskrit.deva:
ब्रह्मण्यो ब्रह्मकृद्ब्रह्मा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविवर्धनः ।
ब्रह्मविद्ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मी ब्रह्मज्ञो ब्राह्मणप्रियः ॥ ८४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
brahmaṇyo brahmakṛd brahmā brahma brahmavivardhanaḥ |
brahmavid brāhmaṇo brahmī brahmajño brāhmaṇapriyaḥ || 84 ||

padaccheda.iast: brahmaṇyaḥ brahma-kṛt brahmā brahma brahma-vivardhanaḥ brahma-vit brāhmaṇaḥ brahmī brahma-jñaḥ brāhmaṇa-priyaḥ
padaccheda.deva: ब्रह्मण्यः ब्रह्म-कृत् ब्रह्मा ब्रह्म ब्रह्म-विवर्धनः ब्रह्म-वित् ब्राह्मणः ब्रह्मी ब्रह्म-ज्ञः ब्राह्मण-प्रियः

translations.text: (He is) Brahmaṇya, good to brahman (austerity, the Vedas, brāhmaṇas, knowledge); Brahmakṛt, the maker of austerity and the rest; Brahmā, who creates all as Brahmā; Brahman, (great, truth, knowledge, infinite); Brahmavivardhana, who increases austerity and the rest; Brahmavit, who knows the Veda and its meaning; Brāhmaṇa, (who as the brāhmaṇa teaches the Veda to the worlds); Brahmī, to whom all called brahman belongs; Brahmajña, who knows the Vedas as his own Self; Brāhmaṇapriya, dear to brāhmaṇas, to whom they are dear.

notes: Śaṅkara: brahmaṇyaḥ: ‘austerity, the Vedas, brāhmaṇas and knowledge are called brahman’; he is good to them. brahmakṛt: maker of austerity and the rest. brahmā: as Brahmā he creates all. brahma: great and making great, of the nature of truth and the rest (‘Brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite’; ‘that knowledge, in which all difference has set, pure being, beyond words, known to itself, is called Brahman’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). brahmavivardhanaḥ: he increases austerity and the rest. brahmavit: he knows the Veda and its meaning as they are. brāhmaṇaḥ: as a brāhmaṇa he teaches all the worlds, saying ‘this is (the teaching) of the Veda’ (vedasyāyam iti; the 1910 print has the misprint vedakhyāyam). brahmī: all that is called brahman belongs to him. brahmajñaḥ: he knows the Vedas as his own Self. brāhmaṇapriyaḥ: dear to brāhmaṇas, or brāhmaṇas are dear to him (‘he who does not bow duly to a brāhmaṇa even when struck, cursed, or spoken to harshly is a sinner, burnt by the fire of brahman, … not mine’, the Lord; Mahābhārata).

sanskrit.deva:
महाक्रमो महाकर्मा महातेजा महोरगः ।
महाक्रतुर्महायज्वा महायज्ञो महाहविः ॥ ८५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
mahākramo mahākarmā mahātejā mahoragaḥ |
mahākratur mahāyajvā mahāyajño mahāhaviḥ || 85 ||

padaccheda.iast: mahā-kramaḥ mahā-karmā mahā-tejāḥ mahā-uragaḥ mahā-kratuḥ mahā-yajvā mahā-yajñaḥ mahā-haviḥ
padaccheda.deva: महा-क्रमः महा-कर्मा महा-तेजाः महा-उरगः महा-क्रतुः महा-यज्वा महा-यज्ञः महा-हविः

translations.text: (He is) Mahākrama, of great strides; Mahākarmā, whose works (creation and the rest) are great; Mahātejā, whose light makes the sun and others shine; Mahoraga, the great serpent (Vāsuki); Mahākratu, the great sacrifice (the horse sacrifice); Mahāyajvā, the great sacrificer (for the good of the world); Mahāyajña, the great worship (the japa-sacrifice); Mahāhavi, the great oblation (the world offered in the Self).

notes: Śaṅkara: mahākramaḥ: his strides are great (‘may Viṣṇu, the wide-striding, give us welfare’). mahākarmā: his work, the creation of the world and the rest, is great. mahātejāḥ: by his light the sun and the other shining ones shine (‘by whose light the sun burns, kindled’; Gītā 15.12); or he is adorned with great qualities, valour and the rest. mahoragaḥ: a great serpent (‘of serpents I am Vāsuki’, Gītā 10.28). mahākratuḥ: a great sacrifice (‘as the horse sacrifice, king of sacrifices’, Manu 11.260); that too is he: praise. mahāyajvā: for the holding together of the world he performs sacrifices. mahāyajñaḥ: the great sacrifice (‘of sacrifices I am the japa-sacrifice’, Gītā 10.25). mahāhaviḥ: the great oblation: the whole world, offered in the Self, which is Brahman, as the Self. Or these, mahākratu and the rest, are bahuvrīhis.

sanskrit.deva:
स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः ।
पूर्णः पूरयिता पुण्यः पुण्यकीर्तिरनामयः ॥ ८६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
stavyaḥ stavapriyaḥ stotraṃ stutiḥ stotā raṇapriyaḥ |
pūrṇaḥ pūrayitā puṇyaḥ puṇyakīrtir anāmayaḥ || 86 ||

lines.iast: stavyaḥ stavapriyaḥ stotraṃ stutiḥ stotā raṇapriyaḥ
lines.deva: स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः

padaccheda.iast: stavyaḥ stava-priyaḥ stotram stutiḥ stotā raṇa-priyaḥ pūrṇaḥ pūrayitā puṇyaḥ puṇya-kīrtiḥ anāmayaḥ
padaccheda.deva: स्तव्यः स्तव-प्रियः स्तोत्रम् स्तुतिः स्तोता रण-प्रियः पूर्णः पूरयिता पुण्यः पुण्य-कीर्तिः अनामयः

translations.text: (He is) Stavya, praised by all and praising none; Stavapriya, fond of praise; Stotra, the hymn (that tells his qualities); Stuti, the act of praising; Stotā, the praiser too; Raṇapriya, to whom battle is dear (holding the five weapons to protect the world); Pūrṇa, full (of all desires and powers); Pūrayitā, who fills all with riches; Puṇya, who wipes out sins by remembrance; Puṇyakīrti, whose fame brings merit; Anāmaya, untouched by ills within and without.

notes: Śaṅkara: stavyaḥ: praised by all, praising none. stavapriyaḥ: hence fond of praise. stotram: that by which he is praised, the telling of his qualities: that too is Hari. stutiḥ: the act of praising. stotā: the praiser too is he. raṇapriyaḥ: battle is dear to him, since he always bears the five great weapons to protect the world. pūrṇaḥ: full of all desires and all powers. pūrayitā: not only full, but filling all with riches. puṇyaḥ: by mere remembrance he wipes out sins. puṇyakīrtiḥ: his fame brings merit to men. anāmayaḥ: not afflicted by ills, inner or outer, that are born of action.

sanskrit.deva:
मनोजवस्तीर्थकरो वसुरेता वसुप्रदः ।
वसुप्रदो वासुदेवो वसुर्वसुमना हविः ॥ ८७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
manojavas tīrthakaro vasuretā vasupradaḥ |
vasuprado vāsudevo vasur vasumanā haviḥ || 87 ||

padaccheda.iast: manaḥ-javaḥ tīrtha-karaḥ vasu-retāḥ vasu-pradaḥ vasu-pradaḥ vāsudevaḥ vasuḥ vasu-manāḥ haviḥ
padaccheda.deva: मनः-जवः तीर्थ-करः वसु-रेताः वसु-प्रदः वसु-प्रदः वासुदेवः वसुः वसु-मनाः हविः

translations.text: (He is) Manojava, swift as the mind (being everywhere); Tīrthakara, the maker and teacher of the fourteen branches of knowledge (and of the doctrines outside them); Vasuretā, whose seed is gold; Vasuprada, who gives wealth directly; Vasuprada, who gives his devotees the highest wealth, liberation; Vāsudeva, the son of Vasudeva; Vasu, (in whom beings dwell, and who dwells in them); Vasumanā, whose mind dwells equally in all things; Havi, the oblation (Brahman).

notes: Śaṅkara: manojavaḥ: being everywhere, his speed is like the mind's. tīrthakaraḥ: the maker and teacher of the fourteen branches of knowledge and of the systems outside them; the Purāṇa-tellers relate that as Hayagrīva, having slain Madhu and Kaiṭabha, he taught Viriñci at the beginning of creation the Vedas and the other branches of knowledge, and taught the systems outside the Veda to delude the enemies of the gods. vasuretāḥ: gold (vasu) is his seed (‘the god first created the waters and cast his seed in them; it became a golden egg, the supreme cause of Brahmā’, Vyāsa). vasupradaḥ: he gives wealth abundantly, being himself the lord of wealth; the other (Kubera) is lord of wealth by his grace.

Śaṅkara: vasupradaḥ (the second): he gives his devotees the highest wealth, the fruit called liberation (‘Brahman is knowledge, bliss, the final goal of the giver’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.9.28); or he utterly destroys (pra-do) the wealth of the gods' enemies. vāsudevaḥ: the son of Vasudeva. vasuḥ: beings dwell in him, and he dwells in them. vasumanāḥ: his mind dwells (vas) equally in all objects. haviḥ: (‘the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman’, Gītā 4.24).

sanskrit.deva:
सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सत्ता सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः ।
शूरसेनो यदुश्रेष्ठः सन्निवासः सुयामुनः ॥ ८८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sadgatiḥ satkṛtiḥ sattā sadbhūtiḥ satparāyaṇaḥ |
śūraseno yaduśreṣṭhaḥ sannivāsaḥ suyāmunaḥ || 88 ||

padaccheda.iast: sat-gatiḥ sat-kṛtiḥ sattā sat-bhūtiḥ sat-parāyaṇaḥ śūra-senaḥ yadu-śreṣṭhaḥ sat-nivāsaḥ su-yāmunaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सत्-गतिः सत्-कृतिः सत्ता सत्-भूतिः सत्-परायणः शूर-सेनः यदु-श्रेष्ठः सत्-निवासः सु-यामुनः

translations.text: (He is) Sadgati, reached by the good (those who know ‘Brahman is’), or whose understanding is good; Satkṛti, whose work (guarding the world) is good; Sattā, being (pure experience without difference within or without); Sadbhūti, (the supreme Self, real because never sublated, and shining); Satparāyaṇa, the supreme goal of those who know the truth; Śūrasena, whose army (Hanūmān and the others) is valiant; Yaduśreṣṭha, the best of the Yadus; Sannivāsa, the abode of the wise; Suyāmuna, (attended by the fair folk of the Yamunā).

notes: Śaṅkara: sadgatiḥ: ‘if one knows that Brahman is, then they know him as being’ (Taittirīya 2.6); those who know Brahman as being are the good (santaḥ), and he is reached by them; or his understanding is good. satkṛtiḥ: his work, protecting the world, is good. Here the seventh hundred names are explained. sattā: experience free of difference within, from things of its kind and of other kinds (‘one only, without a second’, Chāndogya 6.2.1). sadbhūtiḥ: the supreme Self, consciousness, is being, since it is not sublated and it shines; nothing else is, since it is known and is sublated: it is neither being nor non-being; the sublation of the manifold meant is that by scripture or by reasoning.

Śaṅkara: satparāyaṇaḥ: the highest abode of the good, those who know the truth. śūrasenaḥ: his army, in which Hanūmān and other soldiers are valiant. yaduśreṣṭhaḥ: as the chief of the Yadus. sannivāsaḥ: the refuge of the wise. suyāmunaḥ: those of the Yamunā, Devakī, Vasudeva, Nanda, Yaśodā, Balabhadra, Subhadrā and others, who surround him, are fair; or the cowherd folk of the Yamunā, Padmāsana and others, are his fair attendants.

sanskrit.deva:
भूतावासो वासुदेवः सर्वासुनिलयोऽनलः ।
दर्पहा दर्पदो दृप्तो दुर्धरोऽथापराजितः ॥ ८९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhūtāvāso vāsudevaḥ sarvāsunilayo 'nalaḥ |
darpahā darpado dṛpto durdharo 'thāparājitaḥ || 89 ||

padaccheda.iast: bhūta-āvāsaḥ vāsudevaḥ sarva-asu-nilayaḥ analaḥ darpa-hā darpa-daḥ dṛptaḥ durdharaḥ atha aparājitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: भूत-आवासः वासुदेवः सर्व-असु-निलयः अनलः दर्प-हा दर्प-दः दृप्तः दुर्धरः अथ अपराजितः

translations.text: (He is) Bhūtāvāsa, in whom beings dwell; Vāsudeva, (who covers the world by māyā, and is god); Sarvāsunilaya, in whom all the breaths come to rest; Anala, whose powers have no ‘enough’; Darpahā, who destroys the pride of those on the wrong path; Darpada, who gives pride (honour) to those on the path of dharma; Dṛpta, ever joyful (tasting the nectar of the Self); Durdhara, hardly held in the heart; and Aparājita, never conquered.

notes: Śaṅkara: bhūtāvāsaḥ: beings dwell in him (‘beings dwell in you, so you are Bhūtāvāsa’, Harivaṃśa). vāsudevaḥ: he covers (vas) the world by māyā, and is god (‘I cover the whole world, becoming as the sun with its rays’, the Lord). sarvāsunilayaḥ: all the breaths (asu) are dissolved in him, their ground, the self of the jīva. analaḥ: there is no ‘enough’ to his wealth of powers. darpahā: he destroys the pride of those who stand on paths against dharma. darpadaḥ: he gives pride to those who walk the way of dharma. dṛptaḥ: tasting the nectar of the Self, he is ever joyful.

Śaṅkara: durdharaḥ: being free of all adjuncts he cannot be held in meditation; yet by his grace some hold him in the heart with difficulty, by contemplation over thousands of births (‘the trouble is greater for those whose minds are set on the unmanifest’, Gītā 12.5). aparājitaḥ: not defeated by inner foes, attachment and the rest, nor by outer ones, the dānavas.

sanskrit.deva:
विश्वमूर्तिर्महामूर्तिर्दीप्तमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान् ।
अनेकमूर्तिरव्यक्तः शतमूर्तिः शताननः ॥ ९० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
viśvamūrtir mahāmūrtir dīptamūrtir amūrtimān |
anekamūrtir avyaktaḥ śatamūrtiḥ śatānanaḥ || 90 ||

padaccheda.iast: viśva-mūrtiḥ mahā-mūrtiḥ dīpta-mūrtiḥ amūrtimān aneka-mūrtiḥ avyaktaḥ śata-mūrtiḥ śata-ānanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: विश्व-मूर्तिः महा-मूर्तिः दीप्त-मूर्तिः अमूर्तिमान् अनेक-मूर्तिः अव्यक्तः शत-मूर्तिः शत-आननः

translations.text: (He is) Viśvamūrti, whose form is the universe (being the Self of all); Mahāmūrti, of great form (lying on Śeṣa); Dīptamūrti, whose form is knowledge, shining; Amūrtimān, who has no body bound by action; Anekamūrti, who takes many forms (to help the worlds); Avyakta, not manifest (as just this); Śatamūrti, of a hundred forms (born of the many notions of consciousness); Śatānana, hundred-faced.

notes: Śaṅkara: viśvamūrtiḥ: the universe is his form, as he is the Self of all. mahāmūrtiḥ: his form, lying on the couch of Śeṣa, is great. dīptamūrtiḥ: his form is made of knowledge, shining; or the bright form he takes by his own will is shining. amūrtimān: no body bound by action is his. anekamūrtiḥ: in his appearances he takes by his will many forms that help the worlds. avyaktaḥ: though he has many forms, it is not made manifest that he is just such. śatamūrtiḥ: the forms born of various notions belong to him whose form is consciousness. śatānanaḥ: since he has the form of the universe and the rest, he is hundred-faced.

sanskrit.deva:
एको नैकः सवः कः किं यत्तत्पदमनुत्तमम् ।
लोकबन्धुर्लोकनाथो माधवो भक्तवत्सलः ॥ ९१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
eko naikaḥ savaḥ kaḥ kiṃ yat tat padam anuttamam |
lokabandhur lokanātho mādhavo bhaktavatsalaḥ || 91 ||

lines.iast: eko naikaḥ savaḥ kaḥ kiṃ yat tat padam anuttamam
lines.deva: एको नैकः सवः कः किं यत्तत्पदमनुत्तमम्

padaccheda.iast: ekaḥ naikaḥ savaḥ kaḥ kim yat tat padam anuttamam loka-bandhuḥ loka-nāthaḥ mādhavaḥ bhakta-vatsalaḥ
padaccheda.deva: एकः नैकः सवः कः किम् यत् तत् पदम् अनुत्तमम् लोक-बन्धुः लोक-नाथः माधवः भक्त-वत्सलः

translations.text: (He is) Eka, the One (free of all difference); Naika, not one (many by māyā); Sava, the sacrifice in which soma is pressed; Ka, happiness; Kim, what is to be inquired into; Yat, (that from which beings arise); Tat, that (which extends); the unsurpassed State; Lokabandhu, the kinsman of the worlds; Lokanātha, the lord of the worlds; Mādhava, born in the line of Madhu; Bhaktavatsala, loving to his devotees.

notes: Śaṅkara: ekaḥ: in truth free of all difference, of its kind, of other kinds and within (‘one only, without a second’, Chāndogya 6.2.1). naikaḥ: by māyā he has many forms (‘Indra by his māyās goes in many forms’). savaḥ: the sacrifice in which soma is pressed. kaḥ: ka means happiness; he is praised by it (‘Brahman is ka’, Chāndogya 4.10.5). kim: Brahman, to be inquired into, being all the human ends. yat: the word that points to a thing established of itself names Brahman (‘that from which these beings are born’, Taittirīya 3.1). tat: Brahman, which extends (tan) (‘Om tat sat: this is the threefold designation of Brahman’, Gītā 17.23). padam anuttamam: one name with its qualifier: the state reached by seekers of liberation, than which there is nothing higher.

Śaṅkara: lokabandhuḥ: all the worlds are bound (badh) in him, their ground; or, as the father of the worlds, there is no kinsman like him; or he gave the teaching of what is good and bad, śruti and smṛti. lokanāthaḥ: the worlds pray to him; or he afflicts (upatapati), blesses or rules them. mādhavaḥ: born in the line of Madhu. bhaktavatsalaḥ: full of love for his devotees.

sanskrit.deva:
सुवर्णवर्णो हेमाङ्गो वराङ्गश्चन्दनाङ्गदी ।
वीरहा विषमः शून्यो घृताशीरचलश्चलः ॥ ९२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
suvarṇavarṇo hemāṅgo varāṅgaś candanāṅgadī |
vīrahā viṣamaḥ śūnyo ghṛtāśīr acalaś calaḥ || 92 ||

lines.iast: vīrahā viṣamaḥ śūnyo ghṛtāśīr acalaś calaḥ

padaccheda.iast: suvarṇa-varṇaḥ hema-aṅgaḥ vara-aṅgaḥ candana-aṅgadī vīra-hā viṣamaḥ śūnyaḥ ghṛta-āśīḥ acalaḥ calaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सुवर्ण-वर्णः हेम-अङ्गः वर-अङ्गः चन्दन-अङ्गदी वीर-हा विषमः शून्यः घृत-आशीः अचलः चलः

translations.text: (He is) Suvarṇavarṇa, golden of hue; Hemāṅga, whose body is like gold (the golden Puruṣa in the sun); Varāṅga, of fine limbs; Candanāṅgadī, adorned with delightful armlets; Vīrahā, slayer of the heroic asuras; Viṣama, who has no equal; Śūnya, (as if empty, being free of all distinctions); Ghṛtāśī, whose wishes have dropped away; Acala, never moving (from his nature, power or qualities); Cala, moving (as the wind).

notes: Śaṅkara: suvarṇavarṇaḥ: his colour is like gold (‘when the seer sees the golden-hued’, Muṇḍaka 3.1.3). hemāṅgaḥ: his body is like gold (‘the golden Puruṣa within the sun’, Chāndogya 1.6.6). varāṅgaḥ: his limbs are fine. candanāṅgadī: adorned with delightful (candana) armlets. vīrahā: to protect dharma he slays the heroic chiefs of the asuras. viṣamaḥ: none is like him, being unlike all (Gītā 11.43). śūnyaḥ: being free of all distinctions, he is like a void. ghṛtāśīḥ: his wishes have dripped away (ghṛta), dissolved. acalaḥ: there is no moving from his nature, power, knowledge or other qualities. calaḥ: he moves in the form of the wind.

sanskrit.deva:
अमानी मानदो मान्यो लोकस्वामी त्रिलोकधृक् ।
सुमेधा मेधजो धन्यः सत्यमेधा धराधरः ॥ ९३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
amānī mānado mānyo lokasvāmī trilokadhṛk |
sumedhā medhajo dhanyaḥ satyamedhā dharādharaḥ || 93 ||

padaccheda.iast: amānī māna-daḥ mānyaḥ loka-svāmī tri-loka-dhṛk su-medhāḥ medha-jaḥ dhanyaḥ satya-medhāḥ dharā-dharaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अमानी मान-दः मान्यः लोक-स्वामी त्रि-लोक-धृक् सु-मेधाः मेध-जः धन्यः सत्य-मेधाः धरा-धरः

translations.text: (He is) Amānī, who takes nothing that is not the Self for the Self; Mānada, who gives that notion to all by his māyā (and honour to his devotees, and takes it from the knowers of truth); Mānya, honoured by all, being the lord of all; Lokasvāmī, master of the fourteen worlds; Trilokadhṛk, who holds the three worlds; Sumedhā, of good intelligence; Medhaja, born in sacrifice; Dhanya, who has all he seeks; Satyamedhā, whose intelligence is true; Dharādhara, who holds the whole earth (with his portions, Śeṣa and the rest).

notes: Śaṅkara: amānī: being pure consciousness, he has no notion of self in what is not the Self. mānadaḥ: by his māyā he gives all the notion of self in what is not the Self; or gives honour to his devotees; or cuts off that notion in the knowers of the truth. mānyaḥ: to be honoured and worshipped by all, as the lord of all. lokasvāmī: as lord of the fourteen worlds. trilokadhṛk: he holds the three worlds. sumedhāḥ: his intelligence is good (Pāṇini 5.4.122). medhajaḥ: born in the sacrifice (medha). dhanyaḥ: who has attained his ends. satyamedhāḥ: his intelligence is true. dharādharaḥ: by all his portions, Śeṣa and the others, he holds the whole earth.

sanskrit.deva:
तेजोवृषो द्युतिधरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः ।
प्रग्रहो निग्रहो व्यग्रो नैकशृङ्गो गदाग्रजः ॥ ९४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tejovṛṣo dyutidharaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ |
pragraho nigraho vyagro naikaśṛṅgo gadāgrajaḥ || 94 ||

padaccheda.iast: tejaḥ-vṛṣaḥ dyuti-dharaḥ sarva-śastra-bhṛtām varaḥ pragrahaḥ nigrahaḥ vyagraḥ naika-śṛṅgaḥ gada-agrajaḥ
padaccheda.deva: तेजः-वृषः द्युति-धरः सर्व-शस्त्र-भृताम् वरः प्रग्रहः निग्रहः व्यग्रः नैक-शृङ्गः गद-अग्रजः

translations.text: (He is) Tejovṛṣa, who as the sun always rains the waters; Dyutidhara, who bears the beauty of his limbs; the best of all bearers of weapons; Pragraha, who accepts the leaf and flower offered by devotees (and reins in the horses of the senses); Nigraha, who holds all in check; Vyagra, who has no end (and is eager to give devotees their wish); Naikaśṛṅga, four-horned; Gadāgraja, (manifest first by the mantra, or elder brother of Gada).

notes: Śaṅkara: tejovṛṣaḥ: as the sun he always rains the waters (tejas). dyutidharaḥ: he bears the beauty of his limbs. sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ: best of all who bear weapons. pragrahaḥ: he takes the leaf, flower and the like offered by devotees; or by his grace he binds as with reins the horses of the untamed senses running in the forest of objects (Pāṇini 1.1.15 on the word). nigrahaḥ: by his power he holds all in check. vyagraḥ: his end (agra), destruction, has gone; or he is eager in giving devotees what they wish. naikaśṛṅgaḥ: four-horned (‘four horns’, Ṛgveda 4.58.3). gadāgrajaḥ: he is born first (agra) by the mantra (nigada), the ni dropped; or he was born before Gada, the younger brother of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit.deva:
चतुर्मूर्तिश्चतुर्बाहुश्चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्गतिः ।
चतुरात्मा चतुर्भावश्चतुर्वेदविदेकपात् ॥ ९५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
caturmūrtiś caturbāhuś caturvyūhaś caturgatiḥ |
caturātmā caturbhāvaś caturvedavid ekapāt || 95 ||

padaccheda.iast: catur-mūrtiḥ catur-bāhuḥ catur-vyūhaḥ catur-gatiḥ catur-ātmā catur-bhāvaḥ catur-veda-vit eka-pāt
padaccheda.deva: चतुर्-मूर्तिः चतुर्-बाहुः चतुर्-व्यूहः चतुर्-गतिः चतुर्-आत्मा चतुर्-भावः चतुर्-वेद-वित् एक-पात्

translations.text: (He is) Caturmūrti, of four forms (Virāj, the Thread-self, the Unmanifest, the Fourth; or white, red, yellow, dark); Caturbāhu, four-armed (a name proper to Vāsudeva); Caturvyūha, whose four emanations are the four puruṣas; Caturgati, the goal of the four stages and four classes; Caturātmā, whose mind is clear (free of attachment), or the fourfold inner organ; Caturbhāva, from whom the four human ends arise; Caturvedavit, who knows the meaning of the four Vedas; Ekapāt, of one foot (all beings are a quarter of him).

notes: Śaṅkara: caturmūrtiḥ: his four forms are Virāj, the Sūtrātman, the Unmanifest and the Fourth; or white, red, yellow and dark. caturbāhuḥ: four arms are his; the name is fixed for Vāsudeva. caturvyūhaḥ: his four emanations are the four puruṣas of the Ṛgvedic Upaniṣad: the bodily puruṣa, the metrical puruṣa, the Veda-puruṣa and the great puruṣa. caturgatiḥ: the goal of the four stages and four classes who do as enjoined. caturātmā: his mind is clear (catura), free of attachment and the rest; or he is the fourfold inner organ, mind, intellect, ego and memory. caturbhāvaḥ: the four human ends, dharma, wealth, desire and liberation, arise from him. caturvedavit: he knows the meaning of the four Vedas as it is. ekapāt: one foot is his (‘all beings are a quarter of him’, Ṛgveda 10.90.3; ‘I stand supporting this whole world with one portion’, Gītā 10.42).

sanskrit.deva:
समावर्तोऽनिवृत्तात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः ।
दुर्लभो दुर्गमो दुर्गो दुरावासो दुरारिहा ॥ ९६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
samāvarto 'nivṛttātmā durjayo duratikramaḥ |
durlabho durgamo durgo durāvāso durārihā || 96 ||

padaccheda.iast: samāvartaḥ anivṛtta-ātmā durjayaḥ duratikramaḥ durlabhaḥ durgamaḥ durgaḥ durāvāsaḥ durāri-hā
padaccheda.deva: समावर्तः अनिवृत्त-आत्मा दुर्जयः दुरतिक्रमः दुर्लभः दुर्गमः दुर्गः दुरावासः दुरारि-हा

translations.text: (He is) Samāvarta, who rightly turns the wheel of the round; Anivṛttātmā, who, being everywhere, is turned away from nothing; Durjaya, not to be conquered; Duratikrama, whose command none transgresses; Durlabha, gained only by rare devotion; Durgama, known with difficulty; Durga, reached with difficulty (hindered by obstacles); Durāvāsa, lodged in the mind by yogins only with difficulty; Durārihā, slayer of the evil foes, the dānavas.

notes: Śaṅkara: samāvartaḥ: he turns the wheel of the round rightly. anivṛttātmā: being present everywhere, he is not turned away from objects. durjayaḥ: he cannot be conquered. duratikramaḥ: being the cause of fear, the sun and the others do not transgress his command (‘from fear of him fire burns, from fear the sun gives heat, from fear Indra and the wind, and Death runs as the fifth’, Kaṭha 2.3.3; ‘a great fear, a raised thunderbolt’, Kaṭha 2.3.2). durlabhaḥ: gained by rare devotion (‘in men whose sins are spent by austerity, knowledge and absorption over thousands of births, devotion to Kṛṣṇa arises’, Vyāsa; ‘to be gained by undivided devotion’, Gītā 8.22). durgamaḥ: known with difficulty. durgaḥ: reached with difficulty by those hindered by obstacles. durāvāsaḥ: made to dwell in the mind by yogins in absorption only with difficulty. durārihā: he slays the dānavas and other evil foes.

sanskrit.deva:
शुभाङ्गो लोकसारङ्गः सुतन्तुस्तन्तुवर्धनः ।
इन्द्रकर्मा महाकर्मा कृतकर्मा कृतागमः ॥ ९७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śubhāṅgo lokasāraṅgaḥ sutantus tantuvardhanaḥ |
indrakarmā mahākarmā kṛtakarmā kṛtāgamaḥ || 97 ||

padaccheda.iast: śubha-aṅgaḥ loka-sāraṅgaḥ su-tantuḥ tantu-vardhanaḥ indra-karmā mahā-karmā kṛta-karmā kṛta-āgamaḥ
padaccheda.deva: शुभ-अङ्गः लोक-सारङ्गः सु-तन्तुः तन्तु-वर्धनः इन्द्र-कर्मा महा-कर्मा कृत-कर्मा कृत-आगमः

words.meaning: who takes the essence of the worlds

translations.text: (He is) Śubhāṅga, to be meditated on in fair limbs; Lokasāraṅga, who takes the essence of the worlds as a bee (or is known through Om, the essence of the worlds); Sutantu, whose thread, the manifold, is fair; Tantuvardhana, who extends that thread (or cuts it); Indrakarmā, whose deeds are lordly; Mahākarmā, whose works are the great elements; Kṛtakarmā, who has done all (and has nothing to do); Kṛtāgama, who made the scripture, the Veda.

notes: Śaṅkara: śubhāṅgaḥ: as he is to be meditated on with fair limbs. lokasāraṅgaḥ: like a bee (sāraṅga) he takes the essence of the worlds (‘Prajāpati brooded over the worlds’, Chāndogya 2.23.2); or the essence of the worlds is Om, and he is known through it. sutantuḥ: his thread, the spread-out manifold, is fair. tantuvardhanaḥ: he increases that thread, or cuts it. indrakarmā: his deeds are those of Indra, lordly. mahākarmā: his effects are the great elements, space and the rest. kṛtakarmā: having attained all ends he has nothing left to do; or he has done dharma. kṛtāgamaḥ: he made the scripture, the Veda (‘the breath of this great being’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.4.10).

sanskrit.deva:
उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दो रत्ननाभः सुलोचनः ।
अर्को वाजसनः शृङ्गी जयन्तः सर्वविज्जयी ॥ ९८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
udbhavaḥ sundaraḥ sundo ratnanābhaḥ sulocanaḥ |
arko vājasanaḥ śṛṅgī jayantaḥ sarvavijjayī || 98 ||

padaccheda.iast: udbhavaḥ sundaraḥ sundaḥ ratna-nābhaḥ su-locanaḥ arkaḥ vāja-sanaḥ śṛṅgī jayantaḥ sarva-vit-jayī
padaccheda.deva: उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दः रत्न-नाभः सु-लोचनः अर्कः वाज-सनः शृङ्गी जयन्तः सर्व-वित्-जयी

translations.text: (He is) Udbhava, who takes a high birth by his will (or has no birth, being the cause of all); Sundara, beautiful beyond all; Sunda, the compassionate (whose heart is wet); Ratnanābha, whose navel is beautiful as a jewel; Sulocana, whose eyes (and knowledge) are fair; Arka, worshipful even to Brahmā and the others; Vājasana, who gives food to those who ask; Śṛṅgī, (the Fish with a horn in the waters of dissolution); Jayanta, who conquers the foes; Sarvavijjayī, all-knowing and wont to conquer the foes within and without.

notes: Śaṅkara: udbhavaḥ: by his own will he takes a high birth; or birth has gone from him, being the cause of all. sundaraḥ: having a charm surpassing all. sundaḥ: he moistens (und), is tender-hearted, compassionate. ratnanābhaḥ: his navel is lovely as a jewel. sulocanaḥ: his eyes, or his knowledge, are fair. arkaḥ: worthy of worship even by Brahmā and the others who are most worshipful. vājasanaḥ: he gives food (vāja) to those who ask. śṛṅgī: in the waters of dissolution, the Fish with a horn. jayantaḥ: he conquers foes utterly, or is the cause of victory. sarvavijjayī: one name: all-knowing, and wont to conquer the inner foes, attachment and the rest, and the outer ones hard to conquer, Hiraṇyākṣa and the rest.

sanskrit.deva:
सुवर्णबिन्दुरक्षोभ्यः सर्ववागीश्वरेश्वरः ।
महाह्रदो महागर्तो महाभूतो महानिधिः ॥ ९९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
suvarṇabindur akṣobhyaḥ sarvavāgīśvareśvaraḥ |
mahāhrado mahāgarto mahābhūto mahānidhiḥ || 99 ||

padaccheda.iast: suvarṇa-binduḥ akṣobhyaḥ sarva-vāk-īśvara-īśvaraḥ mahā-hradaḥ mahā-gartaḥ mahā-bhūtaḥ mahā-nidhiḥ
padaccheda.deva: सुवर्ण-बिन्दुः अक्षोभ्यः सर्व-वाक्-ईश्वर-ईश्वरः महा-ह्रदः महा-गर्तः महा-भूतः महा-निधिः

words.meaning: lord of the lords of speech

translations.text: (He is) Suvarṇabindu, whose limbs are like gold (or the mantra with fair syllable and bindu); Akṣobhya, unshaken (by attachment, by objects, or by the foes of the gods); Sarvavāgīśvareśvara, lord of all the lords of speech (Brahmā and the others); Mahāhrada, the great lake (where yogins plunge into bliss and rest); Mahāgarta, whose māyā is a great abyss (or the great chariot-warrior); Mahābhūta, unbounded by the three times; Mahānidhi, the great treasure in which all beings are laid.

notes: Śaṅkara: suvarṇabinduḥ: his limbs are like gold (‘to the tips of the nails all golden’, Chāndogya 1.6.6); or he is the mantra in which the syllable and the bindu are fair.
