Here the eighth hundred names are explained. akṣobhyaḥ: not shaken by attachment, aversion and the rest, by sound and the other objects, or by the foes of the thirty gods. sarvavāgīśvareśvaraḥ: lord even of Brahmā and the other lords of speech. mahāhradaḥ: like a great lake: yogins plunge into his bliss and rest at ease. mahāgartaḥ: his māyā is like a great pit, hard to cross (‘my māyā is hard to cross’, Gītā 7.14); or garta means chariot (Nirukta), so the great chariot-warrior, as he is known in the Bhārata. mahābhūtaḥ: his nature is not bounded by the three times. mahānidhiḥ: all beings are laid in him; great and the treasure.

sanskrit.deva:
कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनोऽनिलः ।
अमृताशोऽमृतवपुः सर्वज्ञः सर्वतोमुखः ॥ १०० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kumudaḥ kundaraḥ kundaḥ parjanyaḥ pāvano 'nilaḥ |
amṛtāśo 'mṛtavapuḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ || 100 ||

padaccheda.iast: kumudaḥ kundaraḥ kundaḥ parjanyaḥ pāvanaḥ anilaḥ amṛta-āśaḥ amṛta-vapuḥ sarva-jñaḥ sarvataḥ-mukhaḥ
padaccheda.deva: कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनः अनिलः अमृत-आशः अमृत-वपुः सर्व-ज्ञः सर्वतः-मुखः

translations.text: (He is) Kumuda, who gladdens the earth by taking away its burden; Kundara, who gives pure fruits (or, as the Boar, rent the earth); Kunda, pure as the jasmine (or Paraśurāma, who gave the earth to Kaśyapa); Parjanya, the rain-cloud (stilling the three sorrows, raining all desires); Pāvana, who purifies by remembrance; Anila, whom none prompts (ever awake, and easily reached by devotees); Amṛtāśa, who tastes the nectar of the Self; Amṛtavapu, whose body knows no death; Sarvajña, all-knowing; Sarvatomukha, with faces on every side.

notes: Śaṅkara: kumudaḥ: he gladdens the earth (ku) by lightening its burden. kundaraḥ: he gives (rā) pure fruits like the kunda flower, or takes them (lā), r and l being one; or, as the Boar wishing to slay Hiraṇyākṣa, he rent (dārayāmāsa) the earth. kundaḥ: his limbs fair as the kunda, clear as crystal; or he gave (adāt) the earth (ku) to Kaśyapa (Harivaṃśa, of Paraśurāma at the horse sacrifice); or he cut down (dyati) the lords of the earth (‘he who made the earth bare of kṣatriyas many times and cut the forest of arms of Kārtavīrya, Bhārgava, may that Hari bring me welfare’, Viṣṇudharma). parjanyaḥ: like the cloud he stills the three sorrows, of the body and the rest, or rains all desires. pāvanaḥ: he purifies by mere remembrance.

Śaṅkara: anilaḥ: ila is one who prompts, or one who sleeps; he is neither, being ever awake; or, from the root of hardness, he is not hard, easily reached by devotees. amṛtāśaḥ: he tastes the nectar of the Self; or he gave the churned nectar to the gods and tastes it himself; or his hopes (āśā) are imperishable. amṛtavapuḥ: his body is free of death. sarvajñaḥ: he knows all (Muṇḍaka 1.1.9). sarvatomukhaḥ: (‘with eyes, heads and faces everywhere’, Gītā 13.13).

sanskrit.deva:
सुलभः सुव्रतः सिद्धः शत्रुजिच्छत्रुतापनः ।
न्यग्रोधोदुम्बरोऽश्वत्थश्चाणूरान्ध्रनिषूदनः ॥ १०१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sulabhaḥ suvrataḥ siddhaḥ śatrujic chatrutāpanaḥ |
nyagrodhodumbaro 'śvatthaś cāṇūrāndhraniṣūdanaḥ || 101 ||

padaccheda.iast: sulabhaḥ su-vrataḥ siddhaḥ śatru-jit śatru-tāpanaḥ nyagrodhaḥ udumbaraḥ aśvatthaḥ cāṇūra-andhra-niṣūdanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सुलभः सु-व्रतः सिद्धः शत्रु-जित् शत्रु-तापनः न्यग्रोधः उदुम्बरः अश्वत्थः चाणूर-अन्ध्र-निषूदनः

translations.text: (He is) Sulabha, easily gained (by a leaf, flower or fruit offered with devotion); Suvrata, who partakes of what is fair (or who turns from food); Siddha, accomplished without dependence; Śatrujit, who conquers the foes of the gods; Śatrutāpana, who scorches them; Nyagrodha, (who stands above all, or covers all beings by his māyā); Udumbara, (risen from the sky as cause, or nourishing the world as food); Aśvattha, (the tree that will not stand till tomorrow); Cāṇūrāndhraniṣūdana, slayer of the Andhra named Cāṇūra.

notes: Śaṅkara: sulabhaḥ: easily gained by leaves, flowers, fruits and the like offered with devotion alone (‘when leaves, flowers, fruits and water are always at hand, free, why do men not strive for liberation toward the ancient Puruṣa, gained by devotion alone?’, Mahābhārata). suvrataḥ: he partakes (vratayati, bhuṅkte) of what is fair; or he turns from eating. siddhaḥ: his being depends on nothing else. śatrujit: the enemies of the gods are his; he conquers them. śatrutāpanaḥ: he scorches them.

Śaṅkara: nyagrodhaḥ: growing down, he stands above all; or, making all beings low, he covers and holds them by his māyā. udumbaraḥ: risen from the sky (ambara) as the cause; or udumbara is food, and as it he nourishes the world (‘the udumbara is strength, food’); in nyagrodhodumbaraḥ the visarga is dropped and the sandhi is of the Vedic kind. aśvatthaḥ: it will not stand (stha) even tomorrow (śvas) (‘this ancient aśvattha with roots above and branches below’, Kaṭha 2.3.1; Gītā 15.1). cāṇūrāndhraniṣūdanaḥ: he slew the Andhra named Cāṇūra.
The text reads nyagrodhodumbaraḥ: nyagrodhaḥ and udumbaraḥ, the visarga dropped, as Śaṅkara notes.

sanskrit.deva:
सहस्रार्चिः सप्तजिह्वः सप्तैधाः सप्तवाहनः ।
अमूर्तिरनघोऽचिन्त्यो भयकृद्भयनाशनः ॥ १०२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sahasrārciḥ saptajihvaḥ saptaidhāḥ saptavāhanaḥ |
amūrtir anagho 'cintyo bhayakṛd bhayanāśanaḥ || 102 ||

padaccheda.iast: sahasra-arciḥ sapta-jihvaḥ sapta-edhāḥ sapta-vāhanaḥ amūrtiḥ anaghaḥ acintyaḥ bhaya-kṛt bhaya-nāśanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सहस्र-अर्चिः सप्त-जिह्वः सप्त-एधाः सप्त-वाहनः अमूर्तिः अनघः अचिन्त्यः भय-कृत् भय-नाशनः

translations.text: (He is) Sahasrārci, of a thousand rays; Saptajihva, (fire) with seven tongues; Saptaidhā, of seven flames; Saptavāhana, drawn by seven horses (the sun); Amūrti, without the solid form of the moving and unmoving (or without limbs); Anagha, without sorrow or sin; Acintya, not to be thought (being the witness of the knower and the means of knowing); Bhayakṛt, who brings fear to those on the wrong path (or cuts the fear of devotees); Bhayanāśana, who destroys the fear of those who keep the dharma of class and stage.

notes: Śaṅkara: sahasrārciḥ: his rays are thousands, endless (‘if the light of a thousand suns rose at once in the sky’, Gītā 11.12). saptajihvaḥ: he has seven tongues (‘Kālī, Karālī … these are the seven tongues’, Muṇḍaka 1.2.4). saptaidhāḥ: fire, whose fuels, or lights, are seven (‘seven are your fuels, O Agni, seven your tongues’, a mantra). saptavāhanaḥ: seven horses draw him; or one horse named Sapta (‘one horse named Seven draws him’, Ṛgveda 1.164.2). amūrtiḥ: mūrti is the solid form able to hold, moving and unmoving (‘from them, brooded over, form was born’); he is without it; or without a body with joined limbs.

Śaṅkara: anaghaḥ: no sorrow or sin is his. acintyaḥ: as the witness of the knower and the rest he is beyond all the means of knowledge; being unlike the whole manifold, he cannot be thought of as ‘such’. bhayakṛt: he makes fear for those on the wrong path, or cuts away (kṛt) the fear of devotees. bhayanāśanaḥ: he destroys the fear of those who keep the conduct of their class and stage (‘by the man of the conduct of class and stage the supreme Viṣṇu is worshipped; there is no other way that pleases him’, Parāśara).

sanskrit.deva:
अणुर्बृहत्कृशः स्थूलो गुणभृन्निर्गुणो महान् ।
अधृतः स्वधृतः स्वास्यः प्राग्वंशो वंशवर्धनः ॥ १०३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aṇur bṛhat kṛśaḥ sthūlo guṇabhṛn nirguṇo mahān |
adhṛtaḥ svadhṛtaḥ svāsyaḥ prāgvaṃśo vaṃśavardhanaḥ || 103 ||

lines.iast: aṇur bṛhat kṛśaḥ sthūlo guṇabhṛn nirguṇo mahān

padaccheda.iast: aṇuḥ bṛhat kṛśaḥ sthūlaḥ guṇa-bhṛt nirguṇaḥ mahān adhṛtaḥ sva-dhṛtaḥ sva-āsyaḥ prāgvaṃśaḥ vaṃśa-vardhanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अणुः बृहत् कृशः स्थूलः गुण-भृत् निर्गुणः महान् अधृतः स्व-धृतः स्व-आस्यः प्राग्वंशः वंश-वर्धनः

translations.text: (He is) Aṇu, most subtle; Bṛhat, vast (Brahman, greater than the great); Kṛśa, thin (not a substance); Sthūla, gross (spoken of so, being the Self of all); Guṇabhṛt, who presides over the guṇas in creation and the rest; Nirguṇa, without guṇas in truth; Mahān, great (beyond all that could bind him); Adhṛta, supported by none; Svadhṛta, supported by himself; Svāsya, whose face is fair (from whose mouth the Veda came forth); Prāgvaṃśa, whose line, the manifold, was first; Vaṃśavardhana, who increases (or cuts) that line.

notes: Śaṅkara: aṇuḥ: of surpassing subtlety (‘this subtle Self is to be known by thought’, Muṇḍaka 3.1.9). bṛhat: Brahman, great and making great (‘greater than the great’, Kaṭha 1.2.20). kṛśaḥ: as the denial of his being a substance (‘not gross’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.8.8). sthūlaḥ: called gross figuratively, being the Self of all. guṇabhṛt: he presides over the work of creation, preservation and dissolution of sattva, rajas and tamas. nirguṇaḥ: in truth having no guṇas (‘alone and without guṇas’, Śvetāśvatara 6.11). mahān: being without sound and the other qualities, most subtle, ever pure and all-pervading, nothing that would limit him can be stated even by reasoning (‘without limbs, soundless, bodiless, touchless, great, pure’, Āpastamba).

Śaṅkara: adhṛtaḥ: he supports even earth and the other supporters, and none supports him. svadhṛtaḥ: by whom then is he held? By himself (‘on what does he rest? On his own greatness’, Chāndogya 7.24.1). svāsyaḥ: his face, red as the inside of a lotus, is most fair; or the great mass of words, the Veda, came forth from his mouth to teach the human ends (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.4.10). prāgvaṃśaḥ: others' lines come after; his line, the manifold, was first. vaṃśavardhanaḥ: he increases that line, or cuts it.

sanskrit.deva:
भारभृत्कथितो योगी योगीशः सर्वकामदः ।
आश्रमः श्रमणः क्षामः सुपर्णो वायुवाहनः ॥ १०४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhārabhṛt kathito yogī yogīśaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ |
āśramaḥ śramaṇaḥ kṣāmaḥ suparṇo vāyuvāhanaḥ || 104 ||

padaccheda.iast: bhāra-bhṛt kathitaḥ yogī yogi-īśaḥ sarva-kāma-daḥ āśramaḥ śramaṇaḥ kṣāmaḥ suparṇaḥ vāyu-vāhanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: भार-भृत् कथितः योगी योगि-ईशः सर्व-काम-दः आश्रमः श्रमणः क्षामः सुपर्णः वायु-वाहनः

translations.text: (He is) Bhārabhṛt, who as Ananta bears the burden of the earth; Kathita, the one declared (supreme by all the Vedas); Yogī, reached by knowledge (or ever absorbed in himself); Yogīśa, lord of yogins, unhindered; Sarvakāmada, who gives all desires; Āśrama, the resting-place of all who wander in the forest of the round; Śramaṇa, who afflicts the undiscerning; Kṣāma, who makes all creatures waste; Suparṇa, (the tree of the round) whose fair leaves are the Vedas; Vāyuvāhana, from fear of whom the wind carries beings.

notes: Śaṅkara: bhārabhṛt: as Ananta and the rest he bears the burden of the earth. kathitaḥ: he alone is declared supreme by the Vedas and the rest; or declared by all the Vedas (‘the word which all the Vedas declare’, Kaṭha 1.2.15; ‘by all the Vedas I alone am to be known’, Gītā 15.15; ‘in the Veda, the Rāmāyaṇa and the Bhārata Viṣṇu is sung everywhere’); the Kaṭha, having said ‘he reaches the end of the road, the highest abode of Viṣṇu’, declares him as higher than the senses and all the rest, up to ‘beyond Puruṣa there is nothing; that is the end, the highest goal’ (1.3.9–11). yogī: yoga is knowledge, and he is reached by it alone; or yoga is absorption, and he ever holds himself absorbed in himself. yogīśaḥ: other yogins are struck by obstacles and fall from their state; he, free of them, is their lord. sarvakāmadaḥ: he always gives all desires (Brahmasūtra 3.2.38).

Śaṅkara: āśramaḥ: like a hermitage, he is the resting-place of all who wander in the forest of the round. śramaṇaḥ: he torments all the undiscerning. kṣāmaḥ: he makes all creatures waste away. suparṇaḥ: the tree of the round, whose fair leaves are the Vedas (‘whose leaves are the Vedas’, Gītā 15.1). vāyuvāhanaḥ: from fear of him the wind carries beings (‘from fear of him the wind blows’, Taittirīya 2.8).

sanskrit.deva:
धनुर्धरो धनुर्वेदो दण्डो दमयिता दमः ।
अपराजितः सर्वसहो नियन्ता नियमोऽयमः ॥ १०५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
dhanurdharo dhanurvedo daṇḍo damayitā damaḥ |
aparājitaḥ sarvasaho niyantā niyamo 'yamaḥ || 105 ||

padaccheda.iast: dhanuḥ-dharaḥ dhanuḥ-vedaḥ daṇḍaḥ damayitā damaḥ aparājitaḥ sarva-sahaḥ niyantā niyamaḥ ayamaḥ
padaccheda.deva: धनुः-धरः धनुः-वेदः दण्डः दमयिता दमः अपराजितः सर्व-सहः नियन्ता नियमः अयमः

translations.text: (He is) Dhanurdhara, (Rāma) who held the great bow; Dhanurveda, who knows the science of the bow; Daṇḍa, the rod of those who subdue; Damayitā, who subdues creatures (as Yama and as kings); Dama, the restraint (the fruit of the rod); Aparājita, never defeated; Sarvasaha, able in every work (or bearing all foes); Niyantā, who sets all in their places; Aniyama, (having no ruler over him); Ayama, to whom death does not come.

notes: Śaṅkara: dhanurdharaḥ: the glorious Rāma, who held the great bow. dhanurvedaḥ: that same son of Daśaratha knows the science of the bow. daṇḍaḥ: the rod of those who subdue (‘of subduers I am the rod’, Gītā 10.38). damayitā: as Vaivasvata (Yama), kings and the rest he subdues creatures. damaḥ: restraint, the fruit of the rod in those to be subdued, is also he. aparājitaḥ: not defeated by enemies. sarvasahaḥ: able in all works, or he bears all foes. niyantā: he sets all in their own duties.

Śaṅkara: aniyamaḥ: there is no rule over him, since there is no other controller of the controller of all. ayamaḥ: yama, death, is not his. Or yama and niyama are the limbs of yoga; being reached by them, he is niyama and yama.
The edition prints niyantā niyamo 'yamaḥ; Śaṅkara reads first aniyamaḥ and ayamaḥ, then niyamaḥ and yamaḥ. The word-by-word follows the print.

sanskrit.deva:
सत्त्ववान्सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्यधर्मपरायणः ।
अभिप्रायः प्रियार्होऽर्हः प्रियकृत्प्रीतिवर्धनः ॥ १०६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sattvavān sāttvikaḥ satyaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ |
abhiprāyaḥ priyārho 'rhaḥ priyakṛt prītivardhanaḥ || 106 ||

padaccheda.iast: sattvavān sāttvikaḥ satyaḥ satya-dharma-parāyaṇaḥ abhiprāyaḥ priya-arhaḥ arhaḥ priya-kṛt prīti-vardhanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सत्त्ववान् सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्य-धर्म-परायणः अभिप्रायः प्रिय-अर्हः अर्हः प्रिय-कृत् प्रीति-वर्धनः

translations.text: (He is) Sattvavān, of courage, valour and the like; Sāttvika, abiding chiefly in sattva; Satya, good among the good; Satyadharmaparāyaṇa, intent on truth (saying things as they are) and on enjoined dharma; Abhiprāya, the aim sought by seekers of the human ends (to whom the world goes at dissolution); Priyārha, worthy of what is dearest; Arha, worthy of worship (with welcome, seat, praise, water and homage); Priyakṛt, who does what is dear to those who worship him; Prītivardhana, who increases their love.

notes: Śaṅkara: sattvavān: his are courage, valour and the like (sattva). sāttvikaḥ: abiding chiefly in the guṇa sattva. satyaḥ: being good among the good. satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ: fixed on truth, the telling of things as they are, and on dharma known by injunction. abhiprāyaḥ: those who seek the human ends aim at him; or the world goes toward him at dissolution. priyārhaḥ: worthy of what is dear (‘whatever is most loved in the world, and dear in one's house, should be given to one of virtue, wishing it to be imperishable’). arhaḥ: to be worshipped with welcome, seat, praise, offering of water, foot-water, hymns, bowing and the other means of worship. priyakṛt: not only dear, he does what is dear to those who worship him with praise and the rest. prītivardhanaḥ: he increases their love.

sanskrit.deva:
विहायसगतिर्ज्योतिः सुरुचिर्हुतभुग्विभुः ।
रविर्विरोचनः सूर्यः सविता रविलोचनः ॥ १०७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vihāyasagatir jyotiḥ surucir hutabhug vibhuḥ |
ravir virocanaḥ sūryaḥ savitā ravilocanaḥ || 107 ||

padaccheda.iast: vihāyasa-gatiḥ jyotiḥ su-ruciḥ huta-bhuk vibhuḥ raviḥ virocanaḥ sūryaḥ savitā ravi-locanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: विहायस-गतिः ज्योतिः सु-रुचिः हुत-भुक् विभुः रविः विरोचनः सूर्यः सविता रवि-लोचनः

translations.text: (He is) Vihāyasagati, whose seat is the sky (the step of Viṣṇu, or the sun); Jyoti, light of itself; Suruci, of fair light (or fair will); Hutabhuk, who eats the oblation (offered to any god); Vibhu, everywhere (lord of the three worlds); Ravi, (the sun who takes up the juices); Virocana, shining in many ways; Sūrya, (who brings forth); Savitā, the begetter of the world; Ravilocana, whose eye is the sun.

notes: Śaṅkara: vihāyasagatiḥ: the sky is his seat: the step of Viṣṇu, or the sun. jyotiḥ: he shines of himself (‘Nārāyaṇa, the supreme light’). suruciḥ: his light, or his will, is fair. hutabhuk: he eats the oblation even in rites offered to all the gods; or he protects (bhunakti) it. vibhuḥ: being everywhere; or lord of the three worlds. raviḥ: the sun, who takes up (ā-dā) the juices (rasa). virocanaḥ: he shines variously. sūryaḥ: from sū, to bring forth or impel (Pāṇini 3.1.114). savitā: he begets the whole world (‘from taking up the juices he is called Ravi; from begetting creatures, Savitṛ’, Viṣṇudharmottara). ravilocanaḥ: the sun is his eye (‘fire is his head, the moon and sun his eyes’, Muṇḍaka 2.1.4).

sanskrit.deva:
अनन्तो हुतभुग्भोक्ता सुखदो नैकजोऽग्रजः ।
अनिर्विण्णः सदामर्षी लोकाधिष्ठानमद्भुतः ॥ १०८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ananto hutabhug bhoktā sukhado naikajo 'grajaḥ |
anirviṇṇaḥ sadāmarṣī lokādhiṣṭhānam adbhutaḥ || 108 ||

padaccheda.iast: anantaḥ huta-bhuk bhoktā sukha-daḥ naika-jaḥ agra-jaḥ anirviṇṇaḥ sadā-marṣī loka-adhiṣṭhānam adbhutaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अनन्तः हुत-भुक् भोक्ता सुख-दः नैक-जः अग्र-जः अनिर्विण्णः सदा-मर्षी लोक-अधिष्ठानम् अद्भुतः

translations.text: (He is) Ananta, endless (eternal, everywhere, or Śeṣa); Hutabhuk, who eats the oblation; Bhoktā, who enjoys Prakṛti (or protects the world); Sukhada, who gives devotees the happiness of liberation (or, read Asukhada, who cuts off unhappiness); Naikaja, born many times to guard dharma; Agraja, born first (Hiraṇyagarbha); Anirviṇṇa, never weary; Sadāmarṣī, ever forbearing toward the good; Lokādhiṣṭhāna, the ground on which the three worlds stand; Adbhuta, the wonder.

notes: Śaṅkara: anantaḥ: being eternal and everywhere, without bounds of place or time; or in the form of Śeṣa. hutabhuk: he eats the oblation. bhoktā: he enjoys Prakṛti, unconscious, the thing to be enjoyed; or protects the world. sukhadaḥ: he gives devotees happiness, liberation; or, read asukhadaḥ (bhoktā asukhadaḥ), he cuts off (do) unhappiness (asukha). naikajaḥ: born again and again to guard dharma. agrajaḥ: born first, Hiraṇyagarbha (‘Hiraṇyagarbha arose first’). anirviṇṇaḥ: having all his desires and no cause for want, he knows no weariness. sadāmarṣī: he always bears with the good. lokādhiṣṭhānam: Brahman, itself without support, on which as ground the three worlds stand. adbhutaḥ: being a wonder (‘he whom many cannot even hear of, whom many hearing do not know; wonderful is the teller, skilled the one who gains him’, Kaṭha 1.2.7; ‘one sees him as a wonder’, Gītā 2.29); or wondrous in nature, power, act and effect.

sanskrit.deva:
सनात्सनातनतमः कपिलः कपिरप्ययः ।
स्वस्तिदः स्वस्तिकृत्स्वस्ति स्वस्तिभुक्स्वस्तिदक्षिणः ॥ १०९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sanāt sanātanatamaḥ kapilaḥ kapir apyayaḥ |
svastidaḥ svastikṛt svasti svastibhuk svastidakṣiṇaḥ || 109 ||

padaccheda.iast: sanāt sanātana-tamaḥ kapilaḥ kapiḥ apyayaḥ svasti-daḥ svasti-kṛt svasti svasti-bhuk svasti-dakṣiṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सनात् सनातन-तमः कपिलः कपिः अप्ययः स्वस्ति-दः स्वस्ति-कृत् स्वस्ति स्वस्ति-भुक् स्वस्ति-दक्षिणः

translations.text: (He is) Sanāt, time (from of old, an imagining of the supreme); Sanātanatama, most ancient of the ancient (Viriñci and the others); Kapila, the tawny (submarine fire); Kapi, the sun who drinks the waters (or the Boar); Apyaya, into whom the worlds dissolve; Svastida, who gives welfare to devotees; Svastikṛt, who makes it; Svasti, welfare itself (his own nature, supreme bliss); Svastibhuk, who enjoys it (or protects the welfare of devotees); Svastidakṣiṇa, quick and able to give welfare.

notes: Śaṅkara: sanāt: an indeclinable meaning ‘long since’; time too is a construction of the supreme (‘the first form of the supreme Brahman is Puruṣa; the manifest and unmanifest are others; and Time another’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). sanātanatamaḥ: being the cause of all, more ancient than Viriñci and the other ancient ones. kapilaḥ: the colour of the submarine fire is tawny; he is that form. kapiḥ: ka is water; the sun drinks (pā) it with his rays; or the Boar (‘kapi is the Boar and best’). apyayaḥ: at dissolution the worlds go into him. Here the ninth hundred names are explained.

Śaṅkara: svastidaḥ: he gives welfare to devotees. svastikṛt: he makes it. svasti: his own nature, auspicious, supreme bliss. svastibhuk: he enjoys it; or he protects (bhunakti) the welfare of devotees. svastidakṣiṇaḥ: he grows as welfare, or is able to give it; or dakṣiṇa means quick: he alone can give welfare at once, at whose remembrance all accomplishments are gained (‘remembering him, the vessel of all good arises in a man; I go for refuge to Hari, unborn, eternal’; ‘by remembering Kṛṣṇa the cage of the mass of sins breaks a hundredfold, like a mountain struck by the thunderbolt’).

sanskrit.deva:
अरौद्रः कुण्डली चक्री विक्रम्यूर्जितशासनः ।
शब्दातिगः शब्दसहः शिशिरः शर्वरीकरः ॥ ११० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
araudraḥ kuṇḍalī cakrī vikramy ūrjitaśāsanaḥ |
śabdātigaḥ śabdasahaḥ śiśiraḥ śarvarīkaraḥ || 110 ||

padaccheda.iast: araudraḥ kuṇḍalī cakrī vikramī ūrjita-śāsanaḥ śabda-atigaḥ śabda-sahaḥ śiśiraḥ śarvarī-karaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अरौद्रः कुण्डली चक्री विक्रमी ऊर्जित-शासनः शब्द-अतिगः शब्द-सहः शिशिरः शर्वरी-करः

translations.text: (He is) Araudra, in whom there is nothing fierce (no passion, anger or harshness); Kuṇḍalī, (Śeṣa, or wearing earrings like the sun's orb, or the makara-shaped Sāṃkhya and Yoga); Cakrī, who holds the discus Sudarśana (the mind) to protect the worlds; Vikramī, whose stride and valour are unlike others'; Ūrjitaśāsana, whose command (śruti and smṛti) is mighty; Śabdātiga, beyond the reach of words; Śabdasaha, whom all the Vedas declare; Śiśira, the cool resting-place of those burnt by the three sorrows; Śarvarīkara, who makes night (the round for the knower, the Self for the bound).

notes: Śaṅkara: araudraḥ: action is fierce, passion is fierce, anger is fierce; having all his desires, he has no passion, aversion or the like, so nothing fierce. kuṇḍalī: in the form of Śeṣa; or wearing earrings like the orb of the sun; or Sāṃkhya and Yoga, makara-shaped, are his earrings. cakrī: for the protection of all the worlds he holds the discus Sudarśana, which is the principle of mind (‘Viṣṇu holds in his hand the mind in the form of the discus, moving, swifter than the wind’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). vikramī: his stride, or valour, is unlike that of all others. ūrjitaśāsanaḥ: his command, śruti and smṛti, is mighty (‘śruti and smṛti are my commands; he who transgresses them breaks my command and hates me; though my devotee, he is no Vaiṣṇava’, the Lord).

Śaṅkara: śabdātigaḥ: since genus and the other grounds for words are not in him, words cannot speak of him (‘from which words turn back with the mind, not reaching it’, Taittirīya 2.4). śabdasahaḥ: all the Vedas speak of him in their purport (Kaṭha 1.2.15; Gītā 15.15). śiśiraḥ: the resting-place of those burnt by the three sorrows. śarvarīkaraḥ: for those in the round the Self is as night, for the knowers the round is night; he makes both (‘what is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled is awake; where beings are awake, that is night for the seeing sage’, Gītā 2.69).

sanskrit.deva:
अक्रूरः पेशलो दक्षो दक्षिणः क्षमिणां वरः ।
विद्वत्तमो वीतभयः पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः ॥ १११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
akrūraḥ peśalo dakṣo dakṣiṇaḥ kṣamiṇāṃ varaḥ |
vidvattamo vītabhayaḥ puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ || 111 ||

lines.iast: akrūraḥ peśalo dakṣo dakṣiṇaḥ kṣamiṇāṃ varaḥ
lines.deva: अक्रूरः पेशलो दक्षो दक्षिणः क्षमिणां वरः

padaccheda.iast: akrūraḥ peśalaḥ dakṣaḥ dakṣiṇaḥ kṣamiṇām varaḥ vidvat-tamaḥ vīta-bhayaḥ puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अक्रूरः पेशलः दक्षः दक्षिणः क्षमिणाम् वरः विद्वत्-तमः वीत-भयः पुण्य-श्रवण-कीर्तनः

words.meaning: to hear and sing of whom is holy

translations.text: (He is) Akrūra, without cruelty (having no unfulfilled desire, no anger); Peśala, graceful in deed, mind, speech and body; Dakṣa, grown, able and swift; Dakṣiṇa, (able; or who goes and strikes); the best of the patient (and of those who bear burdens, and of the able); Vidvattama, wisest (knowing all, always); Vītabhaya, from whom the fear of the round has gone; Puṇyaśravaṇakīrtana, to hear and sing of whom brings merit.

notes: Śaṅkara: akrūraḥ: cruelty is a quality of mind, an inner burning with rage born of anger; having all his desires, he has no unfulfilled desire and so no anger, and no cruelty. peśalaḥ: being fair in deed, mind, speech and body. dakṣaḥ: grown, able and quick: all three are fixed in the supreme. dakṣiṇaḥ: has the same sense, with no fault of repetition since the word differs; or from dakṣ, ‘to go’ and ‘to harm’. kṣamiṇāṃ varaḥ: best of the patient, the yogins, and of the earth and the others that bear burdens (‘like the earth in patience’, Vālmīki); bearing the whole egg of Brahmā, he is not weighed down, better even than the earth; or the kṣamins are the able, and he, having all powers, is able in all acts. vidvattamaḥ: knowledge unsurpassed, always, of all things, is his, not others'. vītabhayaḥ: the fear belonging to the round, or the round itself, has gone from him, as he is lord of all and ever free. puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ: to hear and to tell of him brings merit (as the phalaśruti will say: ‘he who hears this daily and he who tells it meets with nothing ill, here or hereafter’, verse 121).

sanskrit.deva:
उत्तारणो दुष्कृतिहा पुण्यो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः ।
वीरहा रक्षणः सन्तो जीवनः पर्यवस्थितः ॥ ११२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
uttāraṇo duṣkṛtihā puṇyo duḥsvapnanāśanaḥ |
vīrahā rakṣaṇaḥ santo jīvanaḥ paryavasthitaḥ || 112 ||

padaccheda.iast: uttāraṇaḥ duṣkṛti-hā puṇyaḥ duḥsvapna-nāśanaḥ vīra-hā rakṣaṇaḥ santaḥ jīvanaḥ paryavasthitaḥ
padaccheda.deva: उत्तारणः दुष्कृति-हा पुण्यः दुःस्वप्न-नाशनः वीर-हा रक्षणः सन्तः जीवनः पर्यवस्थितः

translations.text: (He is) Uttāraṇa, who carries across the ocean of the round; Duṣkṛtihā, who destroys sins (and sinners); Puṇya, who makes merit (or teaches it by śruti and smṛti); Duḥsvapnanāśana, who destroys the bad dreams that foretell ill; Vīrahā, who ends the wanderings (vi-ira) of beings by giving liberation; Rakṣaṇa, who protects the three worlds through sattva; Santa, (the good, as whom he grows learning and humility); Jīvana, who as breath makes all creatures live; Paryavasthita, who stands pervading the universe on every side.

notes: Śaṅkara: uttāraṇaḥ: he carries across from the ocean of the round. duṣkṛtihā: he destroys the misdeeds called sins, or those who do them. puṇyaḥ: he makes merit for all who remember him; or by the words of śruti and smṛti he tells all of merit. duḥsvapnanāśanaḥ: meditated on, praised, named and worshipped, he destroys the bad dreams that foretell coming ill. vīrahā: by giving liberation he ends the various goings of those in the round. rakṣaṇaḥ: presiding over sattva, he protects the three worlds (agent suffix by Pāṇini 3.1.134). santaḥ: those who walk the good path; in their form he grows knowledge and humility. jīvanaḥ: as breath he makes all creatures live. paryavasthitaḥ: he stands pervading the universe on every side.

sanskrit.deva:
अनन्तरूपोऽनन्तश्रीर्जितमन्युर्भयापहः ।
चतुरश्रो गभीरात्मा विदिशो व्यादिशो दिशः ॥ ११३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anantarūpo 'nantaśrīr jitamanyur bhayāpahaḥ |
caturaśro gabhīrātmā vidiśo vyādiśo diśaḥ || 113 ||

padaccheda.iast: ananta-rūpaḥ ananta-śrīḥ jita-manyuḥ bhaya-apahaḥ catur-aśraḥ gabhīra-ātmā vidiśaḥ vyādiśaḥ diśaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अनन्त-रूपः अनन्त-श्रीः जित-मन्युः भय-अपहः चतुर्-अश्रः गभीर-आत्मा विदिशः व्यादिशः दिशः

translations.text: (He is) Anantarūpa, of endless forms (as the manifold); Anantaśrī, of unmeasured power; Jitamanyu, who has conquered anger; Bhayāpaha, who removes men's fear of the round; Caturaśra, just (giving each the fruit of his deeds); Gabhīrātmā, whose nature and mind none can fathom; Vidiśa, who distributes the various fruits; Vyādiśa, who gives Śakra and the others their various commands; Diśa, who as the Veda points out the fruits of all acts.

notes: Śaṅkara: anantarūpaḥ: as the manifold of the universe his forms are endless. anantaśrīḥ: his power (śrī), the supreme śakti, is unmeasured (‘his supreme power is heard of as manifold’, Śvetāśvatara 6.8). jitamanyuḥ: he has conquered anger. bhayāpahaḥ: he removes men's fear born of the round. caturaśraḥ: just, for he gives men the fruit that fits their acts. gabhīrātmā: his nature, or mind, is deep, not to be measured. vidiśaḥ: he gives those entitled their various fruits. vyādiśaḥ: he gives Śakra and the others their various commands. diśaḥ: as the Veda he points out the fruits of all acts.

sanskrit.deva:
अनादिर्भूर्भुवो लक्ष्मीः सुवीरो रुचिराङ्गदः ।
जननो जनजन्मादिर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः ॥ ११४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anādir bhūrbhuvo lakṣmīḥ suvīro rucirāṅgadaḥ |
janano janajanmādir bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ || 114 ||

padaccheda.iast: anādiḥ bhūḥ-bhuvaḥ lakṣmīḥ su-vīraḥ rucira-aṅgadaḥ jananaḥ jana-janma-ādiḥ bhīmaḥ bhīma-parākramaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अनादिः भूः-भुवः लक्ष्मीः सु-वीरः रुचिर-अङ्गदः जननः जन-जन्म-आदिः भीमः भीम-पराक्रमः

words.meaning: root of the birth of creatures

translations.text: (He is) Anādi, without beginning, being the cause of all; Bhūrbhuva, the support (bhūḥ) of the earth (bhuvaḥ); Lakṣmī, (its) splendour (or the knowledge of the Self); Suvīra, whose goings are fair and many; Rucirāṅgada, with lovely armlets; Janana, who begets creatures; Janajanmādi, the root cause of the birth of creatures; Bhīma, the cause of fear; Bhīmaparākrama, whose valour in his appearances is the cause of fear to the asuras.

notes: Śaṅkara: anādiḥ: no cause (ādi) is his, being the cause of all. bhūrbhuvaḥ: bhūḥ, the support, of bhuvaḥ, the earth, known as the support of all beings: the support even of the earth. Or: not only is he the support of the earth, he is its splendour (lakṣmī), bhuvo lakṣmīḥ; or bhūḥ is this world, bhuvaḥ the world Bhuvar (the mid-region), and lakṣmī the knowledge of the Self (‘you, goddess, are the knowledge of the Self’, Śrīstuti); or he is the splendour of earth and mid-region. suvīraḥ: his goings (īra) are fair and many; or he moves in many fair ways. rucirāṅgadaḥ: his armlets are lovely and auspicious. jananaḥ: he begets creatures. janajanmādiḥ: the root cause of the birth of those who are born. bhīmaḥ: as the cause of fear (Pāṇini 3.4.74; ‘a great fear, a raised thunderbolt’, Kaṭha 2.3.2). bhīmaparākramaḥ: in his appearances his valour is the cause of fear to the asuras and others.
The text reads anādir bhūrbhuvo lakṣmīḥ; Śaṅkara divides it in more than one way, as given.

sanskrit.deva:
आधारनिलयोऽधाता पुष्पहासः प्रजागरः ।
ऊर्ध्वगः सत्पथाचारः प्राणदः प्रणवः पणः ॥ ११५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ādhāranilayo 'dhātā puṣpahāsaḥ prajāgaraḥ |
ūrdhvagaḥ satpathācāraḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ paṇaḥ || 115 ||

padaccheda.iast: ādhāra-nilayaḥ adhātā puṣpa-hāsaḥ prajāgaraḥ ūrdhva-gaḥ sat-patha-ācāraḥ prāṇa-daḥ praṇavaḥ paṇaḥ
padaccheda.deva: आधार-निलयः अधाता पुष्प-हासः प्रजागरः ऊर्ध्व-गः सत्-पथ-आचारः प्राण-दः प्रणवः पणः

translations.text: (He is) Ādhāranilaya, the support of the five elements that support all; Adhātā, whom none supports (or who drinks up all creatures at dissolution); Puṣpahāsa, who opens out as the manifold like a bud into a flower; Prajāgara, ever awake; Ūrdhvaga, standing above all; Satpathācāra, who does the deeds of the good; Prāṇada, who gives life to Parīkṣit and others who were dead; Praṇava, (Om, the name of the supreme, one with him); Paṇa, who deals (making names and forms, and giving the fruits of deeds).

notes: Śaṅkara: ādhāranilayaḥ: the support of the five elements, earth and the rest, which are the supports. adhātā: there is no other supporter of him who holds himself; or at dissolution he drinks (dhe) all creatures. puṣpahāsaḥ: as the buds of flowers open out, so he opens out as the manifold. prajāgaraḥ: being ever awake by nature. ūrdhvagaḥ: he stands above all. satpathācāraḥ: the deeds of the good are good paths; he does them. prāṇadaḥ: he made the dead live, Parīkṣit and others. praṇavaḥ: Om, the name of the supreme Self; he is called so by the figure of non-difference. paṇaḥ: paṇ means dealing; he does it (‘the wise one, making all forms and giving them names, goes on speaking’, Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 3.12.7); or, gathering all meritorious acts as a price, he gives their fruit to those entitled.

sanskrit.deva:
प्रमाणं प्राणनिलयः प्राणभृत्प्राणजीवनः ।
तत्त्वं तत्त्वविदेकात्मा जन्ममृत्युजरातिगः ॥ ११६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pramāṇaṃ prāṇanilayaḥ prāṇabhṛt prāṇajīvanaḥ |
tattvaṃ tattvavid ekātmā janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ || 116 ||

padaccheda.iast: pramāṇam prāṇa-nilayaḥ prāṇa-bhṛt prāṇa-jīvanaḥ tattvam tattva-vit eka-ātmā janma-mṛtyu-jarā-atigaḥ
padaccheda.deva: प्रमाणम् प्राण-निलयः प्राण-भृत् प्राण-जीवनः तत्त्वम् तत्त्व-वित् एक-आत्मा जन्म-मृत्यु-जरा-अतिगः

words.meaning: who makes beings live by the breaths

translations.text: (He is) Pramāṇa, knowing itself, self-luminous consciousness; Prāṇanilaya, in whom the senses and breaths, and the jīvas, come to rest; Prāṇabhṛt, who as food nourishes the breaths; Prāṇajīvana, who makes creatures live by the breaths; Tattva, the truth; Tattvavit, who knows his own nature as it is; Ekātmā, the one Self; Janmamṛtyujarātiga, who has gone beyond birth, death, old age and the other changes.

notes: Śaṅkara: pramāṇam: knowing, consciousness, self-luminous (‘Brahman is consciousness’, Aitareya 3.1.3; ‘in truth knowledge, wholly pure, which through error of sight stands as things’, Viṣṇu Purāṇa). prāṇanilayaḥ: the senses are brought into the jīva, depending on it, or the breaths that hold the body rest in it; or the jīva, which breathes, dissolves in the supreme Puruṣa; or he withdraws breaths and jīvas. prāṇabhṛt: as food he nourishes the breaths. prāṇajīvanaḥ: by the winds called breaths he makes creatures live (‘no mortal lives by prāṇa or apāna; they live by another on whom these two rest’, Kaṭha 2.2.5). tattvam: tattva, tathya, amṛta, satya, paramārtha: words of one sense naming Brahman, the highest reality. tattvavit: he knows his own nature as it is. ekātmā: one and the Self (‘the Self alone was this in the beginning’, Aitareya 1.1.1; ‘because it reaches, takes, eats the objects here, and its being is unbroken, it is called ātman’). janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ: he goes beyond the six changes, ‘is born, exists, grows, changes, wanes, perishes’ (‘the wise one is not born, nor dies’, Kaṭha 1.2.18).

sanskrit.deva:
भूर्भुवःस्वस्तरुस्तारः सविता प्रपितामहः ।
यज्ञो यज्ञपतिर्यज्वा यज्ञाङ्गो यज्ञवाहनः ॥ ११७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bhūrbhuvaḥsvastarus tāraḥ savitā prapitāmahaḥ |
yajño yajñapatir yajvā yajñāṅgo yajñavāhanaḥ || 117 ||

padaccheda.iast: bhūḥ-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ-taruḥ tāraḥ savitā prapitāmahaḥ yajñaḥ yajña-patiḥ yajvā yajña-aṅgaḥ yajña-vāhanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: भूः-भुवः-स्वः-तरुः तारः सविता प्रपितामहः यज्ञः यज्ञ-पतिः यज्वा यज्ञ-अङ्गः यज्ञ-वाहनः

words.meaning: tree of bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ and svaḥ

translations.text: (He is) Bhūrbhuvaḥsvastaru, who by the three utterances bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ, the essence of the three Vedas, carries the three worlds across (or the tree of the three worlds); Tāra, who carries across the ocean of the round (or Om); Savitā, the father of the whole world; Prapitāmaha, the father even of Brahmā the grandfather; Yajña, (who goes with all); Yajñapati, protector and lord of sacrifices; Yajvā, (standing) as the sacrificer; Yajñāṅga, (the Boar) whose limbs are sacrifices; Yajñavāhana, who carries the sacrifices that bring fruit.

notes: Śaṅkara: bhūrbhuvaḥsvastaruḥ: the Ṛgvedins call the three utterances bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ bright, the essence of the three Vedas; by offering with them he carries (tarati) the three worlds across, or makes them flow (‘the oblation duly cast in fire reaches the sun; from the sun comes rain, from rain food, from that creatures’, Manu 3.76); or he is the tree (taru) of the round of the three worlds; or he stands pervading the three worlds like a tree. tāraḥ: he carries across the ocean of the round; or Om. savitā: the father of the whole world. prapitāmahaḥ: the father even of the grandfather, Brahmā. yajñaḥ: who goes with (saṃgantṛ). yajñapatiḥ: protector or lord of sacrifices (‘I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices’, Gītā 9.24). yajvā: standing as the sacrificer. yajñāṅgaḥ: the Boar form, whose limbs are sacrifices (the Harivaṃśa verses: Veda his feet, the post his tusk, the rite his hands, the fire his tongue, the darbha his hair …). yajñavāhanaḥ: he carries the sacrifices that cause the fruit.

sanskrit.deva:
यज्ञभृद्यज्ञकृद्यज्ञी यज्ञभुग्यज्ञसाधनः ।
यज्ञान्तकृद्यज्ञगुह्यमन्नमन्नाद एव च ॥ ११८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yajñabhṛd yajñakṛd yajñī yajñabhug yajñasādhanaḥ |
yajñāntakṛd yajñaguhyam annam annāda eva ca || 118 ||

lines.iast: yajñāntakṛd yajñaguhyam annam annāda eva ca

padaccheda.iast: yajña-bhṛt yajña-kṛt yajñī yajña-bhuk yajña-sādhanaḥ yajña-anta-kṛt yajña-guhyam annam anna-adaḥ eva ca
padaccheda.deva: यज्ञ-भृत् यज्ञ-कृत् यज्ञी यज्ञ-भुक् यज्ञ-साधनः यज्ञ-अन्त-कृत् यज्ञ-गुह्यम् अन्नम् अन्न-अदः एव च

words.meaning: who brings sacrifice to its end

translations.text: (He is) Yajñabhṛt, who bears or guards the sacrifice; Yajñakṛt, who makes it at the world's beginning (and cuts it at the end); Yajñī, the principal, whom the sacrifices worship; Yajñabhuk, who enjoys or protects it; Yajñasādhana, reached by sacrifices; Yajñāntakṛt, who brings it to its end, the fruit; Yajñaguhya, the secret of sacrifice (the sacrifice of knowledge, Brahman); Anna, food; and Annāda, the eater of food.

notes: Śaṅkara: yajñabhṛt: he bears or protects the sacrifice. yajñakṛt: at the beginning of the world he makes the sacrifice, and at its end cuts it off. yajñī: he is the principal of the sacrifices, which are his worship. yajñabhuk: he enjoys it, or protects it. yajñasādhanaḥ: sacrifices are the means of reaching him. yajñāntakṛt: he makes the end of the sacrifice, the gaining of its fruit; or by the Vaiṣṇava verse and the full oblation he completes it. yajñaguhyam: the secret of sacrifices is the sacrifice of knowledge, or sacrifice without aim at the fruit; by non-difference, Brahman. annam: it is eaten, and it eats beings. annādaḥ: he eats food. eva shows that the whole world, as food and eater, is only enjoyer and enjoyed; ca, that all the names are to be taken together as resting in the one supreme Puruṣa.

sanskrit.deva:
आत्मयोनिः स्वयंजातो वैखानः सामगायनः ।
देवकीनन्दनः स्रष्टा क्षितीशः पापनाशनः ॥ ११९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ātmayoniḥ svayaṃjāto vaikhānaḥ sāmagāyanaḥ |
devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭā kṣitīśaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ || 119 ||

padaccheda.iast: ātma-yoniḥ svayam-jātaḥ vaikhānaḥ sāma-gāyanaḥ devakī-nandanaḥ sraṣṭā kṣiti-īśaḥ pāpa-nāśanaḥ
padaccheda.deva: आत्म-योनिः स्वयम्-जातः वैखानः साम-गायनः देवकी-नन्दनः स्रष्टा क्षिति-ईशः पाप-नाशनः

translations.text: (He is) Ātmayoni, himself the material cause and no other; Svayaṃjāta, himself the efficient cause too; Vaikhāna, (the Boar) who dug through the earth to slay Hiraṇyākṣa; Sāmagāyana, who sings the Sāmans; Devakīnandana, the son of Devakī; Sraṣṭā, the creator of all the worlds; Kṣitīśa, Lord of the earth (the son of Daśaratha); Pāpanāśana, who destroys sins when named, worshipped, meditated on and remembered.

notes: Śaṅkara: ātmayoniḥ: he himself is the source, the material cause, and nothing else. svayaṃjātaḥ: to show that he is also the efficient cause; that Hari is both causes is established in ‘Prakṛti too, so as not to contradict the proposition and the example’ (Brahmasūtra 1.4.23). vaikhānaḥ: from digging in a special way; taking the form of the Boar he dug through the earth and slew Hiraṇyākṣa who dwelt in the nether world, as the Purāṇas tell. sāmagāyanaḥ: he sings the Sāmans. devakīnandanaḥ: the son of Devakī (‘the bright lights in the world, the three worlds, the three guardians of the worlds, the three fires and the five oblations, all the gods are the son of Devakī’, Mahābhārata). sraṣṭā: the creator of all the worlds. kṣitīśaḥ: lord of the earth, the son of Daśaratha. pāpanāśanaḥ: named, worshipped, meditated on and remembered, he destroys the mass of sins (‘the sin a man destroys by a fortnight's fast, he destroys by a hundred restraints of breath; what a thousand restraints of breath destroy, the meditation of Hari destroys in a moment’, Vṛddha Śātātapa).

sanskrit.deva:
शङ्खभृन्नन्दकी चक्री शार्ङ्गधन्वा गदाधरः ।
रथाङ्गपाणिरक्षोभ्यः सर्वप्रहरणायुधः ।
सर्वप्रहरणायुध ॐ नमः ॥ १२० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śaṅkhabhṛn nandakī cakrī śārṅgadhanvā gadādharaḥ |
rathāṅgapāṇir akṣobhyaḥ sarvapraharaṇāyudhaḥ |
sarvapraharaṇāyudha oṃ namaḥ || 120 ||

padaccheda.iast: śaṅkha-bhṛt nandakī cakrī śārṅga-dhanvā gadā-dharaḥ rathāṅga-pāṇiḥ akṣobhyaḥ sarva-praharaṇa-āyudhaḥ sarva-praharaṇa-āyudhaḥ om namaḥ
padaccheda.deva: शङ्ख-भृत् नन्दकी चक्री शार्ङ्ग-धन्वा गदा-धरः रथाङ्ग-पाणिः अक्षोभ्यः सर्व-प्रहरण-आयुधः सर्व-प्रहरण-आयुधः ॐ नमः

words.meaning: whose weapons are all things that strike
whose weapons are all things that strike

translations.text: (He is) Śaṅkhabhṛt, who bears the conch Pāñcajanya (the ego from which the elements arise); Nandakī, who bears the sword Nandaka (knowledge); Cakrī, who bears the discus Sudarśana (the mind), or turns the wheel of the round; Śārṅgadhanvā, whose bow is Śārṅga (the senses and the ego); Gadādhara, who bears the mace Kaumodakī (the intellect); Rathāṅgapāṇi, with the wheel in his hand; Akṣobhya, therefore unshakable; Sarvapraharaṇāyudha, whose weapons are all things that strike. To Sarvapraharaṇāyudha: Om, homage.

notes: Śaṅkara: śaṅkhabhṛt: he bears the conch Pāñcajanya, which is the ego from which the elements arise. nandakī: his is the sword Nandaka, made of knowledge. cakrī: his is the discus Sudarśana, the principle of mind; or by his command the wheel of the round turns. śārṅgadhanvā: his bow Śārṅga is the senses and the ego (Pāṇini 5.4.132). gadādharaḥ: he bears the mace Kaumodakī, the principle of intellect. rathāṅgapāṇiḥ: the wheel is in his hand. akṣobhyaḥ: therefore none can shake him. sarvapraharaṇāyudhaḥ: it is not fixed that these alone are his weapons; all things that strike are his weapons, even those not known as weapons, such as the nails: this shows that his resolves are true and that he is lord of all (‘he is the lord of all’, Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.22).

Śaṅkara, on the close: the name is said twice to mark the end. Om is for auspiciousness (‘Om and atha, these two came forth of old from Brahmā's throat; so both are auspicious’). Saying ‘homage’ at the end, he worships (‘we offer you the most words of homage’, Īśa 18; ‘that is the right time, that the right star, that the holy day, that the success of the act, where Hari is first bowed to’; ‘first’ stands for the end too, since the wise also bow at the close). The fruit of bowing has been shown before (verse 10): ‘even one bow made to Kṛṣṇa equals the bath at the end of ten horse sacrifices; the one who made ten horse sacrifices is born again, the one who bowed to Kṛṣṇa is not’. Here the tenth hundred names are explained.
The edition prints the last name twice, the second time with Om and namaḥ, as a separate line of the verse.
